statement: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b p : V) : ‖p - a‖ = ‖p - b‖ ↔ inner ℝ (p - (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (a + b)) (b - a) = 0
type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b p : V), ‖p - a‖ = ‖p - b‖ ↔ inner ℝ (p - (1 / 2) • (a + b)) (b - a) = 0
informal: p is equidistant from a and b iff p − midpoint(a,b) is orthogonal to b − a — ‖p−a‖² − ‖p−b‖² = 2⟨p − (a+b)/2, b − a⟩, and norms are nonnegative.

name: top_dist_div_one_add_triangle
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (x y z : X) : dist x z / (1 + dist x z) ≤ dist x y / (1 + dist x y) + dist y z / (1 + dist y z)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] (x y z : X), dist x z / (1 + dist x z) ≤ dist x y / (1 + dist x y) + dist y z / (1 + dist y z)
informal: The bounded metric d/(1+d) satisfies the triangle inequality — t ↦ t/(1+t) is monotone and subadditive on [0,∞); combine with dist_triangle.

name: p3_thm1_disproof
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h5 : 5 < p) : ((p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4) → (p3_fibsum p : ℤ) ≡ 3 [ZMOD p]) ∧ ((p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3) → (p3_fibsum p : ℤ) ≡ 1 [ZMOD p])
type: ¬∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 5 < p → (p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4 → ↑(Mathlib2.p3_fibsum p) ≡ 3 [ZMOD ↑p]) ∧ (p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3 → ↑(Mathlib2.p3_fibsum p) ≡ 1 [ZMOD ↑p])
informal: Theorem 1 as literally written: S_p = 3 mod p if p = 1,4 mod 5 and S_p = 1 mod p if p = 2,3 mod 5

name: geo_sin_mul_sin_pi_div_three_sub_add
statement: (x : ℝ) : Real.sin x * Real.sin (Real.pi / 3 - x) * Real.sin (Real.pi / 3 + x) = Real.sin (3 * x) / 4
type: ∀ (x : ℝ), Real.sin x * Real.sin (Real.pi / 3 - x) * Real.sin (Real.pi / 3 + x) = Real.sin (3 * x) / 4
informal: sin x · sin(π/3 − x) · sin(π/3 + x) = sin(3x)/4 — expand with addition formulas (sin(π/3)=√3/2, cos(π/3)=1/2) to get sin x (3/4 cos²x − 1/4 sin²x), then use the triple angle formula.

name: geo_cos_sum_two_pi_div_seven
statement: : Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) + Real.cos (4 * Real.pi / 7) + Real.cos (6 * Real.pi / 7) = -1 / 2
type: Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) + Real.cos (4 * Real.pi / 7) + Real.cos (6 * Real.pi / 7) = -1 / 2
informal: cos(2π/7) + cos(4π/7) + cos(6π/7) = −1/2 — multiply by 2 sin(π/7) ≠ 0 and telescope with 2 sin x cos y = sin(x+y) − sin(y−x), leaving sin(π) − sin(π/7); or take real parts of the sum of the 7th roots of unity.

name: top_fixed_of_iterate_contraction
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ) (K : ℝ) (hK : K < 1) (h : ∀ x y : X, dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) ≤ K * dist x y) (p : X) (hp : f^[n] p = p) : f p = p
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ), ∀ K < 1, (∀ (x y : X), dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) ≤ K * dist x y) → ∀ (p : X), f^[n] p = p → f p = p
informal: If an iterate f^[n] is a contraction with fixed point p then p is already a fixed point of f — f p is also fixed by f^[n] (iterates commute with f) and a contraction with K < 1 has at most one fixed point.

name: p3_aux_period
statement: (n k i : ℕ) (h2 : 2 ∣ n) : Nat.fib (i + 2 * n * k) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD Nat.fib n]
type: ∀ (n k i : ℕ), 2 ∣ n → Nat.fib (i + 2 * n * k) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD Nat.fib n]
informal: auxiliary: for even n, 2n is a period of Fibonacci mod F_n

name: geo_stewart
statement: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c : V) (t : ℝ) : ‖a - ((1 - t) • b + t • c)‖ ^ 2 = (1 - t) * ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + t * ‖a - c‖ ^ 2 - t * (1 - t) * ‖b - c‖ ^ 2
type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c : V) (t : ℝ), ‖a - ((1 - t) • b + t • c)‖ ^ 2 = (1 - t) * ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + t * ‖a - c‖ ^ 2 - t * (1 - t) * ‖b - c‖ ^ 2
informal: Stewart's theorem in vector form: for d = (1−t)b + tc on line bc, |ad|² = (1−t)|ab|² + t|ac|² − t(1−t)|bc|² — write a − d = (1−t)(a−b) + t(a−c) and expand squared norms via inner products.

name: top_lfp_comp_self
statement: {α : Type*} [CompleteLattice α] (f : α →o α) : OrderHom.lfp (f.comp f) = OrderHom.lfp f
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : CompleteLattice α] (f : α →o α), OrderHom.lfp (f.comp f) = OrderHom.lfp f
informal: The least fixed point of f∘f equals that of f — ≤ since lfp f is fixed by f∘f; for ≥ put a = lfp (f∘f): f a is a fixed point of f∘f so a ≤ f a, hence f a ≤ f (f a) = a, so a is a fixed point of f.

name: geo_cos_pi_div_seven_prod
statement: : Real.cos (Real.pi / 7) * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) * Real.cos (4 * Real.pi / 7) = -1 / 8
type: Real.cos (Real.pi / 7) * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi / 7) * Real.cos (4 * Real.pi / 7) = -1 / 8
informal: cos(π/7)cos(2π/7)cos(4π/7) = −1/8 — multiply by 8 sin(π/7) ≠ 0 and apply sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x three times to get sin(8π/7) = −sin(π/7).

name: geo_centroid_sum_sq_dist
statement: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c : V) : ‖a - (1 / 3 : ℝ) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - (1 / 3 : ℝ) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - (1 / 3 : ℝ) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 = (‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - a‖ ^ 2) / 3
type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c : V), ‖a - (1 / 3) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - (1 / 3) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - (1 / 3) • (a + b + c)‖ ^ 2 = (‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - a‖ ^ 2) / 3
informal: For the centroid g of triangle abc, |ag|² + |bg|² + |cg|² = (|ab|² + |bc|² + |ca|²)/3 — a − g = ((a−b) + (a−c))/3 etc., expand all squared norms into inner products.

name: top_finite_monotone_iterate_bot_fixed
statement: {α : Type*} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] [Finite α] (f : α → α) (hf : Monotone f) : ∃ n : ℕ, f (f^[n] ⊥) = f^[n] ⊥
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : PartialOrder α] [inst_1 : OrderBot α] [Finite α] (f : α → α), Monotone f → ∃ n, f (f^[n] ⊥) = f^[n] ⊥
informal: On a finite poset with bottom, iterating a monotone map from ⊥ reaches a fixed point — n ↦ f^[n] ⊥ is monotone; if never stationary it would be strictly monotone hence injective ℕ → α, contradicting finiteness.

name: p3_prop1
statement: (n : ℕ) : p3_fibsum n = Nat.fib (n + 2) - 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_fibsum n = Nat.fib (n + 2) - 1

name: geo_euler_quadrilateral
statement: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c d : V) : ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - d‖ ^ 2 + ‖d - a‖ ^ 2 = ‖a - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - d‖ ^ 2 + 4 * ‖(1 / 2 : ℝ) • (a + c) - (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (b + d)‖ ^ 2
type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (a b c d : V), ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖c - d‖ ^ 2 + ‖d - a‖ ^ 2 = ‖a - c‖ ^ 2 + ‖b - d‖ ^ 2 + 4 * ‖(1 / 2) • (a + c) - (1 / 2) • (b + d)‖ ^ 2
informal: Euler's quadrilateral theorem: the sum of the squared sides equals the sum of the squared diagonals plus four times the squared distance between the midpoints of the diagonals — expand every squared norm into inner products.

name: p3_remark2
statement: (k : ℕ) : p3_self_summable k ↔ Nat.fib k ∣ Nat.fib (Nat.fib k + 2) - 1
type: ∀ (k : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_self_summable k ↔ Nat.fib k ∣ Nat.fib (Nat.fib k + 2) - 1
informal: k is self-summable iff F_k divides F_{F_k+2} - 1

name: geo_sum_sq_dist_roots_of_unity
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (z : ℂ) (hz : ‖z‖ = 1) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ‖z - Complex.exp (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (k : ℂ) / (n : ℂ))‖ ^ 2 = 2 * (n : ℝ)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∀ (z : ℂ), ‖z‖ = 1 → ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ‖z - Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * ↑k / ↑n)‖ ^ 2 = 2 * ↑n
informal: The sum of squared distances from a point of the unit circle to the vertices of the regular n-gon inscribed in it is 2n — ‖z − ζ^k‖² = 2 − 2 Re(z · conj ζ^k), and Σ ζ^k = 0 for the primitive root ζ = exp(2πi/n), n ≥ 2.

name: top_compact_closed_disjoint_dist_pos
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (K C : Set X) (hK : IsCompact K) (hC : IsClosed C) (hd : Disjoint K C) : ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ C, δ ≤ dist x y
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] (K C : Set X), IsCompact K → IsClosed C → Disjoint K C → ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ C, δ ≤ dist x y
informal: A compact set and a disjoint closed set in a metric space are a positive distance apart — transfer EMetric.exists_pos_forall_lt_edist to dist, or minimize infDist · C over K.

name: geo_sum_cos_two_pi_mul_div
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * (k : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) = 0
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ↑k / ↑n) = 0
informal: The real parts of the n-th roots of unity sum to zero for n ≥ 2 — take the real part of the geometric sum Σ ζ^k = 0 for ζ = exp(2πi/n) (a primitive n-th root, IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_eq_zero).

name: p3_remark3
statement: (a b : ℕ) (hba : b ≤ a) : (a ≡ b [MOD 4] → (Nat.fib a : ℤ) - Nat.fib b = Nat.fib ((a - b) / 2) * p3_lucas ((a + b) / 2)) ∧ (a ≡ b + 2 [MOD 4] → (Nat.fib a : ℤ) - Nat.fib b = Nat.fib ((a + b) / 2) * p3_lucas ((a - b) / 2))
type: ∀ (a b : ℕ), b ≤ a → (a ≡ b [MOD 4] → ↑(Nat.fib a) - ↑(Nat.fib b) = ↑(Nat.fib ((a - b) / 2)) * ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas ((a + b) / 2))) ∧ (a ≡ b + 2 [MOD 4] → ↑(Nat.fib a) - ↑(Nat.fib b) = ↑(Nat.fib ((a + b) / 2)) * ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas ((a - b) / 2)))
informal: F_a - F_b = F_u L_v if a = b mod 4, = F_v L_u if a = b+2 mod 4, where u=(a-b)/2, v=(a+b)/2

name: top_connected_metric_sphere_nonempty
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [PreconnectedSpace X] (x y : X) (r : ℝ) (h0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr : r ≤ dist x y) : ∃ z : X, dist x z = r
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [PreconnectedSpace X] (x y : X) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → r ≤ dist x y → ∃ z, dist x z = r
informal: In a connected metric space every radius between 0 and dist x y is attained as a distance from x — intermediate value theorem for the continuous map z ↦ dist x z on a preconnected space, with values 0 at x and dist x y at y.

name: top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) : ∃! p : X, f p = p
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → ∃! p, f p = p
informal: Edelstein: a strictly distance-decreasing self-map of a nonempty compact metric space has exactly one fixed point — f is 1-Lipschitz hence continuous, x ↦ dist x (f x) attains its minimum at some p; if f p ≠ p then dist (f p) (f (f p)) < dist p (f p) contradicts minimality; uniqueness is immediate from strictness.

name: top_uniformly_discrete_complete
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (h : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → 1 ≤ dist x y) : CompleteSpace X
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X], (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → 1 ≤ dist x y) → CompleteSpace X
informal: A metric space whose distinct points are at distance at least 1 is complete — a Cauchy sequence is eventually within 1/2 of itself hence eventually constant, hence convergent (Metric.complete_of_cauchySeq_tendsto).

name: top_connected_metric_uncountable
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [PreconnectedSpace X] (x y : X) (h : x ≠ y) : ¬ (Set.univ : Set X).Countable
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [PreconnectedSpace X] (x y : X), x ≠ y → ¬Set.univ.Countable
informal: A connected metric space with two distinct points is uncountable — the image of z ↦ dist x z contains the interval [0, dist x y] by the intermediate value theorem, a nondegenerate real interval is uncountable, and images of countable sets are countable.

name: top_tendsto_of_subseq_limits_unique
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (u : ℕ → X) (a : X) (h : ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ → ∀ b : X, Filter.Tendsto (u ∘ φ) Filter.atTop (nhds b) → b = a) : Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop (nhds a)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (u : ℕ → X) (a : X), (∀ (φ : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono φ → ∀ (b : X), Filter.Tendsto (u ∘ φ) Filter.atTop (nhds b) → b = a) → Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop (nhds a)
informal: In a compact metric space a sequence all of whose convergent subsequences have limit a converges to a — otherwise infinitely many terms stay ε-far from a; extract a subsequence of those, then a convergent sub-subsequence by sequential compactness, whose limit is ≠ a.

name: top_galois_u_eq_sSup
statement: {α β : Type*} [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] (l : α → β) (u : β → α) (gc : GaloisConnection l u) (b : β) : u b = sSup {a : α | l a ≤ b}
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : CompleteLattice α] [inst_1 : CompleteLattice β] (l : α → β) (u : β → α), GaloisConnection l u → ∀ (b : β), u b = sSup {a | l a ≤ b}
informal: The upper adjoint of a Galois connection between complete lattices is given by u b = sSup {a | l a ≤ b} — the set equals Set.Iic (u b) by the adjunction, whose supremum is u b.

name: top_isometry_compact_surjective
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : Isometry f) : Function.Surjective f
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), Isometry f → Function.Surjective f
informal: An isometry of a compact metric space into itself is surjective — if y is not in the (closed) range, pick ε > 0 with ball y ε disjoint from range f; the orbit f^[n] y then satisfies dist (f^[m] y) (f^[n] y) = dist y (f^[n-m] y) ≥ ε, so it has no convergent subsequence, contradicting sequential compactness.

name: top_distrib_lattice_median
statement: {α : Type*} [DistribLattice α] (a b c : α) : (a ⊓ b) ⊔ (b ⊓ c) ⊔ (c ⊓ a) = (a ⊔ b) ⊓ (b ⊔ c) ⊓ (c ⊔ a)
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DistribLattice α] (a b c : α), a ⊓ b ⊔ b ⊓ c ⊔ c ⊓ a = (a ⊔ b) ⊓ (b ⊔ c) ⊓ (c ⊔ a)
informal: The median identity in a distributive lattice — ≤ holds in every lattice (each meet is below each join); for ≥ expand the right side using distributivity and absorb.

name: p3_thm1_corrected
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h5 : 5 < p) : ((p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4) → (p3_fibsum p : ℤ) ≡ 1 [ZMOD p]) ∧ ((p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3) → (p3_fibsum p : ℤ) ≡ -2 [ZMOD p])
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 5 < p → (p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4 → ↑(Mathlib2.p3_fibsum p) ≡ 1 [ZMOD ↑p]) ∧ (p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3 → ↑(Mathlib2.p3_fibsum p) ≡ -2 [ZMOD ↑p])
informal: CORRECTED Theorem 1 (auditor's correction, not the paper's wording): S_p = 1 mod p if p = 1,4 mod 5 and S_p = -2 mod p if p = 2,3 mod 5

name: top_countable_compact_t2_isolated_point
statement: {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [Countable X] [Nonempty X] : ∃ x : X, IsOpen ({x} : Set X)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] [Countable X] [Nonempty X], ∃ x, IsOpen {x}
informal: A nonempty countable compact Hausdorff space has an isolated point — compact Hausdorff spaces are Baire; if no singleton were open, each complement {x}ᶜ would be open and dense, so their countable intersection (which is empty) would be dense, contradicting nonemptiness.

name: top_expanding_compact_isometry
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) : Isometry f
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) → Isometry f
informal: A distance non-decreasing self-map of a compact metric space is an isometry — for x, y use compactness of X × X to find iterates n with (f^[n] x, f^[n] y) arbitrarily close to (x, y) (recurrence of the orbit of the expanding map f × f); then dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) ≤ dist x y + 2ε.

name: p3_thm1_not_dvd
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h5 : 5 < p) : ¬ p ∣ p3_fibsum p
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 5 < p → ¬p ∣ Mathlib2.p3_fibsum p
informal: for a prime p > 5, p does not divide S_p

name: p3_prop2
statement: (n : ℕ) (h1 : 1 < n) (h2 : 2 ∣ n) : p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) ∣ 2 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 < n → 2 ∣ n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) ∣ 2 * n
informal: for even n > 1 the Pisano period of F_n divides 2n

name: geo_unit_sum_zero_sum_sq
informal: For unit complex numbers with a+b+c = 0, also a²+b²+c² = 0 — conj a = a⁻¹ etc., so ab+bc+ca = abc·conj(a+b+c) = 0, and a²+b²+c² = (a+b+c)² − 2(ab+bc+ca).

name: p3_thm2
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) (h3 : p % 3 = 2) (h5 : p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3) (hn : n = 2 * p ∨ n = 4 * p) : Nat.fib n ≡ 1 [MOD 2] ∧ (Nat.fib (Nat.fib n + 2) : ℤ) - 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD Nat.fib n]
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Odd p → p % 3 = 2 → p % 5 = 2 ∨ p % 5 = 3 → n = 2 * p ∨ n = 4 * p → Nat.fib n ≡ 1 [MOD 2] ∧ ↑(Nat.fib (Nat.fib n + 2)) - 1 ≡ 0 [ZMOD ↑(Nat.fib n)]
informal: for n = 2p or 4p with p an odd prime, p = 2 mod 3, p = ±2 mod 5: F_n is odd and F_n divides F_{F_n+2} - 1

name: geo_unit_sum_zero_equilateral
statement: (a b c : ℂ) (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1) (hc : ‖c‖ = 1) (h : a + b + c = 0) : ‖a - b‖ = Real.sqrt 3 ∧ ‖b - c‖ = Real.sqrt 3 ∧ ‖c - a‖ = Real.sqrt 3
informal: Three unit complex numbers with sum zero form an equilateral triangle of side √3 — ‖a+b‖² = ‖c‖² = 1 and the parallelogram law give ‖a−b‖² = 2+2−1 = 3; symmetric for the others.

name: geo_leibniz_centroid
statement: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → V) (p : V) : ∑ i ∈ s, ‖p - x i‖ ^ 2 = (s.card : ℝ) * ‖p - (s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ j ∈ s, x j‖ ^ 2 + ∑ i ∈ s, ‖(s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ j ∈ s, x j - x i‖ ^ 2
type: ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ V] {ι : Type u_2} (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → V) (p : V), ∑ i ∈ s, ‖p - x i‖ ^ 2 = ↑s.card * ‖p - (↑s.card)⁻¹ • ∑ j ∈ s, x j‖ ^ 2 + ∑ i ∈ s, ‖(↑s.card)⁻¹ • ∑ j ∈ s, x j - x i‖ ^ 2
informal: Leibniz (moment of inertia / parallel axis) identity: for the centroid g of points x_i, Σ|p − x_i|² = n|p − g|² + Σ|g − x_i|² — write p − x_i = (p − g) + (g − x_i), expand, and the cross term vanishes because Σ(g − x_i) = 0 (empty s is trivial).

name: p3_cor2
statement: : {k : ℕ | Odd k ∧ k ∣ p3_fibsum k}.Infinite
type: {k | Odd k ∧ k ∣ Mathlib2.p3_fibsum k}.Infinite
informal: infinitely many odd k divide F_1+...+F_k (also Conjecture 1 of the paper)

name: p3_cor1
statement: : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => sInf ((fun n : ℕ => (p3_pisano n : ℝ) / n) '' Set.Ioo 0 N)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
type: Filter.Tendsto (fun N => sInf ((fun n => ↑(Mathlib2.p3_pisano n) / ↑n) '' Set.Ioo 0 N)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
informal: lim_{N→∞} min{π(n)/n : 0 < n < N} = 0

name: bld_idempotent_sum_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A = A) (hB : B * B = B) (hAB : (A + B) * (A + B) = A + B) : Matrix.rank (A + B) = Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank B
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A → B * B = B → (A + B) * (A + B) = A + B → (A + B).rank = A.rank + B.rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field three times: rank(A+B) = tr(A+B) = tr A + tr B = rank A + rank B in K, then Nat.cast injectivity in characteristic zero.

name: bld_iterate_shrinking_unique_fixed_point
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) < dist x y) : ∃! p : X, f p = p
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [Nonempty X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) < dist x y) → ∃! p, f p = p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point applied to f^[n]: its unique fixed point p satisfies f^[n] (f p) = f p, so f p = p by uniqueness; any fixed point of f is fixed by f^[n]. (Shrinking analogue of Mathlib2.top_fixed_of_iterate_contraction.)

name: bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : 2 - a n ≤ Real.pi ^ 2 / 4 ^ (n + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form: a n = 2 cos(π/2^(n+1)), so 2 - a n = 4 sin^2(π/2^(n+2)) ≤ 4 (π/2^(n+2))^2 = π^2/4^(n+1). Quantitative rate for Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_tendsto.

name: bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hs : Function.Surjective f) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) : Isometry f
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), Function.Surjective f → (∀ (x y : X), dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) → Isometry f
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_expanding_compact_isometry and Mathlib2.top_isometry_compact_surjective: a right inverse g of f is expanding, hence an isometry by the first theorem and surjective by the second; so g is a bijective isometry and f = g⁻¹ is an isometry.

name: bld_involution_trace_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (h : A * A = 1) : Matrix.trace A + (Fintype.card ι : K) = 2 * (Matrix.rank (1 + A) : K)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = 1 → A.trace + ↑(Fintype.card ι) = 2 * ↑(1 + A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field: P = (1/2) • (1 + A) is idempotent, so tr P = rank P = rank (1 + A) (scaling by a unit preserves rank), and tr P = (n + tr A)/2.

name: bld_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : (∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2) * (2 ^ n * Real.sin (Real.pi / 2 ^ (n + 1))) = 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form: a (i+1)/2 = cos(π/2^(i+2)); induct on n with sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ (finite Viète product).

name: bld_edelstein_iterates_tendsto
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) (p : X) (hp : f p = p) (x : X) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f^[n] x) Filter.atTop (nhds p)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → ∀ (p : X), f p = p → ∀ (x : X), Filter.Tendsto (fun n => f^[n] x) Filter.atTop (nhds p)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_tendsto_of_subseq_limits_unique (and complements Mathlib2.top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point): dist (f^[n] x) p is antitone with limit c; any subsequential limit b satisfies dist b p = c = dist (f b) p by continuity, forcing b = p by strict contraction; conclude by the subsequence criterion on the compact space.

name: bld_involution_rank_add_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (h : A * A = 1) : Matrix.rank (1 + A) + Matrix.rank (1 - A) = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = 1 → (1 + A).rank + (1 - A).rank = Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_rank_complement_field: P = (1/2) • (1 + A) is idempotent with 1 - P = (1/2) • (1 - A); rank is invariant under scaling by the unit 1/2.

name: bld_nilpotent_rank_bound
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (k : ℕ) (h : A ^ k = 0) : k * Matrix.rank A ≤ (k - 1) * Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (k : ℕ), A ^ k = 0 → k * A.rank ≤ (k - 1) * Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_sylvester_rank_rect: by induction on j, j * rank A ≤ (j-1) * n + rank (A^j) (Sylvester applied to A^j and A); at j = k the last term vanishes. Special case k = 2: A^2 = 0 implies 2 rank A ≤ n.

name: bld_sqrt_two_rec_viete_tendsto
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2) Filter.atTop (nhds (2 / Real.pi))
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2) Filter.atTop (nhds (2 / Real.pi))
informal: Uses Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form (and the finite product identity derived from it): the partial products equal 1/(2^n sin(π/2^(n+1))), and 2^n sin(π/2^(n+1)) → π/2 since sin t / t → 1. This is Viète's formula 2/π = (√2/2)(√(2+√2)/2)⋯.

name: bld_mantel_triangle_free
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V ^ 2
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.comb_degree_add_degree_le_of_triangle_free: summing deg u + deg v ≤ |V| over edges gives ∑_v deg(v)^2 ≤ |E| |V|; Cauchy–Schwarz and the handshake lemma give (2|E|)^2 ≤ |V| ∑ deg^2 ≤ |V|^2 |E|. Extends Mathlib2.comb_card_edgeFinset_le_of_coloring_bool from bipartite to triangle-free graphs (Mantel).

name: bld_sum_inv_sqrt_div_sqrt_tendsto
statement: : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / Real.sqrt ((i : ℝ) + 1)) / Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 2)
type: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / √(↑i + 1)) / √↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds 2)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.an2_sum_inv_sqrt_bounds: squeeze between 2(sqrt(n+1) - 1)/sqrt n and 2, both tending to 2.

name: bld_exists_bipartite_subgraph_half_edges
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, H ≤ G ∧ H.Colorable 2 ∧ G.edgeSet.ncard ≤ 2 * H.edgeSet.ncard
type: ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], ∃ H ≤ G, H.Colorable 2 ∧ G.edgeSet.ncard ≤ 2 * H.edgeSet.ncard
informal: Uses Mathlib2.comb_exists_cut_half_edges: take the cut s from the library theorem and let H be the subgraph of G consisting of edges between s and sᶜ; it is 2-coloured by membership in s, and its edges biject with the ordered pairs counted in the cut.

name: bld_frobenius_rank_inequality
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (m n p q : Type*) [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [Fintype q] (A : Matrix m n K) (B : Matrix n p K) (C : Matrix p q K) : Matrix.rank (A * B) + Matrix.rank (B * C) ≤ Matrix.rank B + Matrix.rank (A * B * C)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) (p : Type u_4) (q : Type u_5) [Fintype m] [inst_2 : Fintype n] [inst_3 : Fintype p] [inst_4 : Fintype q] (A : Matrix m n K) (B : Matrix n p K) (C : Matrix p q K), (A * B).rank + (B * C).rank ≤ B.rank + (A * B * C).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_sylvester_rank_rect: take a rank factorisation B = M * N with M : n × Fin r, N : Fin r × p, r = rank B; apply the rectangular Sylvester inequality to (A*M) and (N*C) to get rank(AM) + rank(NC) ≤ r + rank(ABC), then rank(AB) ≤ rank(AM) and rank(BC) ≤ rank(NC).

name: bld_one_add_div_pow_mono
informal: Uses Mathlib2.an2_amgm_range_pow: apply AM-GM to the n+1 numbers consisting of n copies of 1 + x/n and one copy of 1; their mean is 1 + x/(n+1). Generalises Mathlib2.ana_one_add_inv_pow_mono (x = 1).

name: bld_hardy_cross_term
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) * a k ≤ 2 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k ^ 2
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / (↑k + 1) * a k ≤ 2 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.r3_hardy_inequality_finite: by Cauchy–Schwarz the left side is at most sqrt(∑ σ_k^2) * sqrt(∑ a_k^2), and Hardy bounds ∑ σ_k^2 by 4 ∑ a_k^2.

name: bld_zmod_diag_quadratic_form_surjective
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (a b c : ZMod p) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) : ∃ x y : ZMod p, a * x ^ 2 + b * y ^ 2 = c
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a b c : ZMod p), a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → ∃ x y, a * x ^ 2 + b * y ^ 2 = c
informal: Uses Mathlib2.alg_card_range_sq_zmod_prime: for odd p the sets {a x^2} and {c - b y^2} each have (p+1)/2 elements, so they intersect by pigeonhole in ZMod p; p = 2 by direct check.

name: bld_nilpotent_commute_det_add
statement: (n : ℕ) (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (hAB : A * B = B * A) : Matrix.det (B + A) = Matrix.det B
type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), IsNilpotent A → A * B = B * A → (B + A).det = B.det
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_nilpotent_det_one_add_reduced: if B is invertible then B⁻¹A is nilpotent (A, B commute) and det(B + A) = det B * det(1 + B⁻¹A) = det B. For general B apply this to B + t • 1 for the cofinitely many t with det(B + t • 1) ≠ 0 and conclude by the polynomial identity (two polynomials in t agreeing at infinitely many points), then set t = 0.

name: bld_prod_sin_pi_div_odd
statement: (n : ℕ) : ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, Real.sin (((k : ℝ) + 1) * Real.pi / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 1)) = Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ) + 1) / 2 ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, Real.sin ((↑k + 1) * Real.pi / (2 * ↑n + 1)) = √(2 * ↑n + 1) / 2 ^ n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.geo_prod_sin_pi_mul_div with 2n factors: the reflection k ↦ 2n+1-k pairs the factors (sin(π - t) = sin t), so the square of the half product equals (2n+1)/2^(2n); take the positive square root since every factor is positive.

name: bld_fib_even_index_iff_five_sq_add_four
informal: Uses Mathlib2.r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square and Mathlib2.an_cassini_int: solutions of the Pell-type equation x^2 - 5y^2 = 4 are exactly even-indexed Fibonacci numbers. (⇐) the library iff gives y = fib m; if m is odd then Cassini gives 5y^2-4 a square as well, and two squares differing by 8 force y = 1 = fib 2. (⇒) L_{2n}^2 = 5 F_{2n}^2 + 4 from Cassini.

name: bld_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_three_mod_four
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h3 : p % 4 = 3) (x y : ℚ) : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ (p : ℚ)
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 3 → ∀ (x y : ℚ), x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ ↑p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_nt_sq_add_sq_eq_prime_mul_sq: the circle x^2+y^2=p has no rational point when p ≡ 3 mod 4; clear denominators (x = u/w, y = v/w) to get u^2+v^2 = p*w^2 with w ≠ 0, contradicting the library theorem.

name: bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hnc : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card (Subgroup.center G) = p
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card ↥(Subgroup.center G) = p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.alg_center_index_not_prime: the centre of a p-group is non-trivial, so |Z| ∈ {p, p^2, p^3}; p^3 is excluded by non-commutativity and p^2 would give prime index p, contradicting the library theorem.

name: bld_center_eq_bot_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hnc : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Subgroup.center G = ⊥
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Subgroup.center G = ⊥
informal: Uses Mathlib2.alg_center_index_not_prime: |Z| divides p*q; |Z| = p or q gives prime index, contradicting the library theorem, and |Z| = p*q contradicts non-commutativity, so |Z| = 1.

name: bld_fib_consecutive_of_quadratic_form
statement: (x y : ℕ) (hx : 0 < x) (h : ((x : ℤ) ^ 2 - (x : ℤ) * (y : ℤ) - (y : ℤ) ^ 2) ^ 2 = 1) : ∃ n : ℕ, y = Nat.fib n ∧ x = Nat.fib (n + 1)
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), 0 < x → (↑x ^ 2 - ↑x * ↑y - ↑y ^ 2) ^ 2 = 1 → ∃ n, y = Nat.fib n ∧ x = Nat.fib (n + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square and Mathlib2.an_cassini_int: (2x-y)^2 = 5y^2 ± 4, so y = fib n by the library characterisation; Cassini shows fib (n+1) is a root of the same quadratic in x, and positivity of x pins it down (small cases y ≤ 1 by hand). Key lemma of IMO 1981 Q3.

name: p4_z
type: ℕ → ℤ
informal: z(n): the largest integer z with 3z < 2n, i.e. floor((2n-1)/3) (integer floor division)

name: p4_m
statement: def p4_m (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt (2 * n)
type: ℕ → ℕ
informal: m(n): the largest integer m with m^2 <= 2n, i.e. floor(sqrt(2n))

name: p4_r
statement: def p4_r (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.clog 2 n
type: ℕ → ℕ
informal: r(n): the least non-negative integer r with n <= 2^r, i.e. ceil(log2 n)

name: p4_x
statement: def p4_x (n : ℕ) : ℤ := p4_z n - ((p4_r n : ℤ) + 1) * (p4_m n : ℤ)
type: ℕ → ℤ
informal: x(n) = z(n) - (r(n)+1) m(n), the quantity whose sign the paper determines

name: bld2_tripotent_trace_sq_eq_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (h : A * A * A = A) : Matrix.trace (A * A) = (Matrix.rank A : K)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A * A = A → (A * A).trace = ↑A.rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field: A*A is idempotent, so trace (A*A) = rank (A*A); and rank (A*A) = rank A because A = A * (A*A) gives rank A ≤ rank (A*A) ≤ rank A.

name: bld2_mantel_equality_regular
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) (v : V) : 2 * G.degree v = Fintype.card V
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ∀ (v : V), 2 * G.degree v = Fintype.card V
informal: Uses Mathlib2.comb_degree_add_degree_le_of_triangle_free (equality case of Mathlib2.bld_mantel_triangle_free): summing deg u + deg v ≤ n over edges gives ∑ deg^2 ≤ n * e; with Cauchy-Schwarz (2e)^2 ≤ n ∑ deg^2 and 4e = n^2 both are equalities, so ∑ (2 deg v - n)^2 = 0 and every degree equals n/2.

name: bld2_rank_add_rank_one_sub
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank (1 - A) = Fintype.card ι + Matrix.rank (A - A * A)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A.rank + (1 - A).rank = Fintype.card ι + (A - A * A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_sylvester_rank_rect: the inequality ≤ is Sylvester applied to A and 1 - A (A * (1 - A) = A - A*A); for ≥ show range A ⊓ range (1 - A) = range (A * (1 - A)) and range A ⊔ range (1 - A) = ⊤, then use the dimension formula.

name: bld2_tripotent_rank_split
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (h : A * A * A = A) : Matrix.rank A = Matrix.rank (A * A + A) + Matrix.rank (A * A - A)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A * A = A → A.rank = (A * A + A).rank + (A * A - A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_idempotent_sum_rank: P = (1/2)(A*A + A) and Q = (1/2)(A*A - A) are idempotents whose sum A*A is idempotent, so rank (A*A) = rank P + rank Q; scalars 1/2 do not change rank and rank (A*A) = rank A since A = A*(A*A).

name: bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq
statement: (n : ℕ) : (p3_lucas n : ℤ) ^ 2 - 5 * (Nat.fib n : ℤ) ^ 2 = 4 * (-1) ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ^ 2 - 5 * ↑(Nat.fib n) ^ 2 = 4 * (-1) ^ n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.an_cassini_int (with the definition Mathlib2.p3_lucas): the cast of p3_lucas n is 2 F(n+1) - F(n) (no truncation since F(n) ≤ 2 F(n+1)); expand (2F(n+1) - F(n))^2 - 5F(n)^2 = 4(F(n+1)^2 - F(n+1)F(n) - F(n)^2) and rewrite with Cassini F(n+2)F(n) - F(n+1)^2 = (-1)^(n+1), F(n+2) = F(n+1) + F(n).

name: bld2_idempotent_iff_rank_add_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : A * A = A ↔ Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank (1 - A) = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A ↔ A.rank + (1 - A).rank = Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_rank_complement_field (and Mathlib2.gen_lin_sylvester_rank_rect): forward direction is the rank-complement theorem; conversely the rank equality forces range A and range (1 - A) to be complementary, and A(1-A)x lies in both, so A - A*A = 0.

name: bld2_triangle_free_min_degree_le_half
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (d : ℕ) (hd : ∀ v : V, d ≤ G.degree v) : 2 * d ≤ Fintype.card V
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V], G.CliqueFree 3 → ∀ (d : ℕ), (∀ (v : V), d ≤ G.degree v) → 2 * d ≤ Fintype.card V
informal: Uses Mathlib2.comb_degree_add_degree_le_of_triangle_free: if d = 0 trivial; otherwise a vertex v has a neighbour u and 2d ≤ deg u + deg v ≤ card V.

name: bld2_nonexpanding_left_inverse_isometry
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f g : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) (hfg : ∀ x : X, f (g x) = x) : Isometry g ∧ ∀ x : X, g (f x) = x
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f g : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) → (∀ (x : X), f (g x) = x) → Isometry g ∧ ∀ (x : X), g (f x) = x
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry: f is surjective (right inverse g) and non-expanding, hence an isometry, hence injective; so g (f x) = x from f (g (f x)) = f x, and dist (g x) (g y) = dist (f (g x)) (f (g y)) = dist x y.

name: bld2_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod_gt
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : 2 / Real.pi < ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 / Real.pi < ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod: the partial product equals 1 / (2^n * sin (π / 2^(n+1))), and sin x < x for x > 0 gives 2^n * sin (π / 2^(n+1)) < π / 2.

name: bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : Summable (fun n : ℕ => 2 - a n)
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → Summable fun n => 2 - a n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate and Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two: 0 ≤ 2 - a n ≤ π^2 / 4^(n+1), and the geometric series on the right is summable, so comparison applies.

name: bld2_involution_iff_rank_add_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : A * A = 1 ↔ Matrix.rank (1 + A) + Matrix.rank (1 - A) = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = 1 ↔ (1 + A).rank + (1 - A).rank = Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_involution_rank_add_rank and Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_rank_complement_field: forward is the involution rank identity; conversely put P = (1/2)(1 + A), so 1 - P = (1/2)(1 - A) and rank P + rank (1 - P) = n, which forces P idempotent (converse of rank complement), i.e. A*A = 1.

name: bld2_involution_trace_eq_card
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (h : A * A = 1) (ht : Matrix.trace A = (Fintype.card ι : K)) : A = 1
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = 1 → A.trace = ↑(Fintype.card ι) → A = 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_involution_trace_rank and Mathlib2.bld_involution_rank_add_rank: the trace formula gives 2 * rank (1 + A) = 2 * card ι in K, hence (CharZero) rank (1 + A) = card ι; the rank identity then gives rank (1 - A) = 0, so 1 - A = 0.

name: bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_asymptotic
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => 4 ^ n * (2 - a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.pi ^ 2 / 4))
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => 4 ^ n * (2 - a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.pi ^ 2 / 4))
informal: Uses Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form (sharpening Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate): 2 - a n = 2 - 2 cos (π/2^(n+1)) = 4 sin^2 (π/2^(n+2)), so 4^n * (2 - a n) = (2^(n+1) * sin (π/2^(n+2)))^2, which tends to (π/2)^2 since sin x / x → 1.

name: bld2_rank_pow_convex
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (k : ℕ) : 2 * Matrix.rank (A ^ (k + 1)) ≤ Matrix.rank (A ^ k) + Matrix.rank (A ^ (k + 2))
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (k : ℕ), 2 * (A ^ (k + 1)).rank ≤ (A ^ k).rank + (A ^ (k + 2)).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_frobenius_rank_inequality: apply Frobenius to the triple (A, A^k, A): rank (A * A^k) + rank (A^k * A) ≤ rank (A^k) + rank (A * A^k * A).

name: bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h : Summable (fun k : ℕ => a k ^ 2)) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ^ 2) ∧ ∑' k : ℕ, ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * ∑' k : ℕ, a k ^ 2
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), (Summable fun k => a k ^ 2) → (Summable fun k => ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / (↑k + 1)) ^ 2) ∧ ∑' (k : ℕ), ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / (↑k + 1)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * ∑' (k : ℕ), a k ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.r3_hardy_inequality_finite: the partial sums of the nonnegative left series are bounded by 4 * ∑_{k<n} a k^2 ≤ 4 * ∑' a k^2, so the series is summable (summable_of_sum_range_le) and its tsum obeys the same bound.

name: p4_x_block
informal: Auditor's helper lemma (not a statement of the paper): if 2^(s-1) < n <= 2^s and t^2 <= 2n < (t+1)^2 then r(n)=s, m(n)=t and x(n) = floor((2n-1)/3) - (s+1)t.

name: bld2_commuting_idempotents_rank_join
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A = A) (hB : B * B = B) (hAB : A * B = B * A) : Matrix.rank (A + B - A * B) + Matrix.rank (A * B) = Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank B
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A → B * B = B → A * B = B * A → (A + B - A * B).rank + (A * B).rank = A.rank + B.rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_idempotent_sum_rank twice: A and B - A*B are idempotents with idempotent sum A + B - A*B, so rank (A + B - A*B) = rank A + rank (B - A*B); A*B and B - A*B are idempotents with sum B, so rank B = rank (A*B) + rank (B - A*B).

name: bld2_two_pow_mul_factorial_le_succ_pow
statement: (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ n * n.factorial ≤ (n + 1) ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ^ n * n.factorial ≤ (n + 1) ^ n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_an_amgm_finset_ordered_ring (or Mathlib2.an2_amgm_range_pow): apply AM-GM to a i = i + 1 on Finset.range n: n^n * n! ≤ (n(n+1)/2)^n, i.e. 2^n * n^n * n! ≤ n^n * (n+1)^n; cancel n^n for n > 0.

name: bld2_fibsum_sum
statement: (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, p3_fibsum i + n + 3 = Nat.fib (n + 4)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Mathlib2.p3_fibsum i + n + 3 = Nat.fib (n + 4)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_prop1 twice: p3_fibsum i = fib (i+2) - 1, so the sum is (p3_fibsum (n+2) - fib 1 - fib 2) - n = fib (n+4) - 1 - 2 - n; or induct on n using p3_prop1 in the step.

name: bld2_expanding_compact_isometryEquiv
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) : ∃ e : X ≃ᵢ X, ∀ x : X, e x = f x
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) → ∃ e, ∀ (x : X), e x = f x
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_expanding_compact_isometry and Mathlib2.top_isometry_compact_surjective: an expanding self-map of a compact metric space is an isometry, hence surjective; with injectivity of isometries this gives a bijective isometry, packaged as an IsometryEquiv.

name: bld2_fib_odd_index_iff_five_sq_sub_four
informal: Uses Mathlib2.r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square and Mathlib2.bld_fib_even_index_iff_five_sq_add_four: y is Fibonacci iff one of the two Pell conditions holds, and the +4 condition characterises even indices; the two conditions hold simultaneously only for y = 1 = fib 1 = fib 2 (x'^2 - x^2 = 8), which settles the overlap, using strict monotonicity of fib from index 2.

name: bld2_edelstein_no_periodic_points
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) (x : X) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : f^[n] x = x) : f x = x
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → ∀ (x : X) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → f^[n] x = x → f x = x
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point and Mathlib2.bld_edelstein_iterates_tendsto: X is nonempty, so there is a fixed point p and f^[m] x → p; along the subsequence m = n * k the iterates are constantly x, so x = p by uniqueness of limits.

name: bld2_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_mul_coprime
statement: (p m : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h3 : p % 4 = 3) (hm : ¬ p ∣ m) (x y : ℚ) : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ (p : ℚ) * (m : ℚ)
type: ∀ (p m : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 3 → ¬p ∣ m → ∀ (x y : ℚ), x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ ↑p * ↑m
informal: Uses Mathlib2.nt2_prime_three_mod_four_dvd_sq_add_sq (generalising Mathlib2.bld_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_three_mod_four): clear denominators to a^2 + b^2 = p * m * d^2 in ℤ with d ≠ 0; by strong induction on |d| (or on the p-adic valuation), p ∣ a and p ∣ b, so p^2 ∣ p * m * d^2, so p ∣ d (as p ∤ m), and dividing a, b, d by p gives a smaller solution.

name: bld2_pell_five_solutions_lucas
statement: (x y : ℕ) (h : x ^ 2 = 5 * y ^ 2 + 4) : ∃ n : ℕ, y = Nat.fib (2 * n) ∧ x = p3_lucas (2 * n)
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 = 5 * y ^ 2 + 4 → ∃ n, y = Nat.fib (2 * n) ∧ x = Mathlib2.p3_lucas (2 * n)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_fib_even_index_iff_five_sq_add_four and Mathlib2.an_cassini_int: the characterisation gives y = fib (2n); the Lucas identity L(2n)^2 = 5 fib(2n)^2 + 4 (from Cassini, with L = Mathlib2.p3_lucas) gives x^2 = L(2n)^2, hence x = L(2n) in ℕ.

name: bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) ∣ 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) ∣ 4 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_period (and the argument of Mathlib2.p3_prop2): p3_aux_period with index 2n gives fib (i + 4n) ≡ fib i mod fib (2n), and fib n ∣ fib (2n), so 4n is a period modulo fib n; the least period divides every period (division with remainder), as in p3_prop2.

name: p4_z_spec
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 * Mathlib2.p4_z n < 2 * ↑n ∧ ∀ (k : ℤ), 3 * k < 2 * ↑n → k ≤ Mathlib2.p4_z n
informal: The Lean definition p4_z agrees with the paper's: z(n) is the largest integer with 3 z(n) < 2n.

name: p4_m_spec
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m n) ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ↑n ∧ ∀ (k : ℤ), k ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ↑n → k ≤ ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m n)
informal: The Lean definition p4_m agrees with the paper's: m(n) is the largest integer with m(n)^2 <= 2n.

name: p4_r_spec
statement: (n : ℕ) : n ≤ 2 ^ p4_r n ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, n ≤ 2 ^ k → p4_r n ≤ k
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), n ≤ 2 ^ Mathlib2.p4_r n ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), n ≤ 2 ^ k → Mathlib2.p4_r n ≤ k
informal: The Lean definition p4_r agrees with the paper's: r(n) is the least non-negative integer with n <= 2^r(n).

name: p4_ex1_mono
statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) : p4_z a ≤ p4_z b ∧ p4_m a ≤ p4_m b ∧ p4_r a ≤ p4_r b
type: ∀ (a b : ℕ), a ≤ b → Mathlib2.p4_z a ≤ Mathlib2.p4_z b ∧ Mathlib2.p4_m a ≤ Mathlib2.p4_m b ∧ Mathlib2.p4_r a ≤ Mathlib2.p4_r b
informal: The sequences z, m, r are non-decreasing.

name: p4_ex1_levels
informal: Level sets: z(n)=k iff 3k < 2n <= 3k+3; m(n)=k iff k^2 <= 2n < (k+1)^2; for k>=1, r(n)=k iff 2^(k-1) < n <= 2^k.

name: p4_ex1_table
informal: The table of values of x(n) in Exercise 1.

name: p4_lem1_i
type: ∀ (a b n : ℕ), 0 < a → a ≤ n → n ≤ b → Mathlib2.p4_z a - (↑(Mathlib2.p4_r b) + 1) * ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m b) ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n ∧ Mathlib2.p4_x n ≤ Mathlib2.p4_z b - (↑(Mathlib2.p4_r a) + 1) * ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m a)
informal: Lemma 1(i): for positive integers a <= n <= b, z(a)-(r(b)+1)m(b) <= x(n) <= z(b)-(r(a)+1)m(a).

name: bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq
statement: (n : ℕ) (h5 : 5 ≤ n) (hodd : Odd n) : p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) = 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 5 ≤ n → Odd n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) = 4 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_period and Mathlib2.an_cassini_int: 4n is a period (p3_aux_period at index 2n, fib n ∣ fib (2n)), so the period k divides 4n and n ∣ k, k ∈ {n, 2n, 4n}; k = n fails since fib (n+1) ≡ fib (n-1) ≢ 1; k = 2n fails since fib (2n+1) = fib(n)^2 + fib(n+1)^2 ≡ fib(n-1)^2 ≡ (-1)^n = -1 mod fib n by Cassini, and fib n > 2.

name: p4_lem1_ii
statement: (a b n : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (h1 : a ≤ n) (h2 : n ≤ b) (hx : p4_x a < 0) (hb : 2 * b ≤ 3 * (p4_r a + 1) * p4_m a) (hbmax : ∀ c : ℕ, 2 * c ≤ 3 * (p4_r a + 1) * p4_m a → c ≤ b) : p4_x n < 0
type: ∀ (a b n : ℕ), 0 < a → a ≤ n → n ≤ b → Mathlib2.p4_x a < 0 → 2 * b ≤ 3 * (Mathlib2.p4_r a + 1) * Mathlib2.p4_m a → (∀ (c : ℕ), 2 * c ≤ 3 * (Mathlib2.p4_r a + 1) * Mathlib2.p4_m a → c ≤ b) → Mathlib2.p4_x n < 0
informal: Lemma 1(ii): if x(a) < 0 and b is the largest integer with 2b <= 3(r(a)+1)m(a), then x(n) < 0 for a <= n <= b.

name: bld2_pisano_fib_even_eq
statement: (n : ℕ) (h4 : 4 ≤ n) (h2 : 2 ∣ n) : p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) = 2 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 4 ≤ n → 2 ∣ n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) = 2 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_prop2: the period k divides 2n; being a period forces fib n ∣ fib k, hence n ∣ k (gcd property of Fibonacci numbers, n ≥ 3), so k = n or k = 2n; k = n is impossible because fib (n+1) ≡ fib (n-1) mod fib n and 1 < fib (n-1) < fib n for n ≥ 4.

name: p4_lem1_iii
statement: (a b n : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (h1 : a ≤ n) (h2 : n ≤ b) (hx : 0 < p4_x b) (hamin : 3 * (p4_r b + 1) * p4_m b + 4 ≤ 2 * a) (haleast : ∀ c : ℕ, 3 * (p4_r b + 1) * p4_m b + 4 ≤ 2 * c → a ≤ c) : 0 < p4_x n
type: ∀ (a b n : ℕ), 0 < a → a ≤ n → n ≤ b → 0 < Mathlib2.p4_x b → 3 * (Mathlib2.p4_r b + 1) * Mathlib2.p4_m b + 4 ≤ 2 * a → (∀ (c : ℕ), 3 * (Mathlib2.p4_r b + 1) * Mathlib2.p4_m b + 4 ≤ 2 * c → a ≤ c) → 0 < Mathlib2.p4_x n
informal: Lemma 1(iii): if x(b) > 0 and a is the least integer with 2a >= 3(r(b)+1)m(b)+4, then x(n) > 0 for a <= n <= b.

name: p4_thm1_v_step_disproof
informal: Claim made inside the proof of Theorem 1(v), formalized literally: if B is a positive integer and 2^(k+2) > 3B+1 then x(2^(2k+2)) > B. (Numerically false: k=1, B=2 gives x(16) = -15.)

name: bld2_card_le_sum_of_prod_eq_one
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (ι : Type*) (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → R) (ha : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ a i) (hp : ∏ i ∈ s, a i = 1) : (s.card : R) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, a i
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (ι : Type u_2) (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → R), (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ a i) → ∏ i ∈ s, a i = 1 → ↑s.card ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, a i
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_an_amgm_finset_ordered_ring: with ∏ a = 1 the AM-GM inequality reads card^card ≤ (∑ a)^card; both bases are nonnegative, so for s nonempty taking card-th roots (pow_le_pow_left contrapositive) gives card ≤ ∑ a; s empty is trivial.

name: p4_rem1_4096
type: Mathlib2.p4_z 4096 = 2730 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_m 4096 = 90 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_r 4096 = 12 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_x 4096 = 1560

name: p4_small_classify
informal: Auditor's helper lemma (not a numbered statement of the paper): the finite verification for 1 <= n <= 4096 underlying Theorem 1, done block by block on the maximal intervals where r and m are constant (the paper's Lemma 2 / table).

name: bld2_commutator_eq_center_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hnc : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : commutator G = Subgroup.center G
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → commutator G = Subgroup.center G
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: the centre has order p, so G / Z(G) has order p^2 and is abelian, giving commutator G ≤ Z(G); the commutator subgroup is nontrivial (G non-abelian) and Z(G) has prime order, so the inclusion is an equality.

name: p4_lem2_greatest
statement: (a q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hq : 2 * q < (p4_m a + 1) ^ 2) (hqmax : ∀ c : ℕ, 2 * c < (p4_m a + 1) ^ 2 → c ≤ q) : IsGreatest {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ p4_r k = p4_r a ∧ p4_m k = p4_m a} (min q (2 ^ p4_r a))
type: ∀ (a q : ℕ), 0 < a → 2 * q < (Mathlib2.p4_m a + 1) ^ 2 → (∀ (c : ℕ), 2 * c < (Mathlib2.p4_m a + 1) ^ 2 → c ≤ q) → IsGreatest {k | 0 < k ∧ Mathlib2.p4_r k = Mathlib2.p4_r a ∧ Mathlib2.p4_m k = Mathlib2.p4_m a} (min q (2 ^ Mathlib2.p4_r a))
informal: Lemma 2, first part: with s=r(a), t=m(a), q the largest integer with 2q < (t+1)^2 and b(a)=min(q,2^s), b(a) is the largest positive integer k with r(k)=s and m(k)=t.

name: p4_lem2_chain
type: ∀ (a q : ℕ), 0 < a → 2 * q < (Mathlib2.p4_m a + 1) ^ 2 → (∀ (c : ℕ), 2 * c < (Mathlib2.p4_m a + 1) ^ 2 → c ≤ q) → ∀ (n1 n2 : ℕ), a ≤ n1 → n1 ≤ n2 → n2 ≤ min q (2 ^ Mathlib2.p4_r a) → Mathlib2.p4_x a ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n1 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_x n1 = Mathlib2.p4_z n1 - (↑(Mathlib2.p4_r a) + 1) * ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m a) ∧ Mathlib2.p4_x n1 ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n2 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_x n2 ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x (min q (2 ^ Mathlib2.p4_r a))
informal: Lemma 2, second part: for a <= n1 <= n2 <= b(a): x(a) <= x(n1) = z(n1)-(r(a)+1)m(a) <= x(n2) <= x(b(a)).

name: p4_rem1_lower
type: ∀ (s n : ℕ), 2 ^ s < n → n ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) → Mathlib2.p4_r n = s + 1 ∧ Mathlib2.p4_z (2 ^ s) - (↑s + 2) * ↑(Mathlib2.p4_m (2 ^ (s + 1))) ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n

name: p4_rem1_even
informal: Remark 1, s=2k: 2^k <= m(2^s) < 2^(k+1) and z(2^s)=p where 2^(2k+1)=3p+2.

name: p4_rem1_odd
informal: Remark 1, s=2k+1: m(2^s)=2^(k+1) and z(2^s)=q where 2^(2k+2)=3q+1.

name: bld2_card_conjClasses_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hnc : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card (ConjClasses G) = p ^ 2 + p - 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card (ConjClasses G) = p ^ 2 + p - 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: |Z(G)| = p gives p singleton classes; a non-central x has centralizer containing Z(G) and x, proper in G, hence of order p^2, so its class has p elements; the p^3 - p non-central elements form p^2 - 1 classes (class equation).

name: p4_rem1_large
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 4096 < n → 0 < Mathlib2.p4_x n
informal: Remark 1 conclusion: x(n) > 0 for every n > 2^12 = 4096.

name: p4_thm1_i
informal: Theorem 1(i): x(n)=0 iff n is one of 436, 451, 529, 545, 546.

name: p4_thm1_ii
informal: Theorem 1(ii): x(n)<0 iff n <= 435 or n = 450 or 513 <= n <= 528.

name: lib_matrix_rank_smul
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (m n : Type*) [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (c : K) (hc : c ≠ 0) (M : Matrix m n K) : Matrix.rank (c • M) = Matrix.rank M
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) [Fintype m] [inst_2 : Fintype n] (c : K), c ≠ 0 → ∀ (M : Matrix m n K), (c • M).rank = M.rank
informal: Scaling a (rectangular) matrix over a field by a nonzero scalar does not change its rank: rank (c • M) = rank M. Promoted from Mathlib2.bld_involution_trace_rank_aux1 (also re-proved as bld2_tripotent_rank_split_aux1 and bld2_involution_iff_rank_add_rank_aux1); generalised from square to rectangular matrices.

name: p4_thm1_iii
informal: Theorem 1(iii): x(n)>0 iff 437 <= n <= 512 with n not 450, 451, or n >= 530 with n not 545, 546.

name: lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (m n : Type*) [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n K) : Matrix.rank A = 0 ↔ A = 0
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) [Fintype m] [inst_2 : Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n K), A.rank = 0 ↔ A = 0
informal: A matrix over a field has rank zero iff it is the zero matrix (Matrix.rank A = 0 ↔ A = 0). Promoted from inline derivations (Submodule.finrank_eq_zero + LinearMap.range_eq_bot) inside two bld2 rank proofs in shard S0017.

name: p4_thm1_iv
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 547 ≤ n → 0 < Mathlib2.p4_x n
informal: Theorem 1(iv): x(n) > 0 for every n >= 547.

name: p4_thm1_vi
type: Mathlib2.p4_x 129 = -59 ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ≠ 129 → -58 ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n
informal: Theorem 1(vi): x(129) = -59 and x(n) >= -58 for every positive n other than 129.

name: p4_thm1_v_step_fixed
informal: Auditor's correction, not the paper's wording: the claim in the proof of Theorem 1(v) holds once k >= 4: if 2^(k+2) > 3B+1 and k >= 4 then x(2^(2k+2)) > B.

name: p4_thm1_v
type: ¬∃ n0, 0 < n0 ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → Mathlib2.p4_x n ≤ Mathlib2.p4_x n0
informal: Theorem 1(v): x(n) has no maximal value (over positive integers n).

name: p4_rem2
statement: : IsLeast {N : ℕ | 0 < N ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → 0 < p4_x m} 547
type: IsLeast {N | 0 < N ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ), N ≤ m → 0 < Mathlib2.p4_x m} 547
informal: Remark 2: 547 is the least positive integer N such that x(m) > 0 for all m >= N.

name: lib_matrix_charpoly_eq_X_pow_of_isNilpotent
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι R) (h : IsNilpotent A) : A.charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] [IsReduced R] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι R), IsNilpotent A → A.charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card ι
informal: The characteristic polynomial of a nilpotent square matrix over a reduced commutative ring is X^n (n = size). Promoted from the inline first step of Mathlib2.gen_lin_nilpotent_pow_card_reduced (also re-derived in gen_lin_nilpotent_det_one_add_reduced).

name: lib_matrix_transpose_mul_self_eq_zero_iff
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (m n : Type*) [Fintype m] (B : Matrix m n R) : B.transpose * B = 0 ↔ B = 0
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) [inst_3 : Fintype m] (B : Matrix m n R), B.transpose * B = 0 ↔ B = 0
informal: Over a linearly ordered ring, Bᵀ * B = 0 iff B = 0, for rectangular B (the Gram matrix vanishes only for the zero matrix; diagonal entries are sums of squares). Promoted from Mathlib2.gen_lin_symm_nilpotent_eq_zero_ordered_aux1 (also inline in lin_symm_nilpotent_eq_zero); generalised to rectangular matrices and to an iff.

name: lib_matrix_rank_le_iff_exists_factorization
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (n p : Type*) [Fintype n] [Fintype p] (B : Matrix n p K) (r : ℕ) : B.rank ≤ r ↔ ∃ (M : Matrix n (Fin r) K) (N : Matrix (Fin r) p K), B = M * N
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (n : Type u_2) (p : Type u_3) [Fintype n] [inst_2 : Fintype p] (B : Matrix n p K) (r : ℕ), B.rank ≤ r ↔ ∃ M N, B = M * N
informal: Rank factorisation, as a characterisation of rank: an n×p matrix B over a field has rank ≤ r iff it factors as B = M * N through K^r (M : n×r, N : r×p). The case r = rank B is Mathlib2.bld_frobenius_rank_inequality_aux1, from which this is promoted.

name: lib_matrix_mul_rank_le_add_rank_pow
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (j : ℕ) : j * Matrix.rank A ≤ (j - 1) * Fintype.card ι + Matrix.rank (A ^ j)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (j : ℕ), j * A.rank ≤ (j - 1) * Fintype.card ι + (A ^ j).rank
informal: Iterated Sylvester rank inequality for powers of a square matrix over a field: j * rank A ≤ (j - 1) * n + rank (A^j) (so A^j = 0 forces rank A ≤ (j-1)n/j). Promoted from Mathlib2.bld_nilpotent_rank_bound_aux1 (stated there with j+1).

name: lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period
statement: (m N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) : p3_pisano m ∣ N ↔ ∀ i : ℕ, Nat.fib (i + N) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m]
type: ∀ (m N : ℕ), 0 < N → (Mathlib2.p3_pisano m ∣ N ↔ ∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.fib (i + N) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m])
informal: The positive periods of the Fibonacci sequence mod m are exactly the positive multiples of the Pisano period p3_pisano m (the least period divides every period, and every multiple of it is a period). Promoted from Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul_aux1 and bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq_aux1 (same argument also inline in p3_prop2).

name: lib_fib_period_iff
statement: (N m : ℕ) : (∀ i : ℕ, Nat.fib (i + m) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD N]) ↔ Nat.fib m ≡ 0 [MOD N] ∧ Nat.fib (m + 1) ≡ 1 [MOD N]
type: ∀ (N m : ℕ), (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.fib (i + m) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD N]) ↔ Nat.fib m ≡ 0 [MOD N] ∧ Nat.fib (m + 1) ≡ 1 [MOD N]
informal: Fibonacci period criterion: m is a period of the Fibonacci sequence modulo N iff F_m ≡ 0 and F_(m+1) ≡ 1 (mod N). Promoted from Mathlib2.p3_aux_period_aux2 / p3_aux_period_aux3 (the same two-term induction is re-done in p3_cor1_aux3/aux4).

name: lib_fib_sq_modEq_neg_one_pow
statement: (n : ℕ) : (Nat.fib n : ℤ) ^ 2 ≡ (-1) ^ (n + 1) [ZMOD (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℤ)]
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib n) ^ 2 ≡ (-1) ^ (n + 1) [ZMOD ↑(Nat.fib (n + 1))]
informal: Cassini's identity as a congruence: F_n^2 ≡ (-1)^(n+1) modulo F_(n+1); in particular F_n^4 ≡ 1 (mod F_(n+1)). Sharpens Mathlib2.p3_cor1_aux1 / p3_cor1_aux2 (squared Cassini), which re-derive Cassini although Mathlib2.an_cassini_int exists (also re-proved as p3_aux_period_aux1 and r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square_s1h1).

name: lib_simpleGraph_sum_degree_sq_le_card_mul_card_edgeFinset
statement: (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : ∑ v, G.degree v ^ 2 ≤ Fintype.card V * G.edgeFinset.card
type: ∀ (V : Type u_1) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → ∑ v, G.degree v ^ 2 ≤ Fintype.card V * G.edgeFinset.card
informal: In a triangle-free graph on n vertices with e edges the sum of squared degrees is at most n * e (sum deg u + deg v ≤ n over the edges); this is the key step of Mantel's theorem. Promoted from Mathlib2.bld2_mantel_equality_regular_aux1 (also proved inline in bld_mantel_triangle_free); generalised to an arbitrary universe.

name: lib_mul_pow_mul_sub_le_pow_succ_sub_pow_succ
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (a b : R) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (m : ℕ) : ((m : R) + 1) * a ^ m * (b - a) ≤ b ^ (m + 1) - a ^ (m + 1) ∧ b ^ (m + 1) - a ^ (m + 1) ≤ ((m : R) + 1) * b ^ m * (b - a)
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (a b : R), 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → ∀ (m : ℕ), (↑m + 1) * a ^ m * (b - a) ≤ b ^ (m + 1) - a ^ (m + 1) ∧ b ^ (m + 1) - a ^ (m + 1) ≤ (↑m + 1) * b ^ m * (b - a)
informal: Two-sided tangent-line (generalised Bernoulli / mean-value) inequality for powers in a linearly ordered commutative ring: for a, b ≥ 0, (m+1) a^m (b - a) ≤ b^(m+1) - a^(m+1) ≤ (m+1) b^m (b - a). Promoted from Mathlib2.gen_an_amgm_finset_ordered_ring_aux1 (the left inequality).

name: lib_expanding_iterate_dist_le
statement: {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) (k : ℕ) (x y : X) : dist x y ≤ dist (f^[k] x) (f^[k] y)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : PseudoMetricSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), dist x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y)) → ∀ (k : ℕ) (x y : X), dist x y ≤ dist (f^[k] x) (f^[k] y)
informal: Iterates of a distance non-decreasing (expanding) self-map of a pseudometric space are again expanding: dist x y ≤ dist (f^[k] x) (f^[k] y). Promoted from Mathlib2.top_expanding_compact_isometry_aux1 (the isometry analogue is re-derived in top_isometry_compact_surjective); generalised from metric to pseudometric spaces.

name: lib_compactSpace_exists_lt_and_dist_lt
statement: {Y : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (u : ℕ → Y) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ m n : ℕ, m < n ∧ dist (u m) (u n) < ε
type: ∀ {Y : Type u_1} [inst : PseudoMetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (u : ℕ → Y) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ m n, m < n ∧ dist (u m) (u n) < ε
informal: Pigeonhole principle in a compact pseudometric space: every sequence has two terms u m, u n with m < n at distance < ε (take a convergent subsequence). Promoted from Mathlib2.top_expanding_compact_isometry_aux2 (the same argument is used in top_isometry_compact_surjective); generalised from metric to pseudometric spaces.

name: lib_list_exists_perm_isChain_of_pairwise_or
statement: {α : Type*} (r : α → α → Prop) (l : List α) (hnd : l.Nodup) (hl : ∀ a ∈ l, ∀ b ∈ l, a ≠ b → r a b ∨ r b a) : ∃ l' : List α, l'.Perm l ∧ List.IsChain r l'
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (r : α → α → Prop) (l : List α), l.Nodup → (∀ a ∈ l, ∀ b ∈ l, a ≠ b → r a b ∨ r b a) → ∃ l', l'.Perm l ∧ List.IsChain r l'
informal: Rédei's theorem in list form (every tournament has a Hamiltonian path): a duplicate-free list whose distinct elements are pairwise r-comparable (r a b ∨ r b a) can be permuted into an r-chain. Promoted from Mathlib2.comb_tournament_hamiltonian_path_aux2; generalised to an arbitrary universe.

name: lib_finset_exists_cut_sum_le_four_mul
statement: (V : Type*) [DecidableEq V] (f : V → V → ℕ) (hsym : ∀ u v, f u v = f v u) (hirr : ∀ u, f u u = 0) (S : Finset V) : ∃ s : Finset V, s ⊆ S ∧ (∑ u ∈ S, ∑ v ∈ S, f u v) ≤ 4 * ∑ u ∈ s, ∑ v ∈ S \ s, f u v
type: ∀ (V : Type u_1) [inst : DecidableEq V] (f : V → V → ℕ), (∀ (u v : V), f u v = f v u) → (∀ (u : V), f u u = 0) → ∀ (S : Finset V), ∃ s ⊆ S, ∑ u ∈ S, ∑ v ∈ S, f u v ≤ 4 * ∑ u ∈ s, ∑ v ∈ S \ s, f u v
informal: Weighted max-cut bound: for a symmetric, zero-diagonal weight f : V → V → ℕ on a finset S there is a cut (s, S \ s) carrying at least half of the total weight (the ordered-pair sum over S × S is ≤ 4 × the one-directional cut sum). Promoted from Mathlib2.comb_exists_cut_half_edges_aux1; generalised to an arbitrary universe.

name: bld3_pell_five_neg_one_solutions
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 + 1 = 5 * y ^ 2 → ∃ n, 2 * y = Nat.fib (6 * n + 3) ∧ 2 * x = Mathlib2.p3_lucas (6 * n + 3)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_fib_odd_index_iff_five_sq_sub_four and Mathlib2.bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq: (2x)^2 + 4 = 5 (2y)^2, so 2y = fib (2m+1) and 2x = L_(2m+1) by the odd-index description and the Lucas–Fibonacci identity; fib (2m+1) even forces 3 ∣ 2m+1, i.e. 2m+1 = 6n+3.

name: bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : Matrix.rank (A ^ (Fintype.card ι + 1)) = Matrix.rank (A ^ Fintype.card ι)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), (A ^ (Fintype.card ι + 1)).rank = (A ^ Fintype.card ι).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex: Fitting-type stabilisation: the drops d_k = rank A^k - rank A^(k+1) are non-negative and, by convexity, non-increasing; if d_n > 0 with n = card ι then d_0,...,d_n ≥ 1 and rank A^0 = n ≥ n + 1, contradiction.

name: bld3_pell_five_neg_four_solutions_lucas
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 + 4 = 5 * y ^ 2 → ∃ n, y = Nat.fib (2 * n + 1) ∧ x = Mathlib2.p3_lucas (2 * n + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_fib_odd_index_iff_five_sq_sub_four and Mathlib2.bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq: the odd-index characterisation gives y = fib (2n+1) (choose n with the right value; fib 1 = fib 2 only matters for y = 1 where n = 0 works), and L^2 = 5 F^2 - 4 at odd index forces x = p3_lucas (2n+1) by injectivity of squaring on ℕ.

name: bld3_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod_le
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : ∏ i ∈ Finset.range n, a (i + 1) / 2 ≤ 2 / Real.pi + 2 * Real.pi / (3 * 4 ^ (n + 1))
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod and Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_viete_prod_gt: by the finite Viète product the product equals 1/(2^n sin x) with x = π/2^(n+1); sin x ≥ x - x^3/6 and 1/(1-t) ≤ 1 + 2t for t = x^2/6 ≤ 1/2 give the explicit O(4^-n) upper bound matching the library lower bound 2/π.

name: bld3_nilpotent_rank_pow_le
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (k : ℕ) : Matrix.rank (A ^ k) ≤ Fintype.card ι - k
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → ∀ (k : ℕ), (A ^ k).rank ≤ Fintype.card ι - k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex and Mathlib2.bld_nilpotent_rank_bound: by convexity the drops d_k are non-increasing, so once d_k = 0 the rank is constant forever; nilpotency forces that constant to be 0, hence the rank drops by at least 1 at each step until it reaches 0, giving rank A^k ≤ n - k (truncated subtraction).

name: bld3_pell_five_one_solutions
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 = 5 * y ^ 2 + 1 → ∃ n, 2 * y = Nat.fib (6 * n) ∧ 2 * x = Mathlib2.p3_lucas (6 * n)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pell_five_solutions_lucas: (2x)^2 = 5 (2y)^2 + 4, so 2y = fib (2m) and 2x = p3_lucas (2m); fib (2m) is even iff 3 ∣ 2m iff 3 ∣ m (fib mod 2 has period 3), so 2m = 6n.

name: bld3_sqrt_two_rec_pi_limit
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ n * Real.sqrt (2 - a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.pi / 2))
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => 2 ^ n * √(2 - a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.pi / 2))
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_asymptotic: (2^n √(2 - a n)) = √(4^n (2 - a n)); compose the defect asymptotic 4^n (2 - a n) → π^2/4 with continuity of the square root, √(π^2/4) = π/2 (the classical nested-radical formula for π).

name: bld3_mantel_equality_same_neighbors
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) (x y : V) (hxy : ¬ G.Adj x y) (z : V) : G.Adj x z ↔ G.Adj y z
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ∀ (x y : V), ¬G.Adj x y → ∀ (z : V), G.Adj x z ↔ G.Adj y z
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_mantel_equality_regular and Mathlib2.comb_degree_add_degree_le_of_triangle_free: all degrees are n/2; for an edge u v the neighbourhoods are disjoint of total size n so they partition V; if z ~ x then y lies in N(x) or N(z), the former is excluded, so y ~ z (the extremal graph is complete bipartite).

name: bld3_commuting_idempotents_rank_sub
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A = A) (hB : B * B = B) (hAB : A * B = B * A) : Matrix.rank (A - B) + 2 * Matrix.rank (A * B) = Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank B
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A → B * B = B → A * B = B * A → (A - B).rank + 2 * (A * B).rank = A.rank + B.rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_idempotent_sum_rank and Mathlib2.bld2_commuting_idempotents_rank_join: P = A - AB and Q = B - AB are orthogonal idempotents with A = AB + P, B = AB + Q, so rank P = rank A - rank AB and rank Q = rank B - rank AB; (P - Q)^2 = P + Q is idempotent of rank rank P + rank Q, which squeezes rank (A - B) = rank (P - Q) between rank (P + Q) and rank P + rank Q.

name: bld3_sqrt_two_rec_defect_tsum_bounds
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate and Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable: upper bound: compare termwise with the geometric series ∑ π^2/4^(n+1) = π^2/3 using the rate; lower bound: 2 - a (n+1) = (2 - a n)/(2 + a (n+1)) ≥ (2 - a n)/4 gives 2 - a n ≥ 2/4^n, whose sum is 8/3; summability from the library.

name: bld3_mantel_equality_colorable_two
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) : G.Colorable 2
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → G.Colorable 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_mantel_equality_regular and Mathlib2.bld_mantel_triangle_free: if there is no edge then n = 0; otherwise fix an edge u v: N(u) and N(v) are disjoint with |N(u)| + |N(v)| = n by regularity, so they partition V, and each is independent by triangle-freeness; colour by membership in N(u).

name: bld3_sq_card_le_sum_mul_sum_inv
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] (ι : Type*) (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → K) (ha : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < a i) : (s.card : K) ^ 2 ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, a i) * ∑ i ∈ s, (a i)⁻¹
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] (ι : Type u_2) (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → K), (∀ i ∈ s, 0 < a i) → ↑s.card ^ 2 ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, a i) * ∑ i ∈ s, (a i)⁻¹
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_an_amgm_finset_ordered_ring and Mathlib2.bld2_card_le_sum_of_prod_eq_one: AM-GM for a and for a⁻¹ gives n^n ∏ a ≤ (∑ a)^n and n^n ∏ a⁻¹ ≤ (∑ a⁻¹)^n; multiply (the products cancel) to get (n^2)^n ≤ ((∑ a)(∑ a⁻¹))^n and take n-th roots by monotonicity of powers.

name: bld3_iterate_shrinking_iterates_tendsto
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) < dist x y) (p : X) (hp : f p = p) (x : X) : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => f^[k] x) Filter.atTop (nhds p)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (n : ℕ), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f^[n] x) (f^[n] y) < dist x y) → ∀ (p : X), f p = p → ∀ (x : X), Filter.Tendsto (fun k => f^[k] x) Filter.atTop (nhds p)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_edelstein_iterates_tendsto and Mathlib2.bld_iterate_shrinking_unique_fixed_point: n = 0 forces X subsingleton; otherwise apply Edelstein convergence to g = f^[n] (which fixes p) at each of the n starting points f^[r] x, r < n, and merge the n residue-class subsequences f^[n k + r] x = g^[k] (f^[r] x).

name: bld3_rank_tripotent_defect
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : Matrix.rank (A * A + A) + Matrix.rank (A * A - A) = Matrix.rank A + Matrix.rank (A * A * A - A)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), (A * A + A).rank + (A * A - A).rank = A.rank + (A * A * A - A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_frobenius_rank_inequality and Mathlib2.bld2_tripotent_rank_split: generalises the tripotent rank split (the case A^3 = A); ≤ is Frobenius for the triple (A + 1, A, A - 1); ≥ by block elimination on diag(A^2 + A, A^2 - A) using 2A = (A^2 + A) - (A^2 - A) and invertibility of 2.

name: bld3_self_summable_of_two_mul_dvd_fib
statement: (n : ℕ) (h2 : 2 ∣ n) (h : 2 * n ∣ Nat.fib n) : p3_self_summable n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ∣ n → 2 * n ∣ Nat.fib n → Mathlib2.p3_self_summable n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_period and Mathlib2.p3_remark2: write fib n = 2 n k; by the period lemma fib (2 + 2 n k) ≡ fib 2 = 1 mod fib n, so fib n ∣ fib (fib n + 2) - 1, which is self-summability by Remark 2 (e.g. n = 12, 24, 36).

name: bld3_pisano_pos_and_period
statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : 0 < p3_pisano m ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, Nat.fib (i + p3_pisano m) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m]
type: ∀ (m : ℕ), 0 < m → 0 < Mathlib2.p3_pisano m ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.fib (i + Mathlib2.p3_pisano m) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m]
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq: by its auxiliary lemma bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq_aux1 it suffices to exhibit one positive period N; pigeonhole on the pairs (fib i, fib (i+1)) mod m gives i < j with equal pairs, and the recurrence run backwards (fib (i) = fib (i+2) - fib (i+1)) shows N = j - i is a period.

name: bld3_rank_involution_defect
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : Matrix.rank (1 + A) + Matrix.rank (1 - A) = Fintype.card ι + Matrix.rank (1 - A * A)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), (1 + A).rank + (1 - A).rank = Fintype.card ι + (1 - A * A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rank_add_rank_one_sub and Mathlib2.bld2_involution_iff_rank_add_rank: apply the idempotent-defect identity to B = (1/2) • (1 + A): 1 - B = (1/2) • (1 - A) and B - B * B = (1/4) • (1 - A * A), and nonzero scalars do not change rank; this refines the involution criterion.

name: bld3_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_of_odd_padicValNat
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp4 : p % 4 = 3) (hodd : Odd (padicValNat p n)) (x y : ℚ) : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ (n : ℚ)
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 3 → Odd (padicValNat p n) → ∀ (x y : ℚ), x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 ≠ ↑n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_mul_coprime: write n = p^(2k+1) m with p ∤ m; if x^2 + y^2 = n then (x/p^k)^2 + (y/p^k)^2 = p m, contradicting the library theorem (rational form of the two-squares obstruction).

name: bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period
statement: (m k : ℕ) (hk : ∀ i : ℕ, Nat.fib (i + k) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m]) : p3_pisano m ∣ k
type: ∀ (m k : ℕ), (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.fib (i + k) ≡ Nat.fib i [MOD m]) → Mathlib2.p3_pisano m ∣ k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq: if k = 0 trivial; otherwise by the auxiliary lemma bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq_aux1 the Pisano period P is a positive period, and k % P is again a period smaller than P, so by minimality (Nat.sInf_le) k % P = 0.

name: bld3_dvd_fibsum_of_pisano_dvd
statement: (m : ℕ) (h : p3_pisano m ∣ m) : m ∣ p3_fibsum m
type: ∀ (m : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_pisano m ∣ m → m ∣ Mathlib2.p3_fibsum m
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_prop1 and Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq: if p3_pisano m = 0 then m = 0 and p3_fibsum 0 = 0; otherwise m is a multiple of a period (aux1), so fib (m + 2) ≡ fib 2 = 1 mod m and p3_fibsum m = fib (m + 2) - 1 ≡ 0.

name: bld3_pow_prime_mem_center_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (g : G) : g ^ p ∈ Subgroup.center G
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → ∀ (g : G), g ^ p ∈ Subgroup.center G
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld2_commutator_eq_center_of_card_prime_cube: the centre has order p so G/Z has order p^2 and is not cyclic (else G abelian), hence every element of G/Z has order dividing p, i.e. g^p ∈ Z.

name: bld3_pisano_even
statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : Even (p3_pisano m)
type: ∀ (m : ℕ), 3 ≤ m → Even (Mathlib2.p3_pisano m)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq and Mathlib2.r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square_s1h1: let k be the Pisano period (if it is 0 done; else a period by bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq_aux1), so fib k ≡ 0 and fib (k+1) ≡ 1 mod m; Cassini fib(k+1)^2 - fib(k+1) fib k - fib k^2 = (-1)^k then gives (-1)^k ≡ 1 mod m, and m ≥ 3 excludes k odd.

name: bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd
statement: (m n : ℕ) (h : m ∣ n) : p3_pisano m ∣ p3_pisano n
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m ∣ n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano m ∣ Mathlib2.p3_pisano n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq: if p3_pisano n = 0 trivial; otherwise it is a period mod n (aux1 of bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq), hence a period mod m, and the least period mod m divides every period (remainder argument with minimality).

name: bld3_compact_mutual_expanding_isometry
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X) (hf : ∀ x x' : X, dist x x' ≤ dist (f x) (f x')) (hg : ∀ y y' : Y, dist y y' ≤ dist (g y) (g y')) : Isometry f ∧ Function.Surjective f
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X), (∀ (x x' : X), dist x x' ≤ dist (f x) (f x')) → (∀ (y y' : Y), dist y y' ≤ dist (g y) (g y')) → Isometry f ∧ Function.Surjective f
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_expanding_compact_isometryEquiv and Mathlib2.top_expanding_compact_isometry: g ∘ f is expanding on compact X hence an isometry, which squeezes dist x x' ≤ dist (f x) (f x') ≤ dist (g (f x)) (g (f x')) = dist x x'; f ∘ g is expanding on Y hence a bijective isometry, so f is surjective (Cantor–Bernstein for compact metric spaces).

name: bld3_compact_mutual_nonexpanding_surjections_isometry
