statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hf' : ∀ x x' : X, dist (f x) (f x') ≤ dist x x') (hg : Function.Surjective g) (hg' : ∀ y y' : Y, dist (g y) (g y') ≤ dist y y') : Isometry f
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X), Function.Surjective f → (∀ (x x' : X), dist (f x) (f x') ≤ dist x x') → Function.Surjective g → (∀ (y y' : Y), dist (g y) (g y') ≤ dist y y') → Isometry f
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry: g ∘ f is a non-expanding surjection of compact X, hence an isometry, so dist x x' = dist (g (f x)) (g (f x')) ≤ dist (f x) (f x') ≤ dist x x'.

name: bld3_pisano_fib_div_fib_tendsto_zero
statement: : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (p3_pisano (Nat.fib n) : ℝ) / (Nat.fib n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
type: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Nat.fib n)) / ↑(Nat.fib n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul: the Pisano period of fib n divides 4n so is at most 4n, while fib n grows at least like n^2 (e.g. fib (n+2) ≥ n^2/4 or exponentially), so the ratio is squeezed to 0; strengthens the liminf statement p3_cor1.

name: bld3_edelstein_iterates_tendsto_uniformly
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) (p : X) (hp : f p = p) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) p < ε
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → ∀ (p : X), f p = p → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → ∀ (x : X), dist (f^[n] x) p < ε
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_edelstein_iterates_tendsto: the continuous functions x ↦ dist (f^[n] x) p decrease in n and tend to 0 pointwise by the library theorem; Dini's argument (the open sets {x | dist (f^[n] x) p < ε} increase and cover the compact X) gives uniformity.

name: bld3_mul_pow_prime_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (a b : G) : (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → p ≠ 2 → ∀ (a b : G), (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_commutator_eq_center_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: commutators are central of order dividing p, so by induction (a b)^k = a^k b^k c^(k(k-1)/2) with c the central commutator of b and a; for odd p, p ∣ p(p-1)/2 and c^p = 1 (false for p = 2, e.g. the dihedral group of order 8).

name: bld3_card_sylow_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card (Sylow p G) = q
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Nat.Prime q → p < q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card (Sylow p G) = q
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_eq_bot_of_card_prime_mul_prime: the number of Sylow p-subgroups divides q, so is 1 or q; if 1 the Sylow p-subgroup P is normal of order p, G acts on it by conjugation through Aut(P) of order p - 1 coprime to pq, so P is central, contradicting the trivial centre.

name: bld3_card_conjClasses_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card (ConjClasses G) = p + (q - 1) / p
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → p < q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card (ConjClasses G) = p + (q - 1) / p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_eq_bot_of_card_prime_mul_prime and Mathlib2.alg_isCyclic_of_card_eq_prime_mul_prime: the centre is trivial, so every non-identity class has size p or q; the normal Sylow q-subgroup contributes (q-1)/p classes of size p (centralizer of order q), the remaining q(p-1) elements of order p have centralizer of order p and form p - 1 classes of size q; total 1 + (q-1)/p + (p-1).

name: bld3_card_centralizer_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (g : G) (hg : g ∉ Subgroup.center G) : Nat.card (Subgroup.centralizer ({g} : Set G)) = p ^ 2
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → ∀ g ∉ Subgroup.center G, Nat.card ↥(Subgroup.centralizer {g}) = p ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: the centralizer strictly contains the centre (order p, and it contains g) and is a proper subgroup (g not central), so by Lagrange its order is p^2.

name: bld3_edelstein_iInter_range_iterate
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) (p : X) (hp : f p = p) : ⋂ n : ℕ, Set.range (f^[n]) = {p}
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → ∀ (p : X), f p = p → ⋂ n, Set.range f^[n] = {p}
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_edelstein_iterates_tendsto and Mathlib2.bld2_edelstein_no_periodic_points: p is in every range since f^[n] p = p; conversely if y = f^[n] (x_n) for all n, uniform convergence of the iterates to p (Dini applied to the monotone pointwise convergence from the library) gives dist y p < ε for every ε.

name: bld3_card_abelianization_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card (Abelianization G) = p ^ 2
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card (Abelianization G) = p ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_commutator_eq_center_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: Abelianization G = G ⧸ commutator G, the commutator subgroup equals the centre, which has order p; Lagrange gives index p^2.

name: bld3_hardy_means_tendsto_zero
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (ha : Summable (fun k : ℕ => a k ^ 2)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), (Summable fun k => a k ^ 2) → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) / (↑k + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum: by Hardy the squares of the Cesàro means are summable, so they tend to 0, hence so do the means (continuity of sqrt / abs).

name: p5_dedekind_psi
statement: def p5_dedekind_psi (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, p ^ (n.factorization p - 1) * (p + 1)
type: ℕ → ℕ
informal: Dedekind psi function: psi(n) = prod over primes p | n of p^(a_p - 1) (p+1), where a_p is the exponent of p in n; psi(1) = 1 (and psi(0) = 1 by the empty-product convention).

name: p5_psi_prime_pow
statement: (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : p5_dedekind_psi (p ^ (k + 1)) = p ^ k * (p + 1)
type: ∀ (p k : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi (p ^ (k + 1)) = p ^ k * (p + 1)
informal: Spec for the Dedekind psi definition: psi(p^(k+1)) = p^k (p+1).

name: p5_sigma_ge_succ
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n + 1 ≤ ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → n + 1 ≤ (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n
informal: Equation (8): sigma(n) >= n+1 for n >= 2.

name: p5_sigma_prime_mul_of_dvd
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p ∣ n) (hn : n ≠ 0) : p * ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n < ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 (p * n)
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ n → n ≠ 0 → p * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n < (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) (p * n)
informal: Equation (7), sigma part: if p | n then sigma(np) > p sigma(n).

name: lib_convexOn_univ_eq_of_bddAbove
statement: {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f) (M : ℝ) (hM : ∀ x, f x ≤ M) (x y : E) : f x = f y
type: ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : Module ℝ E] (f : E → ℝ), ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f → ∀ (M : ℝ), (∀ (x : E), f x ≤ M) → ∀ (x y : E), f x = f y
informal: A convex function on a real vector space that is bounded above is constant (Liouville-type property of convex functions). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.ana_convex_bddAbove_const_aux1 (the case E = ℝ).

name: lib_convex_nat_seq_add_mul_sub_le
informal: For a convex ℕ-valued sequence, a drop d = f m - f (m+1) ≥ 0 at step m propagates backwards, so f 0 ≥ f (m+1) + (m+1)·d (quantitative form; d ≥ 1 gives f (m+1) + (m+1) ≤ f 0). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes_aux2 (and _aux1; used for rank stabilisation of matrix powers).

name: p5_psi_mul_coprime
statement: (m n : ℕ) (h : m.Coprime n) : p5_dedekind_psi (m * n) = p5_dedekind_psi m * p5_dedekind_psi n
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m.Coprime n → Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi (m * n) = Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi m * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n
informal: Spec: Dedekind psi is multiplicative on coprime arguments.

name: lib_fib_cassini_cast
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) : (Nat.fib (n + 2) : R) * (Nat.fib n : R) - (Nat.fib (n + 1) : R) ^ 2 = (-1) ^ (n + 1)
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib (n + 2)) * ↑(Nat.fib n) - ↑(Nat.fib (n + 1)) ^ 2 = (-1) ^ (n + 1)
informal: Cassini's identity F_(n+2) F_n - F_(n+1)^2 = (-1)^(n+1) in an arbitrary commutative ring (e.g. ZMod p). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.p3_aux_period_aux1 (same identity over ℤ as Mathlib2.an_cassini_int, r3_fib_iff_five_sq_pm_four_is_square_s1h1, p3_cor1_aux1).

name: p5_psi_prime_mul_of_dvd
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p ∣ n) (hn : n ≠ 0) : p5_dedekind_psi (p * n) = p * p5_dedekind_psi n
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ n → n ≠ 0 → Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi (p * n) = p * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n
informal: Equation (7), psi part: if p | n then psi(np) = p psi(n).

name: lib_fib_dvd_fib_iff
statement: (m n : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 2) : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib n ↔ m ∣ n
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m ≠ 2 → (Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib n ↔ m ∣ n)
informal: Fibonacci divisibility criterion: for m ≠ 2, F_m ∣ F_n iff m ∣ n (converse of Nat.fib_dvd, via Nat.fib_gcd). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq_aux2 (also used in bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq / bld2_pisano_fib_even_eq).

name: lib_isIdempotentElem_of_mul_self_eq_one
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] [Invertible (2 : R)] (a : R) (h : a * a = 1) : IsIdempotentElem (⅟(2 : R) * (1 + a)) ∧ IsIdempotentElem (⅟(2 : R) * (1 - a))
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : Invertible 2] (a : R), a * a = 1 → IsIdempotentElem (⅟2 * (1 + a)) ∧ IsIdempotentElem (⅟2 * (1 - a))
informal: Spectral projections of an involution: if a^2 = 1 and 2 is invertible then (1 + a)/2 and (1 - a)/2 are idempotent, in any ring. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld_involution_trace_rank_aux2 (the case of matrices over a char-0 field; used in bld_involution_rank_add_rank, bld2_involution_iff_rank_add_rank, bld3_rank_involution_defect).

name: lib_matrix_det_add_of_isNilpotent_of_commute
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι R) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (hAB : Commute A B) (hB : IsUnit B.det) : (B + A).det = B.det
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] [IsReduced R] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι R), IsNilpotent A → Commute A B → IsUnit B.det → (B + A).det = B.det
informal: A nilpotent perturbation commuting with an invertible matrix does not change the determinant: det (B + A) = det B, over any reduced commutative ring and any finite index type. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld_nilpotent_commute_det_add_aux1 (which is the case Fin n, ℝ; builds on gen_lin_nilpotent_det_one_add_reduced).

name: lib_matrix_ker_mulVecLin_le_ker_mul
statement: (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (m n p : Type*) [Fintype n] [Fintype p] (M : Matrix m n R) (N : Matrix n p R) : LinearMap.ker N.mulVecLin ≤ LinearMap.ker (M * N).mulVecLin
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommSemiring R] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) (p : Type u_4) [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : Fintype p] (M : Matrix m n R) (N : Matrix n p R), LinearMap.ker N.mulVecLin ≤ LinearMap.ker (M * N).mulVecLin
informal: Null space of a product: ker N ≤ ker (M * N), over any commutative semiring (dual companion of range (M * N) ≤ range M). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_rank_tripotent_defect_aux1 (kernel companion; used inline in rank-defect proofs).

name: p5_psi_ge_succ
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n + 1 ≤ p5_dedekind_psi n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → n + 1 ≤ Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n
informal: Equation (8): psi(n) >= n+1 for n >= 2.

name: lib_matrix_range_mulVecLin_mul_le
statement: (R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] (m n p : Type*) [Fintype n] [Fintype p] (M : Matrix m n R) (N : Matrix n p R) : LinearMap.range (M * N).mulVecLin ≤ LinearMap.range M.mulVecLin
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommSemiring R] (m : Type u_2) (n : Type u_3) (p : Type u_4) [inst_1 : Fintype n] [inst_2 : Fintype p] (M : Matrix m n R) (N : Matrix n p R), LinearMap.range (M * N).mulVecLin ≤ LinearMap.range M.mulVecLin
informal: Column space of a product: range (M * N) ≤ range M, over any commutative semiring and rectangular index types. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_rank_tripotent_defect_aux1 (same step inline in bld3_rank_involution_defect, bld_frobenius_rank_inequality).

name: p5_lemma1
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 2 * n ≤ n.totient + p5_dedekind_psi n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 2 * n ≤ n.totient + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n
informal: Lemma 1 (Atanassov): phi(n)+psi(n) >= 2n for n >= 2.

name: lib_monotone_sub_of_convex_seq
statement: {α : Type*} [AddCommGroup α] [PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] (f : ℕ → α) (h : ∀ k, f (k + 1) + f (k + 1) ≤ f k + f (k + 2)) : Monotone (fun k => f (k + 1) - f k)
type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedAddMonoid α] (f : ℕ → α), (∀ (k : ℕ), f (k + 1) + f (k + 1) ≤ f k + f (k + 2)) → Monotone fun k => f (k + 1) - f k
informal: A convex sequence (second differences nonnegative) in an ordered abelian group has monotone increments f(k+1) - f(k). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes_aux1 (also used with bld2_rank_pow_convex, bld3_nilpotent_rank_pow_le).

name: p5_lemma2
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 2 * n ≤ n.totient + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 2 * n ≤ n.totient + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n
informal: Lemma 2 (Sandor-Atanassov): phi(n)+sigma(n) >= 2n for n >= 2.

name: lib_p3_lucas_cast
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] (n : ℕ) : ((p3_lucas n : ℕ) : R) = 2 * (Nat.fib (n + 1) : R) - (Nat.fib n : R)
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] (n : ℕ), ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) = 2 * ↑(Nat.fib (n + 1)) - ↑(Nat.fib n)
informal: Cast formula for the Lucas numbers L_n = 2 F_(n+1) - F_n (Mathlib2.p3_lucas) in an arbitrary ring: the truncated subtraction in the definition is exact. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.p3_remark3_aux1 (the case R = ℤ; re-derived in bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq, bld2_pell_five_solutions_lucas, bld3_pell_five_neg_four_solutions_lucas).

name: lib_pow_mul_pow_eq_of_mul_eq_central_mul
statement: {M : Type*} [Monoid M] (a b c : M) (hca : Commute c a) (hcb : Commute c b) (h : b * a = c * a * b) (k l : ℕ) : b ^ k * a ^ l = c ^ (k * l) * a ^ l * b ^ k
type: ∀ {M : Type u_1} [inst : Monoid M] (a b c : M), Commute c a → Commute c b → b * a = c * a * b → ∀ (k l : ℕ), b ^ k * a ^ l = c ^ (k * l) * a ^ l * b ^ k
informal: Commutation of powers when the commutator is central (class-2 / Heisenberg relation): if c commutes with a, b and b*a = c*a*b then b^k * a^l = c^(k*l) * a^l * b^k. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_mul_pow_prime_of_card_prime_cube_aux1 (the l = 1 case; see also _aux2 for (a*b)^k = a^k*b^k*c^(k.choose 2)).

name: lib_real_sqrt_sub_sqrt_bounds
statement: (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) : (b - a) / (2 * Real.sqrt b) ≤ Real.sqrt b - Real.sqrt a ∧ Real.sqrt b - Real.sqrt a ≤ (b - a) / (2 * Real.sqrt a)
informal: Two-sided mean-value bound for the square root: (b-a)/(2√b) ≤ √b - √a ≤ (b-a)/(2√a) for 0 < a ≤ b (the telescoping estimate behind ∑ 1/√k ~ 2√n). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.an2_sum_inv_sqrt_bounds_aux1 (the case b = a + 1; used in bld_sum_inv_sqrt_div_sqrt_tendsto).

name: lib_sylow_card_eq_pow_and_index_eq
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type*) [Group G] (n m : ℕ) (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ n * m) (hm : ¬ p ∣ m) (P : Sylow p G) : Nat.card P = p ^ n ∧ (P : Subgroup G).index = m
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] (n m : ℕ), Nat.card G = p ^ n * m → ¬p ∣ m → ∀ (P : Sylow p G), Nat.card ↥↑P = p ^ n ∧ (↑P).index = m
informal: Order and index of a Sylow p-subgroup: if |G| = p^n * m with p ∤ m then |P| = p^n and [G : P] = m. Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.bld3_card_sylow_of_card_prime_mul_prime_aux1 (the case |G| = r*s; same computation inline in alg_isCyclic_of_card_eq_prime_mul_prime, bld_center_eq_bot_of_card_prime_mul_prime).

name: p5_thm1
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 3 * n ^ 3 + 3 * n ^ 2 + 9 * n + 1 ≤ n.totient ^ 3 + p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 3 + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 3
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 3 * n ^ 3 + 3 * n ^ 2 + 9 * n + 1 ≤ n.totient ^ 3 + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 3 + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 3
informal: Theorem 1: phi^3+psi^3+sigma^3 >= 3n^3+3n^2+9n+1 for n >= 2.

name: lib_fib_add_modEq_mul_fib_succ
statement: (N m i : ℕ) (h : N ∣ Nat.fib m) : Nat.fib (i + m) ≡ Nat.fib i * Nat.fib (m + 1) [MOD N]
type: ∀ (N m i : ℕ), N ∣ Nat.fib m → Nat.fib (i + m) ≡ Nat.fib i * Nat.fib (m + 1) [MOD N]
informal: Fibonacci shift congruence: if N ∣ F_m then F_(i+m) ≡ F_i * F_(m+1) (mod N), i.e. shifting by a zero of the sequence mod N multiplies by F_(m+1). Promoted and generalised from Mathlib2.p3_cor1_aux3 (the case N = F_(n+1); re-derived in p3_cor1_aux4, p3_aux_period_aux4, bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul).

name: p5_thm2
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 3 * n ^ 4 + 4 * n ^ 3 + 18 * n ^ 2 + 4 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 4 + p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 4 + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 4
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 3 * n ^ 4 + 4 * n ^ 3 + 18 * n ^ 2 + 4 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 4 + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 4 + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 4
informal: Theorem 2: phi^4+psi^4+sigma^4 >= 3n^4+4n^3+18n^2+4n+3 for n >= 2.

name: bld4_pell_five_one_iff
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 = 5 * y ^ 2 + 1 ↔ ∃ n, 2 * y = Nat.fib (6 * n) ∧ 2 * x = Mathlib2.p3_lucas (6 * n)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pell_five_one_solutions and Mathlib2.bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq: the forward direction is exactly bld3_pell_five_one_solutions. Conversely bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq at index 6n gives L^2 − 5F^2 = 4 over ℤ; substituting L = 2x, F = 2y and cancelling 4 gives x^2 = 5y^2 + 1.

name: bld4_tripotent_trace_eq_rank_sub_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A * A = A) : A.trace = ((A * A + A).rank : K) - ((A * A - A).rank : K)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A * A = A → A.trace = ↑(A * A + A).rank - ↑(A * A - A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_smul: P = (1/2)(A^2 + A) and Q = (1/2)(A^2 − A) are idempotent when A^3 = A, and A = P − Q. So tr A = tr P − tr Q = rank P − rank Q by gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field, and lib_matrix_rank_smul removes the scalar 1/2 from the ranks.

name: p5_thm3
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 3 * n ^ 4 + 4 * n ^ 3 + 2 * n ^ 2 + 4 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 * p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 + n.totient ^ 2 * ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 2 + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 2 * p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 3 * n ^ 4 + 4 * n ^ 3 + 2 * n ^ 2 + 4 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 + n.totient ^ 2 * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 2 + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 2 * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2
informal: Theorem 3: phi^2 psi^2 + phi^2 sigma^2 + sigma^2 psi^2 >= 3n^4+4n^3+2n^2+4n+3 for n >= 2.

name: bld4_pisano_mul_of_coprime
statement: (m n : ℕ) (h : Nat.Coprime m n) : p3_pisano (m * n) = Nat.lcm (p3_pisano m) (p3_pisano n)
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m.Coprime n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (m * n) = (Mathlib2.p3_pisano m).lcm (Mathlib2.p3_pisano n)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_pos_and_period and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd (m ∣ mn, n ∣ mn) gives lcm ∣ π(mn). Conversely pos_and_period makes L = lcm(π m, π n) a period mod m and mod n (iterate the period), hence mod mn by Nat.modEq_and_modEq_iff_modEq_mul for coprime m n, and dvd_of_period gives π(mn) ∣ L. Case m = 0 forces n = 1 (both sides 0).

name: bld4_pell_five_neg_four_y_sum_two_squares
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pell_five_neg_four_solutions_lucas: the classification gives y = F_{2n+1}, and Nat.fib_two_mul_add_one gives F_{2n+1} = F_{n+1}^2 + F_n^2, so a = F_{n+1}, b = F_n.

name: p5_thm4
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 6 * n ^ 3 + 6 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n + 2 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 * (p5_dedekind_psi n + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) + p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 * (n.totient + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 2 * (n.totient + p5_dedekind_psi n)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 6 * n ^ 3 + 6 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n + 2 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 * (Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 * (n.totient + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 2 * (n.totient + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n)
informal: Theorem 4: phi^2(psi+sigma)+psi^2(phi+sigma)+sigma^2(phi+psi) >= 6n^3+6n^2+2n+2 for n >= 2.

name: bld4_tripotent_trace_eq_rank_idempotent
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A * A = A) (ht : A.trace = (A.rank : K)) : A * A = A
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A * A * A = A → A.trace = ↑A.rank → A * A = A
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_tripotent_rank_split, Mathlib2.gen_lin_idempotent_trace_eq_rank_field, Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_smul and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff: as for the trace formula, tr A = rank(A^2 + A) − rank(A^2 − A) (idempotents (A^2 ± A)/2, trace = rank, rank_smul), while bld2_tripotent_rank_split gives rank A = rank(A^2 + A) + rank(A^2 − A). The hypothesis then forces 2·rank(A^2 − A) = 0 in K, so rank(A^2 − A) = 0 by CharZero and A^2 − A = 0 by lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff.

name: bld4_pell_five_neg_four_prime_mul_y_not_rat_sum_sq
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pell_five_neg_four_solutions_lucas, Mathlib2.nt2_fib_odd_index_no_prime_factor_three_mod_four and Mathlib2.bld2_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_mul_coprime: the Pell classification gives y = F_{2n+1}; nt2_fib_odd_index_no_prime_factor_three_mod_four gives ¬ p ∣ y; then bld2_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_prime_mul_coprime with m = y is the claim.

name: p5_thm5
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 6 * n ^ 4 + 8 * n ^ 3 + 12 * n ^ 2 + 8 * n ≤ n.totient ^ 3 * (p5_dedekind_psi n + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) + p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 3 * (n.totient + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 3 * (n.totient + p5_dedekind_psi n) + 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 6 * n ^ 4 + 8 * n ^ 3 + 12 * n ^ 2 + 8 * n ≤ n.totient ^ 3 * (Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 3 * (n.totient + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 3 * (n.totient + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n) + 2
informal: Theorem 5: phi^3(psi+sigma)+psi^3(phi+sigma)+sigma^3(phi+psi) >= 6n^4+8n^3+12n^2+8n-2 for n >= 2 (the -2 moved to the other side to avoid natural subtraction).

name: bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_pred_of_isSquare_five
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hp5 : p ≠ 5) (h : IsSquare (5 : ZMod p)) : p3_pisano p ∣ p - 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → p ≠ 5 → IsSquare 5 → Mathlib2.p3_pisano p ∣ p - 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_fib_prime, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: by Euler's criterion (ZMod.euler_criterion) 5^(p/2) = 1 in ZMod p, so p3_aux_fib_prime gives F_p ≡ 1 and 2F_{p+1} − F_p ≡ 1, hence F_{p+1} ≡ 1 and F_{p−1} = F_{p+1} − F_p ≡ 0 mod p. lib_fib_period_iff (with m = p − 1) turns this into p − 1 being a period, and bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period concludes.

name: bld4_nilpotent_corank_one_rank_pow
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (hr : A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card ι) : (A ^ k).rank = Fintype.card ι - k
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι → ∀ k ≤ Fintype.card ι, (A ^ k).rank = Fintype.card ι - k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_nilpotent_rank_pow_le and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_mul_rank_le_add_rank_pow: the upper bound rank A^k ≤ n − k is bld3_nilpotent_rank_pow_le. For the lower bound, lib_matrix_mul_rank_le_add_rank_pow gives k(n − 1) ≤ (k − 1)n + rank A^k, i.e. rank A^k ≥ n − k (k = 0 separately: rank 1 = n). This is the single-Jordan-block case.

name: p5_cited_squares
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 3 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 + p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 3 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n + 3 ≤ n.totient ^ 2 + Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n ^ 2 + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ 2
informal: Cited result (Dimitrov 2023): phi^2+psi^2+sigma^2 >= 3n^2+2n+3 for n >= 2.

name: p5_cited_products
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 3 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n ≤ n.totient * p5_dedekind_psi n + n.totient * ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n * p5_dedekind_psi n + 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 3 * n ^ 2 + 2 * n ≤ n.totient * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n + n.totient * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n + 1
informal: Cited result (Dimitrov 2023): phi psi + phi sigma + sigma psi >= 3n^2+2n-1 for n >= 2 (the -1 moved across).

name: bld4_sqrt_two_rec_defect_tsum_lower
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : Real.pi ^ 2 / 3 - Real.pi ^ 4 / 180 ≤ ∑' n : ℕ, (2 - a n)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable, Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form and Mathlib2.ana_sin_ge_cubic_of_nonneg: termwise 2 − a_n ≥ π^2/4^(n+1) − π^4/(192·16^n) (closed form + cubic sine bound, as in the pointwise estimate). The right side is a difference of geometric series with sum π^2/3 − π^4/180; bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable supplies summability of the left side so tsum comparison (hasSum_le / tsum_le_tsum) applies. Improves the bound 8/3 of bld3_sqrt_two_rec_defect_tsum_bounds.

name: bld4_sqrt_two_rec_defect_lower
informal: Uses Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_closed_form and Mathlib2.ana_sin_ge_cubic_of_nonneg: the closed form gives 2 − a_n = 2 − 2cos(2θ) = 4 sin^2 θ with θ = π/2^(n+2). ana_sin_ge_cubic_of_nonneg gives sin θ ≥ θ − θ^3/6 ≥ 0, so 4 sin^2 θ ≥ 4θ^2(1 − θ^2/6)^2 ≥ 4θ^2 − 4θ^4/3, which is the stated bound (matching upper bound: bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate).

name: bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_two_mul_succ_of_not_isSquare_five
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (h : ¬ IsSquare (5 : ZMod p)) : p3_pisano p ∣ 2 * (p + 1)
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], ¬IsSquare 5 → Mathlib2.p3_pisano p ∣ 2 * (p + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_fib_prime, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: p ≠ 2, 5 since 5 is a square there; Euler's criterion gives 5^(p/2) = −1, so p3_aux_fib_prime yields F_p ≡ −1, F_{p+1} ≡ 0, hence F_{p+2} ≡ −1 mod p. By Nat.fib_add, F_{2p+2} ≡ 0 and F_{2p+3} ≡ F_{p+2}^2 ≡ 1, so lib_fib_period_iff makes 2(p+1) a period and bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period concludes.

name: bld4_rat_sum_two_squares_iff_nat
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_of_odd_padicValNat: (⇐) is a cast. (⇒) by Mathlib's Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_iff it suffices that padicValNat q n is even for every prime q ≡ 3 mod 4; if it were odd, bld3_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_of_odd_padicValNat would contradict the rational representation.

name: bld4_rat_sq_add_sq_eq_mul_sq_trivial
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp3 : p % 4 = 3) (hodd : Odd (padicValNat p n)) (x y z : ℚ) (h : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = (n : ℚ) * z ^ 2) : x = 0 ∧ y = 0 ∧ z = 0
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 3 → Odd (padicValNat p n) → ∀ (x y z : ℚ), x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = ↑n * z ^ 2 → x = 0 ∧ y = 0 ∧ z = 0
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_of_odd_padicValNat: if z ≠ 0 then (x/z)^2 + (y/z)^2 = n, contradicting bld3_rat_sq_add_sq_ne_of_odd_padicValNat; so z = 0, and then x^2 + y^2 = 0 in ℚ forces x = y = 0.

name: bld4_permMatrix_involution_rank_fixed_points
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (hσ : σ * σ = 1) : 2 * (1 + σ.permMatrix K).rank = Fintype.card ι + (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : ι => σ i = i)).card
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (σ : Equiv.Perm ι), σ * σ = 1 → 2 * (1 + Equiv.Perm.permMatrix K σ).rank = Fintype.card ι + {i | σ i = i}.card
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_involution_trace_rank: the permutation matrix P of an involution satisfies P * P = 1 (Matrix.permMatrix_mul), so bld_involution_trace_rank gives tr P + n = 2 rank(1 + P) in K; tr P is the number of fixed points of σ (diagonal entries are 1 or 0), and Nat.cast injectivity in characteristic 0 gives the identity in ℕ.

name: bld4_prime_dvd_fib_pred_mul_fib_mul_fib_succ
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : p ∣ Nat.fib (p - 1) * Nat.fib p * Nat.fib (p + 1)
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ∣ Nat.fib (p - 1) * Nat.fib p * Nat.fib (p + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.p3_aux_fib_prime and Mathlib2.an_cassini_int: p = 2 and p = 5 by computation (F_3 = 2, F_5 = 5). Otherwise p3_aux_fib_prime gives F_p ≡ 5^(p/2), so F_p^2 ≡ 5^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p by Fermat; an_cassini_int at n = p − 1 gives F_{p+1} F_{p−1} = F_p^2 + (−1)^p = F_p^2 − 1 ≡ 0 mod p.

name: bld4_rank_pow_eq_of_card_le
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (j : ℕ) (hj : Fintype.card ι ≤ j) : (A ^ j).rank = (A ^ Fintype.card ι).rank
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (j : ℕ), Fintype.card ι ≤ j → (A ^ j).rank = (A ^ Fintype.card ι).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes and Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex: induct on j showing rank A^(j+1) = rank A^j for j ≥ n. Base case is bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes; for the step, bld2_rank_pow_convex gives 2 r_{j+1} ≤ r_j + r_{j+2} = r_{j+1} + r_{j+2}, so r_{j+2} ≥ r_{j+1}, and r_{j+2} ≤ r_{j+1} by Matrix.rank_mul_le_left.

name: p5_cited_atanassov
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n ^ 3 + n ^ 2 ≤ n.totient * p5_dedekind_psi n * ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n + n + 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → n ^ 3 + n ^ 2 ≤ n.totient * Mathlib2.p5_dedekind_psi n * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n + n + 1
informal: Cited result (Atanassov 2013): phi psi sigma >= n^3+n^2-n-1 for n >= 2 (subtractions moved across).

name: bld4_fitting_range_inter_ker_pow_card
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (v : ι → K) (h : (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec ((A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec v) = 0) : (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec v = 0
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (v : ι → K), (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec ((A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec v) = 0 → (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVec v = 0
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_rank_pow_card_stabilizes and Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex: with N = A^n, stabilisation (base case from rank_pow_card_stabilizes, propagated to exponent 2n by rank_pow_convex) gives rank(N * N) = rank N. By rank–nullity ker N ≤ ker (N * N) have equal finrank, hence are equal, which is the claim (Fitting: range N ∩ ker N = 0).

name: bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul
statement: (n : ℕ) : p3_pisano (p3_lucas n) ∣ 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∣ 4 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.an_cassini_int, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: modulo L_n = F_{n+1} + F_{n−1} one has F_{2n} = F_n L_n ≡ 0 and F_{2n+1} = F_{n+1}^2 + F_n^2 ≡ F_n^2 − F_{n+1}F_{n−1} = ±1 by an_cassini_int. Hence F_{4n} ≡ 0 and F_{4n+1} ≡ F_{2n+1}^2 ≡ 1, so lib_fib_period_iff makes 4n a period mod L_n and bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period concludes (n = 0 trivial).

name: bld4_pow_prime_monoidHom_center_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : ∃ φ : G →* Subgroup.center G, ∀ g : G, ((φ g : Subgroup.center G) : G) = g ^ p
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → p ≠ 2 → ∃ φ, ∀ (g : G), ↑(φ g) = g ^ p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pow_prime_mem_center_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld3_mul_pow_prime_of_card_prime_cube: define φ g = ⟨g^p, _⟩ using pow_prime_mem_center for membership; map_mul is exactly (ab)^p = a^p b^p from mul_pow_prime (p odd), map_one is one_pow.

name: bld4_card_pow_prime_eq_one_ge_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : p ^ 2 ≤ Nat.card {g : G // g ^ p = 1}
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → p ≠ 2 → p ^ 2 ≤ Nat.card { g // g ^ p = 1 }
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pow_prime_mem_center_of_card_prime_cube, Mathlib2.bld3_mul_pow_prime_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: the p-th power map is a homomorphism φ : G →* center G (first two theorems); |ker φ| · |range φ| = p^3 and |range φ| ≤ |center G| = p by bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube, so |ker φ| ≥ p^2, and ker φ is the set {g | g^p = 1}.

name: bld4_pisano_ten
statement: : p3_pisano 10 = 60
type: Mathlib2.p3_pisano 10 = 60
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd: lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period + lib_fib_period_iff reduce 'π(m) ∣ N' to the decidable check F_N ≡ 0, F_{N+1} ≡ 1 mod m; this gives π(10) ∣ 60, and identifies π(2) = 3 and π(5) = 20 (20 works, the divisors 4 and 10 fail). bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd then gives 3 ∣ π(10) and 20 ∣ π(10), so 60 ∣ π(10).

name: bld4_hardy_harmonic_means_tsum_le
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum: apply it to a k = 1/(k+1); the hypothesis is summability of 1/(k+1)^2 and the right side is 4 · ∑' 1/(k+1)^2 = 4 · π^2/6 by Mathlib's Basel sum hasSum_zeta_two (reindexed by k ↦ k + 1).

name: bld4_mantel_equality_complete_bipartite
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) : ∃ s : Finset V, 2 * s.card = Fintype.card V ∧ ∀ x y : V, G.Adj x y ↔ (x ∈ s ↔ y ∉ s)
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ∃ s, 2 * s.card = Fintype.card V ∧ ∀ (x y : V), G.Adj x y ↔ (x ∈ s ↔ y ∉ s)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_mantel_equality_regular and Mathlib2.bld3_mantel_equality_same_neighbors: if V is empty take s = ∅; otherwise fix v and let s = G.neighborFinset v, of size n/2 by bld2_mantel_equality_regular. Two vertices of s are non-adjacent (triangle-free); a vertex y ∉ s is non-adjacent to v so by bld3_mantel_equality_same_neighbors it has the same neighbours as v, i.e. it is adjacent exactly to the vertices of s; this gives Adj x y ↔ (x ∈ s ↔ y ∉ s) in all four cases.

name: bld4_compact_mutual_isometric_embeddings_isometryEquiv
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X) (hf : Isometry f) (hg : Isometry g) : Nonempty (X ≃ᵢ Y)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (g : Y → X), Isometry f → Isometry g → Nonempty (X ≃ᵢ Y)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_compact_mutual_expanding_isometry: isometries are expanding (dist equality), so the cited theorem gives that f is a surjective isometry; an isometry is injective, so Equiv.ofBijective f packaged with hf is the IsometryEquiv.

name: bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : Isometry f) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) x < ε
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), Isometry f → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∀ (x : X), dist (f^[n] x) x < ε
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_compactSpace_exists_lt_and_dist_lt: take a finite ε/3-net t of X and apply the lemma in the compact space Y = (t → X) (sup metric) to u k = fun i => f^[k] i, getting m < n' with dist (f^[m] i) (f^[n'] i) < ε/3 for all i ∈ t. With n = n' − m, the isometry property gives dist i (f^[n] i) < ε/3 on the net, and the triangle inequality (f^[n] is an isometry) gives dist (f^[n] x) x < ε for all x.

name: bld4_commuting_idempotents_rank_add
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (B : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A = A) (hB : B * B = B) (hAB : A * B = B * A) : (A + B).rank + (A * B).rank = A.rank + B.rank
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A → B * B = B → A * B = B * A → (A + B).rank + (A * B).rank = A.rank + B.rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_commuting_idempotents_rank_join: A + B = (A + B − AB)(1 + AB), and 1 + AB is invertible with inverse 1 − (1/2)AB because (AB)^2 = AB (char ≠ 2); multiplying by a unit preserves rank, so rank(A + B) = rank(A + B − AB), and the cited join formula finishes.

name: bld4_edelstein_surjective_subsingleton
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) (hs : Function.Surjective f) : Subsingleton X
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → Function.Surjective f → Subsingleton X
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry: f is non-expanding (≤ from <, equality case x = y) and surjective, hence an isometry by the cited theorem; for x ≠ y this gives dist (f x) (f y) = dist x y, contradicting the strict inequality.

name: bld4_edelstein_diam_range_iterate_tendsto_zero
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : ∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Metric.diam (Set.range (f^[n]))) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), (∀ (x y : X), x ≠ y → dist (f x) (f y) < dist x y) → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Metric.diam (Set.range f^[n])) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point and Mathlib2.bld3_edelstein_iterates_tendsto_uniformly: if X is empty the diameters are 0. Otherwise top_edelstein_unique_fixed_point gives a fixed point p, and bld3_edelstein_iterates_tendsto_uniformly gives N with dist (f^[n] x) p < ε/2 for all n ≥ N and x, so diam (range f^[n]) ≤ ε by Metric.diam_le_of_forall_dist_le.

name: bld4_carleman_finite_three
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (ha : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ a i) (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ 3 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ a i) → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), a i) ^ (1 / (↑k + 1)) ≤ 3 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.an2_amgm_range_pow and Mathlib2.an2_succ_pow_lt_three_mul_pow (Carleman's inequality with constant 3 > e): with weights c_i = (i+2)^(i+1)/(i+1)^i (0-indexed) one has ∏_{i≤k} c_i = (k+2)^(k+1), so by an2_amgm_range_pow applied to a_i c_i, (∏_{i≤k} a_i)^(1/(k+1)) ≤ (∑_{i≤k} a_i c_i)/((k+1)(k+2)). Summing over k < n, swapping sums and telescoping ∑_{k≥i} 1/((k+1)(k+2)) ≤ 1/(i+1) gives ≤ ∑ a_i c_i/(i+1) = ∑ a_i ((i+2)/(i+1))^(i+1) ≤ 3 ∑ a_i by an2_succ_pow_lt_three_mul_pow.

name: bld4_card_orderOf_eq_prime_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card {g : G // orderOf g = p} = q * (p - 1)
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Nat.Prime q → p < q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card { g // orderOf g = p } = q * (p - 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_card_sylow_of_card_prime_mul_prime: there are exactly q Sylow p-subgroups, each of order p; two distinct ones meet trivially, and every element of order p generates one. So the elements of order p are the disjoint union over the q Sylow p-subgroups of their p − 1 non-identity elements.

name: poly_fermat_catalan_2_3_7
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b c : Polynomial k) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hab : IsCoprime a b) (hbc : IsCoprime b c) (hca : IsCoprime c a) (heq : a ^ 2 + b ^ 3 = c ^ 7) : a.natDegree = 0 ∧ b.natDegree = 0 ∧ c.natDegree = 0
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b c : Polynomial k), a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → IsCoprime a b → IsCoprime b c → IsCoprime c a → a ^ 2 + b ^ 3 = c ^ 7 → a.natDegree = 0 ∧ b.natDegree = 0 ∧ c.natDegree = 0
informal: In characteristic 0, a^2 + b^3 = c^7 has no non-constant pairwise coprime polynomial solutions (1/2+1/3+1/7 < 1) — Uses Mathlib2.ms_fermat_catalan with (p,q,r)=(2,3,7), u=v=1, w=-1; ringChar k = 0 divides none of 2,3,7; rewrite heq as C 1 * a^2 + C 1 * b^3 + C (-1) * c^7 = 0.

name: poly_fermat_quartic_4_4_2
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b c : Polynomial k) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hab : IsCoprime a b) (hbc : IsCoprime b c) (hca : IsCoprime c a) (heq : a ^ 4 + b ^ 4 = c ^ 2) : a.natDegree = 0 ∧ b.natDegree = 0 ∧ c.natDegree = 0
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b c : Polynomial k), a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → IsCoprime a b → IsCoprime b c → IsCoprime c a → a ^ 4 + b ^ 4 = c ^ 2 → a.natDegree = 0 ∧ b.natDegree = 0 ∧ c.natDegree = 0
informal: Polynomial analogue of Fermat's quartic theorem: a^4 + b^4 = c^2 forces coprime nonzero a, b, c to be constant in char 0 (borderline case 1/4+1/4+1/2 = 1) — Uses Mathlib2.ms_fermat_catalan with (p,q,r)=(4,4,2), u=v=1, w=-1; the only work is the ringChar and the 1/p+1/q+1/r ≤ 1 side conditions.

name: poly_x2_x_1_dvd_trinomial
statement: (k m : ℕ) : (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.X + 1 : Polynomial ℤ) ∣ Polynomial.X ^ (3 * k + 2) + Polynomial.X ^ (3 * m + 1) + 1
type: ∀ (k m : ℕ), Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.X + 1 ∣ Polynomial.X ^ (3 * k + 2) + Polynomial.X ^ (3 * m + 1) + 1
informal: X^2+X+1 divides X^(3k+2) + X^(3m+1) + 1 over ℤ — X^3 ≡ 1 mod X^2+X+1 (since X^3 - 1 = (X-1)(X^2+X+1)), so the trinomial is ≡ X^2 + X + 1 ≡ 0.

name: poly_int_odd_at_zero_one_no_root
statement: (p : Polynomial ℤ) (h0 : Odd (Polynomial.eval 0 p)) (h1 : Odd (Polynomial.eval 1 p)) (n : ℤ) : Polynomial.eval n p ≠ 0
type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℤ), Odd (Polynomial.eval 0 p) → Odd (Polynomial.eval 1 p) → ∀ (n : ℤ), Polynomial.eval n p ≠ 0
informal: An integer polynomial with p(0) and p(1) odd has no integer root — n - 0 ∣ p(n) - p(0) and n - 1 ∣ p(n) - p(1) (Polynomial.sub_dvd_eval_sub); if p(n) = 0 then both n and n-1 divide odd numbers, but one of them is even.

name: poly_int_three_ones_no_root
statement: (p : Polynomial ℤ) (a b c : ℤ) (hab : a ≠ b) (hbc : b ≠ c) (hac : a ≠ c) (ha : Polynomial.eval a p = 1) (hb : Polynomial.eval b p = 1) (hc : Polynomial.eval c p = 1) (r : ℤ) : Polynomial.eval r p ≠ 0
type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℤ) (a b c : ℤ), a ≠ b → b ≠ c → a ≠ c → Polynomial.eval a p = 1 → Polynomial.eval b p = 1 → Polynomial.eval c p = 1 → ∀ (r : ℤ), Polynomial.eval r p ≠ 0
informal: An integer polynomial taking the value 1 at three distinct integers has no integer root — if p(r) = 0 then r-a, r-b, r-c each divide p(r) - 1 = -1 (sub_dvd_eval_sub), so they are three distinct elements of {1,-1}, impossible.

name: poly_real_nonneg_coeff_no_pos_root
statement: (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hp : p ≠ 0) (h : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ p.coeff i) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) : Polynomial.eval x p ≠ 0
type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ), p ≠ 0 → (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ p.coeff i) → ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 < x → Polynomial.eval x p ≠ 0
informal: A nonzero real polynomial with nonnegative coefficients has no positive root (trivial case of Descartes' rule) — eval x p = Σ coeff i * x^i is a sum of nonnegative terms, at least one (the leading one) strictly positive.

name: poly_sophie_germain_not_irreducible
statement: (a : ℤ) : ¬ Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 + Polynomial.C (4 * a ^ 4) : Polynomial ℤ)
type: ∀ (a : ℤ), ¬Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 + Polynomial.C (4 * a ^ 4))
informal: Sophie Germain: X^4 + 4a^4 is reducible over ℤ for every integer a — X^4 + 4a^4 = (X^2 + 2aX + 2a^2)(X^2 - 2aX + 2a^2), both monic of degree 2 hence non-units.

name: poly_abc_radical_bound_of_coprime
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b : Polynomial k) (hab : IsCoprime a b) (ha : 0 < a.natDegree) : max a.natDegree b.natDegree + 1 ≤ (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (a * b * (a + b))).natDegree
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (a b : Polynomial k), IsCoprime a b → 0 < a.natDegree → max a.natDegree b.natDegree + 1 ≤ (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (a * b * (a + b))).natDegree
informal: ABC for polynomials in two-variable form: coprime a, b in char 0 with a non-constant satisfy max(deg a, deg b) + 1 ≤ deg rad(ab(a+b)) — b ≠ 0 and a+b ≠ 0 follow from coprimality and deg a > 0; Uses Mathlib2.ms_mason_stothers_v2 with c = -(a+b) (derivative a ≠ 0 in char 0 kills the first alternative), and radical(a*b*(-(a+b))) = radical(a*b*(a+b)) by associatedness.

name: poly_catalan_pow_add_one
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (m n : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (g h : Polynomial k) (heq : g ^ m + 1 = h ^ n) : g.natDegree = 0 ∧ h.natDegree = 0
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (m n : ℕ), 2 ≤ m → 2 ≤ n → ∀ (g h : Polynomial k), g ^ m + 1 = h ^ n → g.natDegree = 0 ∧ h.natDegree = 0
informal: Catalan for polynomials: in char 0 two perfect powers g^m, h^n (m,n ≥ 2) differing by 1 are constants — Uses Mathlib2.ms_mason_stothers_v2 with a = g^m, b = 1, c = -h^n (pairwise coprime since g^m and h^n differ by a unit): if g is non-constant, D = m·deg g = n·deg h < deg rad(g^m h^n) ≤ deg g + deg h = D/m + D/n ≤ D, contradiction; g = 0 or g constant handled separately.

name: poly_chebyshev_T_abs_le_one
statement: (n : ℤ) (x : ℝ) (hx : |x| ≤ 1) : |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ n)| ≤ 1
type: ∀ (n : ℤ) (x : ℝ), |x| ≤ 1 → |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ n)| ≤ 1
informal: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind are bounded by 1 on [-1,1] — write x = cos θ with θ = arccos x, then T_n(cos θ) = cos(nθ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T_real_cos) and |cos| ≤ 1.

name: poly_x3_x_1_irreducible_rat
statement: : Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 3 + Polynomial.X + 1 : Polynomial ℚ)
type: Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 3 + Polynomial.X + 1)
informal: X^3 + X + 1 is irreducible over ℚ — a cubic is irreducible iff it has no root; by the rational root theorem a rational root would be ±1, and neither is a root.

name: poly_flt_noncoprime_proportional
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (a b c : Polynomial k) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (heq : a ^ n + b ^ n = c ^ n) : ∃ (d : Polynomial k) (α β γ : k), a = Polynomial.C α * d ∧ b = Polynomial.C β * d ∧ c = Polynomial.C γ * d
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (a b c : Polynomial k), a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → a ^ n + b ^ n = c ^ n → ∃ d α β γ, a = Polynomial.C α * d ∧ b = Polynomial.C β * d ∧ c = Polynomial.C γ * d
informal: FLT for polynomials without coprimality: in char 0, any nonzero solution of a^n + b^n = c^n (n ≥ 3) is a common polynomial d times a constant solution — take d = gcd(a,b); d^n ∣ c^n gives d ∣ c; the quotients are pairwise coprime and satisfy the same equation, so Uses Mathlib2.ms_flt_poly to make them constants.

name: poly_cubic_real_roots_newton
statement: (a b c : ℝ) (h : (Polynomial.X ^ 3 + Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C c : Polynomial ℝ).roots.card = 3) : 3 * b ≤ a ^ 2
type: ∀ (a b c : ℝ), (Polynomial.X ^ 3 + Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C c).roots.card = 3 → 3 * b ≤ a ^ 2
informal: Newton's inequality for a real cubic with three real roots (with multiplicity): X^3 + aX^2 + bX + c splitting over ℝ forces a^2 ≥ 3b — the polynomial equals (X-r)(X-s)(X-t), so a = -(r+s+t), b = rs+st+tr and a^2 - 3b = ((r-s)^2 + (s-t)^2 + (t-r)^2)/2 ≥ 0.

name: poly_ratfunc_fermat_curve_const
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (f g : RatFunc k) (heq : f ^ n + g ^ n = 1) : (∃ c : k, f = RatFunc.C c) ∧ (∃ d : k, g = RatFunc.C d)
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (f g : RatFunc k), f ^ n + g ^ n = 1 → (∃ c, f = RatFunc.C c) ∧ ∃ d, g = RatFunc.C d
informal: The Fermat curve x^n + y^n = 1 (n ≥ 3) has no non-constant rational parametrisation in char 0 — write f = a/c, g = b/c with common denominator, cancel gcd(a,b,c) to get pairwise coprime a^n + b^n = c^n, then Uses Mathlib2.ms_flt_poly to conclude a, b, c constant; the cases a = 0 or b = 0 (g^n = 1 forces g constant) are separate.

name: poly_davenport_sharp_deg_two
statement: : IsLeast {d : ℕ | ∃ f g : Polynomial ℚ, f.natDegree = 2 ∧ g.natDegree = 3 ∧ f ^ 3 ≠ g ^ 2 ∧ (f ^ 3 - g ^ 2).natDegree = d} 2
type: IsLeast {d | ∃ f g, f.natDegree = 2 ∧ g.natDegree = 3 ∧ f ^ 3 ≠ g ^ 2 ∧ (f ^ 3 - g ^ 2).natDegree = d} 2
informal: Davenport's bound is sharp in degree (2,3): the least possible degree of f^3 - g^2 ≠ 0 with deg f = 2, deg g = 3 over ℚ is exactly 2 — membership by f = X^2 + 2, g = X^3 + 3X (f^3 - g^2 = 3X^2 + 8); lower bound Uses Mathlib2.ms_davenport: f.natDegree + 2 = 4 ≤ 2·d.

name: poly_x4_x_1_irreducible_zmod2
statement: : Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 + Polynomial.X + 1 : Polynomial (ZMod 2))
type: Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 + Polynomial.X + 1)
informal: X^4 + X + 1 is irreducible over F_2 — no roots in F_2, and the only irreducible quadratic is X^2+X+1 whose square is X^4+X^2+1 ≠ X^4+X+1.

name: poly_x4_sub_10x2_add_1_irreducible_int
statement: : Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1 : Polynomial ℤ)
type: Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1)
informal: The minimal polynomial X^4 - 10X^2 + 1 of √2+√3 is irreducible over ℤ — no integer roots (±1 fail); a factorisation into monic quadratics (X^2+aX+b)(X^2-aX+d) with bd = 1 forces a(d-b) = 0 and b+d-a^2 = -10, i.e. a^2 = 12 or a^2 = 8 or (a = 0, b + d = -10 with bd = 1), all impossible.

name: poly_x4_sub_10x2_add_1_reducible_zmod
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ¬ Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1 : Polynomial (ZMod p))
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], ¬Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1)
informal: X^4 - 10X^2 + 1 is reducible modulo every prime — one of 2, 3, 6 is a square mod p (Legendre symbol multiplicativity; p = 2, 3 by hand), and X^4-10X^2+1 = (X^2-1)^2 - 8X^2 = (X^2+1)^2 - 12X^2 = (X^2-5)^2 - 24, each a difference of squares when 2, 3, 6 respectively is a square.

name: bld5_permMatrix_involution_rank_one_sub
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (hσ : σ * σ = 1) : 2 * (1 - Equiv.Perm.permMatrix K σ).rank + (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => σ i = i)).card = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (σ : Equiv.Perm ι), σ * σ = 1 → 2 * (1 - Equiv.Perm.permMatrix K σ).rank + {i | σ i = i}.card = Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_permMatrix_involution_rank_fixed_points and Mathlib2.bld_involution_rank_add_rank: P = permMatrix σ satisfies P*P = 1 (permMatrix is multiplicative up to order and σ*σ = 1), so bld_involution_rank_add_rank gives rank(1+P) + rank(1−P) = n, and bld4 gives 2·rank(1+P) = n + fix. Subtracting: 2·rank(1−P) = n − fix, i.e. rank(1 − P) is the number of 2-cycles of σ.

name: poly_trinomial_3k2_not_irreducible_int
statement: (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : ¬ Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ (3 * k + 2) + Polynomial.X + 1 : Polynomial ℤ)
type: ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → ¬Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ (3 * k + 2) + Polynomial.X + 1)
informal: X^n + X + 1 is reducible over ℤ for n ≡ 2 mod 3, n ≥ 5 (e.g. X^5+X+1 = (X^2+X+1)(X^3-X^2+1)) — X^2+X+1 divides it since X^3 ≡ 1; the monic cofactor has degree 3k ≥ 3 so neither factor is a unit.

name: poly_no_consecutive_powerful
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k) (hf : ∀ p : Polynomial k, Irreducible p → p ∣ f → p ^ 2 ∣ f) (hf1 : ∀ p : Polynomial k, Irreducible p → p ∣ f + 1 → p ^ 2 ∣ f + 1) : f.natDegree = 0
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k), (∀ (p : Polynomial k), Irreducible p → p ∣ f → p ^ 2 ∣ f) → (∀ (p : Polynomial k), Irreducible p → p ∣ f + 1 → p ^ 2 ∣ f + 1) → f.natDegree = 0
informal: In char 0 there are no non-constant 'consecutive powerful polynomials': if every irreducible factor of f and of f+1 occurs at least squared then f is constant — a powerful polynomial g satisfies 2·deg rad g ≤ deg g; Uses Mathlib2.ms_mason_stothers_v2 with (f, 1, -(f+1)): deg f < deg rad(f(f+1)) = deg rad f + deg rad(f+1) ≤ deg f/2 + deg f/2, contradiction.

name: bld5_gcd_fib_lucas_dvd_two
statement: (n : ℕ) : Nat.gcd (Nat.fib n) (p3_lucas n) ∣ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), (Nat.fib n).gcd (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∣ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq: with g = gcd(F_n, L_n), g² divides L_n² − 5F_n² = 4·(−1)^n (the bld2 identity, in ℤ), so g² ∣ 4 and hence g ∣ 2 (g ≤ 2 by size, then case check, or Nat.pow_dvd_pow_iff with 4 = 2²).

name: bld5_sqrt_two_rec_partial_sum_lower
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : 2 * (n : ℝ) - Real.pi ^ 2 / 3 ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, a i
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 * ↑n - Real.pi ^ 2 / 3 ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, a i
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable, Mathlib2.bld3_sqrt_two_rec_defect_tsum_bounds and Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two: ∑_{i<n} (2 − a_i) ≤ ∑' (2 − a_i) by sum_le_tsum (terms non-negative by ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two, summable by bld2), and the series is ≤ π²/3 by bld3; rearrange using Finset.sum_sub_distrib and Finset.sum_const.

name: bld5_pell_five_neg_four_pisano_mod_eight
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 + 4 = 5 * y ^ 2 → 5 ≤ y → Mathlib2.p3_pisano y % 8 = 4
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pell_five_neg_four_solutions_lucas and Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq: the Pell classification gives y = F_{2n+1}; y ≥ 5 forces 2n+1 ≥ 5 (F_1 = 1, F_3 = 2), so bld2_pisano_fib_odd_eq gives pisano y = 4(2n+1) = 8n + 4.

name: bld5_carleman_sqrt_two_rec_defect
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (2 - a i)) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ Real.pi ^ 2
type: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ), a 0 = 0 → (∀ (n : ℕ), a (n + 1) = √(2 + a n)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (2 - a i)) ^ (1 / (↑k + 1)) ≤ Real.pi ^ 2
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_carleman_finite_three, Mathlib2.bld3_sqrt_two_rec_defect_tsum_bounds, Mathlib2.bld2_sqrt_two_rec_defect_summable and Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two: the defects 2 − a_i are non-negative (ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two), so Carleman's inequality with constant 3 (bld4) bounds the sum of geometric means by 3·∑_{k<n}(2 − a_k) ≤ 3·∑'(2 − a_k) (sum_le_tsum with bld2 summability) ≤ 3·π²/3 = π² (bld3).

name: bld5_pisano_prime_le_four_mul
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : p3_pisano p ≤ 4 * p
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Mathlib2.p3_pisano p ≤ 4 * p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_pred_of_isSquare_five, Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_two_mul_succ_of_not_isSquare_five, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: for p = 2 and p = 5 check F_3 ≡ 0, F_4 ≡ 1 mod 2 and F_20 ≡ 0, F_21 ≡ 1 mod 5, so (lib_fib_period_iff, bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period) pisano ∣ 3 resp. 20 = 4·5 (equality case). Otherwise split on IsSquare (5 : ZMod p): the first bld4 theorem gives pisano ∣ p − 1, the second pisano ∣ 2(p+1) ≤ 4p; conclude with Nat.le_of_dvd.

name: bld5_hardy_sqrt_two_rec_defect_means
statement: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (h0 : a 0 = 0) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = Real.sqrt (2 + a n)) : ∑' k : ℕ, ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (2 - a i)) / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * Real.pi ^ 4 / 15
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum, Mathlib2.bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate and Mathlib2.ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two: by ana_sqrt_two_rec_lt_two and bld_sqrt_two_rec_rate, 0 ≤ 2 − a_k ≤ π²/4^(k+1), so (2 − a_k)² ≤ π⁴/16^(k+1), which is summable (geometric) with sum π⁴/15 (tsum_geometric_of_lt_one, tsum_le_tsum). Hardy's inequality bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum applied to the defect sequence bounds the left side by 4·∑'(2 − a_k)² ≤ 4π⁴/15.

name: poly_abc_distinct_roots_complex
statement: (a b : Polynomial ℂ) (hab : IsCoprime a b) (ha : 0 < a.natDegree) : a.natDegree + 1 ≤ (a * b * (a + b)).roots.toFinset.card
type: ∀ (a b : Polynomial ℂ), IsCoprime a b → 0 < a.natDegree → a.natDegree + 1 ≤ (a * b * (a + b)).roots.toFinset.card
informal: Stothers' form over ℂ: for coprime a, b with a non-constant, the product ab(a+b) has at least deg a + 1 distinct complex roots — Uses Mathlib2.ms_mason_stothers_v2 (c = -(a+b)) to get deg a < deg rad(ab(a+b)), then show over an algebraically closed field that natDegree (radical p) equals the number of distinct roots of p (radical is the product of the distinct monic linear factors).

name: bld5_nonexpanding_denseRange_compact_recurrence
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hd : DenseRange f) (hf : ∀ x y : X, dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : Isometry f ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) x < ε
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), DenseRange f → (∀ (x y : X), dist (f x) (f y) ≤ dist x y) → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → Isometry f ∧ ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∀ (x : X), dist (f^[n] x) x < ε
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry and Mathlib2.bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence: f is 1-Lipschitz hence continuous, so range f is compact, hence closed, and dense, hence everything (DenseRange.closure_range): f is surjective. bld_surjective_nonexpanding_compact_isometry makes f an isometry and bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence gives the uniform return time.

name: poly_derivative_dvd_self_char_zero
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k) (hf : 0 < f.natDegree) (h : Polynomial.derivative f ∣ f) : ∃ c a : k, f = Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ f.natDegree
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k), 0 < f.natDegree → Polynomial.derivative f ∣ f → ∃ c a, f = Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ f.natDegree
informal: In char 0, a non-constant f with f' ∣ f is c·(X-a)^n — f = f'·q with q linear, q = (X-a)/n by comparing leading coefficients; then n·f = (X-a)f', and induction on n (or comparing root multiplicities at a: f = (X-a)^m g with g(a) ≠ 0 forces m = n) gives the claim.

name: bld5_prime_dvd_fib_succ_of_not_isSquare_five
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (h : ¬ IsSquare (5 : ZMod p)) : p ∣ Nat.fib (p + 1)
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], ¬IsSquare 5 → p ∣ Nat.fib (p + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_prime_dvd_fib_pred_mul_fib_mul_fib_succ, Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_two_mul_succ_of_not_isSquare_five and Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period: p is odd (5 = 1 is a square in ZMod 2). The second bld4 theorem with lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period (i = 0) gives p ∣ F_{2(p+1)}. By the first, p divides F_{p-1}, F_p or F_{p+1}. If p ∣ F_p then Nat.fib_gcd gives p ∣ F_{gcd(p, 2p+2)} = F_1 = 1; if p ∣ F_{p-1} then p ∣ F_{gcd(p-1, 2p+2)} with gcd(p-1, 2p+2) ∣ 4, so p ∣ F_4 = 3, p = 3, but then F_{p-1} = F_2 = 1. Both impossible, so p ∣ F_{p+1}.

name: bld5_prime_dvd_pred_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : p ∣ q - 1
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Nat.Prime q → p < q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → p ∣ q - 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_card_sylow_of_card_prime_mul_prime: a non-abelian group of order pq (p < q) has exactly q Sylow p-subgroups by the bld3 theorem; Sylow's third theorem (card_sylow_modEq_one) gives q ≡ 1 mod p, i.e. p ∣ q − 1 ((Nat.modEq_iff_dvd' hq.one_le).mp after symmetry).

name: bld5_pell_five_four_prime_y
type: ∀ (x y : ℕ), x ^ 2 = 5 * y ^ 2 + 4 → Nat.Prime y → y = 3 ∧ x = 7
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_pell_five_solutions_lucas: it gives n with y = F_{2n}, x = L_{2n}. By Nat.fib_two_mul, y = F_n·L_n (p3_lucas n unfolds to 2F_{n+1} − F_n). For n ≥ 3 both factors exceed 1 (F_n ≥ 2, L_n ≥ 4), contradicting primality; n ≤ 1 gives y ≤ 1; so n = 2, y = F_4 = 3 and x = L_4 = 7.

name: bld5_fitting_isCompl_pow_card
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : IsCompl (LinearMap.range (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVecLin) (LinearMap.ker (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVecLin)
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsCompl (LinearMap.range (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVecLin) (LinearMap.ker (A ^ Fintype.card ι).mulVecLin)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_fitting_range_inter_ker_pow_card: that theorem says exactly that range(A^n) ⊓ ker(A^n) = ⊥ (a vector A^n v killed by A^n is 0), giving Disjoint. For Codisjoint, rank–nullity (LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker) gives finrank range + finrank ker = card ι, so by Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq the sup has full finrank and equals ⊤ (Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq). Mathlib only has the 'eventually' version (LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow); this pins the exponent to card ι.

name: bld5_prime_three_mod_four_dvd_lucas
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p % 4 = 3) : ∃ n : ℕ, p ∣ p3_lucas n
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 3 → ∃ n, p ∣ Mathlib2.p3_lucas n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_pos_and_period and Mathlib2.nt2_fib_odd_index_no_prime_factor_three_mod_four: bld3_pisano_pos_and_period at i = 0 gives some k > 0 with p ∣ F_k; take the least such a (Nat.find). The nt2 theorem (no prime ≡ 3 mod 4 divides an odd-indexed Fibonacci number) forces a even, a = 2n with 0 < n < a. Nat.fib_two_mul gives F_{2n} = F_n·L_n (the factor 2F_{n+1} − F_n is p3_lucas n by definition); p ∤ F_n by minimality, so p ∣ L_n.

name: poly_radical_coprime_derivative_quot
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k) (hf : f ≠ 0) : IsCoprime (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical f) (Polynomial.derivative f / (f / UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical f))
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (f : Polynomial k), f ≠ 0 → IsCoprime (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical f) (Polynomial.derivative f / (f / UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical f))
informal: Snyder's ingredient, sharp form in char 0: the cofactor f' / (f / rad f) is coprime to rad f (so gcd(f, f') is associated to f / rad f) — Uses Mathlib2.ms_divrad_dvd_derivative_v2 to know the division is exact; then for each prime p ∣ f with multiplicity e, f = p^e·g gives f'/(f/rad f) ≡ e·p'·rad(g)·(g/..) mod p, which is nonzero mod p since e ≠ 0 in char 0 and p ∤ p'.

name: bld5_prime_dvd_lucas_four_mul_mod_eight
statement: (p n : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hd : p ∣ p3_lucas (4 * n)) : p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 7
type: ∀ (p n : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ≠ 2 → p ∣ Mathlib2.p3_lucas (4 * n) → p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 7
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_lucas_sq_sub_five_fib_sq and Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast: first the duplication formula L_{2m} = L_m² − 2(−1)^m in ℤ (from lib_p3_lucas_cast, Nat.fib_two_mul, Nat.fib_two_mul_add_one, giving 2L_{2m} = L_m² + 5F_m², then the bld2 identity L_m² − 5F_m² = 4(−1)^m). With m = 2n: L_{4n} = L_{2n}² − 2, so p ∣ L_{4n} makes 2 a square in ZMod p, and ZMod.exists_sq_eq_two_iff (p ≠ 2) gives p ≡ ±1 mod 8.

name: bld5_commuting_idempotents_rank_sub_iff
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : A * A = A) (hB : B * B = B) (hAB : A * B = B * A) : (A - B).rank + B.rank = A.rank ↔ A * B = B
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι K), A * A = A → B * B = B → A * B = B * A → ((A - B).rank + B.rank = A.rank ↔ A * B = B)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_commuting_idempotents_rank_sub, Mathlib2.bld_idempotent_sum_rank and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff: bld3 gives rank(A−B) + 2·rank(AB) = rank A + rank B, so the left side is equivalent to rank(AB) = rank B. AB and B − AB are idempotents (commutativity) with idempotent sum B, so bld_idempotent_sum_rank gives rank B = rank(AB) + rank(B − AB). Hence rank(AB) = rank B ↔ rank(B − AB) = 0 ↔ B − AB = 0 by lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff.

name: bld5_isometries_compact_simultaneous_recurrence
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y) (hf : Isometry f) (hg : Isometry g) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) x < ε) ∧ ∀ y : Y, dist (g^[n] y) y < ε
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y), Isometry f → Isometry g → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ (∀ (x : X), dist (f^[n] x) x < ε) ∧ ∀ (y : Y), dist (g^[n] y) y < ε
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence: apply it to Prod.map f g on the compact metric space X × Y (sup metric; Prod.map of isometries is an isometry, and (Prod.map f g)^[n] = Prod.map f^[n] g^[n]) to get n > 0 with dist((f^[n] x, g^[n] y), (x, y)) < ε for all (x, y); Prod.dist_eq (max) splits it into the two components. If X or Y is empty apply the theorem to the other factor alone.

name: bld5_isometry_compact_id_uniform_limit
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X) (hf : Isometry f) : ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => f^[φ k] x) id Filter.atTop
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (f : X → X), Isometry f → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => f^[φ k] x) id Filter.atTop
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence: first upgrade to arbitrarily large return times: for ε > 0 and N ≥ 1, the bld4 theorem with ε/N gives n > 0 with dist(f^[n] x, x) < ε/N for all x; since f^[n] is an isometry, the triangle inequality gives dist(f^[nN] x, x) ≤ N·sup dist(f^[n] y, y) < ε with nN ≥ N. Then build φ recursively (φ(k+1) > φ(k) with sup-distance < 1/(k+2)) and unfold Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff.

name: poly_chebyshev_T_card_distinct_real_roots
statement: (n : ℕ) : (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ (n : ℤ)).roots.toFinset.card = n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑n).roots.toFinset.card = n
informal: T_n has exactly n distinct real roots — the n points cos((2k+1)π/(2n)), k < n, are distinct (cos is injective on [0,π]) roots since T_n(cos θ) = cos(nθ); and T_n has degree n so at most n roots.

name: bld5_quadratic_annihilated_iff_rank_add_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (a b : K) (hab : a ≠ b) : (A - a • (1 : Matrix ι ι K)) * (A - b • (1 : Matrix ι ι K)) = 0 ↔ (A - a • (1 : Matrix ι ι K)).rank + (A - b • (1 : Matrix ι ι K)).rank = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (a b : K), a ≠ b → ((A - a • 1) * (A - b • 1) = 0 ↔ (A - a • 1).rank + (A - b • 1).rank = Fintype.card ι)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_idempotent_iff_rank_add_rank and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_smul: put P = (b − a)⁻¹ • (A − a•1), so 1 − P = −(b − a)⁻¹ • (A − b•1). A direct computation gives P*P − P = (b − a)⁻² • (A − a•1)(A − b•1), so the left side is equivalent to P*P = P, which by bld2_idempotent_iff_rank_add_rank is rank P + rank(1 − P) = card ι; lib_matrix_rank_smul (non-zero scalars (b−a)⁻¹ and −(b−a)⁻¹) rewrites the ranks as those of A − a•1 and A − b•1. Generalises the idempotent (a,b) = (0,1) and involution (1,−1) criteria to any split quadratic, with no characteristic assumption.

name: bld5_fib_entry_point_pisano_ratio
statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, m ∣ Nat.fib k ↔ a ∣ k) ∧ (p3_pisano m = a ∨ p3_pisano m = 2 * a ∨ p3_pisano m = 4 * a)
type: ∀ (m : ℕ), 0 < m → ∃ a, 0 < a ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), m ∣ Nat.fib k ↔ a ∣ k) ∧ (Mathlib2.p3_pisano m = a ∨ Mathlib2.p3_pisano m = 2 * a ∨ Mathlib2.p3_pisano m = 4 * a)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_pos_and_period, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd and Mathlib2.bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul: bld3_pisano_pos_and_period at i = 0 gives m ∣ F_π with π = pisano m > 0, so a := Nat.find of {k > 0 | m ∣ F_k} exists (rank of apparition). m ∣ F_k ↔ a ∣ k: (⇐) Nat.fib_dvd; (⇒) m ∣ gcd(F_k, F_a) = F_{gcd(k,a)} by Nat.fib_gcd and minimality forces gcd(k,a) = a. Hence a ∣ π. Conversely m ∣ F_a gives π ∣ pisano(F_a) (bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd) ∣ 4a (bld2_pisano_fib_dvd_four_mul). So π = a·t with t ∣ 4, t ∈ {1,2,4}.

name: bld5_mantel_equality_connected
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) (hn : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) : G.Connected
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → 2 ≤ Fintype.card V → G.Connected
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_mantel_equality_complete_bipartite: it gives s with 2|s| = n and Adj x y ↔ (x ∈ s ↔ y ∉ s). Since n ≥ 2, both s and its complement are non-empty; pick u ∈ s, w ∉ s. Any x ∈ s is adjacent to w and any x ∉ s is adjacent to u, and u ~ w, so every two vertices are joined by a walk of length ≤ 3 through u, w: G is preconnected and V is non-empty.

name: bld5_pisano_lucas_odd_eq
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (ho : Odd n) : p3_pisano (p3_lucas n) = 2 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → Odd n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) = 2 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_cassini_cast and Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast: F_{2n} = F_n·L_n ≡ 0 (Nat.fib_two_mul) and F_{2n+1} = F_{n+1}·L_n − (−1)^n ≡ 1 mod L_n for odd n (lib_p3_lucas_cast, Nat.fib_two_mul_add_one, lib_fib_cassini_cast); so lib_fib_period_iff + bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period give π ∣ 2n (improving bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul). Conversely lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period (i = 0) gives L_n ∣ F_π, hence by Nat.fib_gcd L_n ∣ F_{gcd(π,2n)}; F_{n+1} < L_n forces gcd(π, 2n) ≥ n + 2, and the only divisor of 2n above n is 2n, so 2n ∣ π.
source: builds on Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_cassini_cast, Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast

name: poly_cyclotomic_two_mul_odd_comp_neg
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h1 : 1 < n) : Polynomial.cyclotomic (2 * n) ℤ = (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).comp (-Polynomial.X)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → 1 < n → Polynomial.cyclotomic (2 * n) ℤ = (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).comp (-Polynomial.X)
informal: For odd n > 1, Φ_{2n}(X) = Φ_n(-X) — Polynomial.cyclotomic_mul_prime_of_not_dvd-type identity Φ_{2n}(X)·Φ_n(X) = Φ_n(X^2) (expand by the prime 2 ∤ n), together with Φ_n(X^2) = Φ_n(X)·Φ_n(-X) up to sign, proved via strong induction on n using X^n - 1 = ∏_{d ∣ n} Φ_d and (-X)^n - 1 = -(X^n + 1) for odd n; φ(n) even for n > 1 fixes the sign.

name: poly_cyclotomic_reverse_eq_self
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).reverse = Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).reverse = Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ
informal: Cyclotomic polynomials Φ_n (n ≥ 2) are palindromic — strong induction: X^n - 1 = ∏_{d ∣ n} Φ_d, reverse is multiplicative, reverse(X^n - 1) = -(X^n - 1), reverse(Φ_1) = -Φ_1, and cancel the product over proper divisors d ≥ 2 by the induction hypothesis.

name: bld5_nilpotent_pow_rank_succ_eq_zero
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) : A ^ (A.rank + 1) = 0
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → A ^ (A.rank + 1) = 0
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex, Mathlib2.gen_lin_nilpotent_pow_card_reduced, Mathlib2.bld4_rank_pow_eq_of_card_le and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff (nilpotency index ≤ rank + 1): let r_k = rank(A^k). If r_{k+1} = r_k for some k then by bld2_rank_pow_convex (non-increasing non-negative drops) r_j = r_k for all j ≥ k, and by gen_lin_nilpotent_pow_card_reduced / bld4_rank_pow_eq_of_card_le r_j = 0 for large j, so r_k = 0. Hence r_k strictly decreases until it reaches 0, so r_{k+1} ≤ r_1 − k while positive; thus r_{r_1 + 1} = 0 and lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff gives A^(rank A + 1) = 0.

name: bld5_nilpotent_max_index_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (h : A ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) ≠ 0) : A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → A ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) ≠ 0 → A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_rank_pow_convex, Mathlib2.gen_lin_nilpotent_pow_card_reduced and Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff (converse of bld4_nilpotent_corank_one_rank_pow): let r_k = rank(A^k), n = card ι, d_k = r_k − r_{k+1} ≥ 0 (Matrix.rank_mul_le_left). gen_lin_nilpotent_pow_card_reduced gives r_n = 0, and lib_matrix_rank_eq_zero_iff with the hypothesis gives r_{n−1} ≥ 1, so d_{n−1} ≥ 1. bld2_rank_pow_convex says d_k is non-increasing, so d_k ≥ 1 for all k ≤ n−1. Since d_0 + … + d_{n−1} = r_0 − r_n = n, every d_k = 1; in particular rank A = r_1 = n − 1.

name: poly_real_nonneg_eq_sum_two_squares
statement: (p : Polynomial ℝ) (h : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x p) : ∃ f g : Polynomial ℝ, p = f ^ 2 + g ^ 2
type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x p) → ∃ f g, p = f ^ 2 + g ^ 2
informal: A real polynomial that is nonnegative on ℝ is a sum of two squares of real polynomials — strong induction on degree: real roots have even multiplicity (factor out (X-r)^2), irreducible quadratic factors are (X-u)^2 + v^2, and sums of two squares are closed under multiplication (Brahmagupta identity).

name: bld5_card_orderOf_eq_larger_prime_of_card_prime_mul_prime
statement: (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) : Nat.card {g : G // orderOf g = q} = q - 1
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Nat.Prime q → p < q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → Nat.card { g // orderOf g = q } = q - 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_card_orderOf_eq_prime_of_card_prime_mul_prime: every element has order dividing pq, i.e. in {1, p, q, pq}; order pq is impossible since then G is cyclic (isCyclic_of_orderOf_eq_card) hence commutative. Partition G by order: pq = 1 + q(p−1) + #{order q}, where q(p−1) is the bld4 count of elements of order p; so #{order q} = pq − 1 − q(p−1) = q − 1.

name: bld5_card_pow_prime_eq_one_of_card_prime_cube
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p ^ 3) (hna : ∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : Nat.card {g : G // g ^ p = 1} = p ^ 2 ∨ Nat.card {g : G // g ^ p = 1} = p ^ 3
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p ^ 3 → (∃ a b, a * b ≠ b * a) → p ≠ 2 → Nat.card { g // g ^ p = 1 } = p ^ 2 ∨ Nat.card { g // g ^ p = 1 } = p ^ 3
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_pow_prime_monoidHom_center_of_card_prime_cube and Mathlib2.bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube: the bld4 theorem gives a homomorphism φ : G →* Z(G) with φ g = g^p, so {g | g^p = 1} is the carrier of φ.ker. By the first isomorphism theorem |G| = |ker φ|·|range φ|, and |range φ| divides |Z(G)| = p (bld_center_card_of_card_prime_cube, Lagrange), so |range φ| ∈ {1, p} and |ker φ| ∈ {p³, p²}. (Sharpens bld4_card_pow_prime_eq_one_ge_of_card_prime_cube: exponent-p case vs. exponent-p² case.)

name: bld5_pisano_lucas_even_eq
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (he : Even n) : p3_pisano (p3_lucas n) = 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → Even n → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) = 4 * n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_cassini_cast and Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast: π := pisano(L_n) ∣ 4n by the bld4 theorem. By lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period (i = 0) L_n ∣ F_π; also L_n ∣ F_{2n} (Nat.fib_two_mul), so by Nat.fib_gcd L_n ∣ F_g with g = gcd(π, 2n) ∣ 2n; since F_{n+1} < L_n ≤ F_g forces g ≥ n+2 > n, g = 2n, i.e. 2n ∣ π. So π ∈ {2n, 4n}. If π = 2n then (lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, i = 1) F_{2n+1} ≡ 1 mod L_n; but F_{2n+1} = F_{n+1}·L_n − (−1)^n (from lib_p3_lucas_cast, Nat.fib_two_mul_add_one and lib_fib_cassini_cast), which is ≡ −1 for even n, giving L_n ∣ 2, false as L_n ≥ 3.
source: builds on Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_cassini_cast, Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast

name: bld5_pisano_mul_dvd_mul
statement: (d m : ℕ) (hd : d ∣ m) : p3_pisano (d * m) ∣ d * p3_pisano m
type: ∀ (d m : ℕ), d ∣ m → Mathlib2.p3_pisano (d * m) ∣ d * Mathlib2.p3_pisano m
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_pos_and_period, Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff and Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period: (m = 0 is trivial.) Let N = pisano m; bld3_pisano_pos_and_period + lib_fib_period_iff give F_N ≡ 0, F_{N+1} ≡ 1 mod m, i.e. Q^N = 1 + m•M for the Fibonacci matrix Q = !![1,1;1,0] over ℤ (Matrix.fib-style identity Q^n = [[F_{n+1},F_n],[F_n,F_{n-1}]]). Binomial expansion (Commute.add_pow) of (1 + m•M)^d: the j = 1 term is d·m·M and for j ≥ 2 m^j is divisible by m·d since d ∣ m; so Q^{dN} ≡ 1 mod d·m, i.e. F_{dN} ≡ 0, F_{dN+1} ≡ 1 mod d·m. lib_fib_period_iff turns this into dN being a period and bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period concludes. Special case: π(p^(k+1)) ∣ p·π(p^k).
