name: bld5_pisano_two_pow
type: ∀ (k : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_pisano (2 ^ (k + 1)) = 3 * 2 ^ k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd and Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period: prove by induction on j ≥ 1, using Nat.fib_two_mul and Nat.fib_two_mul_add_one, that F_{3·2^j} ≡ 2^(j+2) mod 2^(j+3) and F_{3·2^j+1} ≡ 1 + 2^(j+1) mod 2^(j+2) (base F_6 = 8, F_7 = 13). Upper bound: F_{3·2^k} ≡ 0, F_{3·2^k+1} ≡ 1 mod 2^(k+1), so lib_fib_period_iff + bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period give pisano ∣ 3·2^k. Lower bound by induction on k: bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd gives 3·2^(k-1) = pisano(2^k) ∣ pisano(2^(k+1)), so the value is 3·2^(k-1) or 3·2^k; the former is not a period (lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period at i = 1, or i = 0 when k = 1) because F_{3·2^(k-1)+1} ≡ 1 + 2^k ≢ 1 mod 2^(k+1). Base: pisano 2 = 3 by direct check.
source: builds on Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period

name: bld5_pisano_five_pow
type: ∀ (k : ℕ), Mathlib2.p3_pisano (5 ^ (k + 1)) = 4 * 5 ^ (k + 1)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd and Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period: key identity F_{5n} = 25F_n^5 + 25(-1)^n F_n^3 + 5F_n (over ℤ), whence by induction 5^j ∣ F_{5^j} but 5^(j+1) ∤ F_{5^j}. Upper bound: induct with the matrix/binomial argument (Q^{4·5^k} = 1 + 5^k•M ⇒ Q^{4·5^(k+1)} ≡ 1 mod 5^(k+1)), base F_20 = 6765, F_21 = 10946; then lib_fib_period_iff + bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period give pisano ∣ 4·5^(k+1). Lower bound by induction: bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd gives 4·5^k ∣ pisano(5^(k+1)) ∣ 4·5^(k+1), so the quotient is 1 or 5; if pisano = 4·5^k then (lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period, i = 0) 5^(k+1) ∣ F_{4·5^k}, and with 5^(k+1) ∣ F_{5^(k+1)} and Nat.fib_gcd this gives 5^(k+1) ∣ F_{5^k}, contradiction. Base pisano 5 = 20 by direct check of the divisors of 20.
source: builds on Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_of_period, Mathlib2.bld3_pisano_dvd_pisano_of_dvd, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period

name: lib_radical_pow_dvd_of_irreducible_pow_dvd
statement: {M : Type*} [CommMonoidWithZero M] [IsCancelMulZero M] [NormalizationMonoid M] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid M] (n : ℕ) (g : M) (hg : ∀ p : M, Irreducible p → p ∣ g → p ^ n ∣ g) : (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical g) ^ n ∣ g
type: ∀ {M : Type u_1} [inst : CancelCommMonoidWithZero M] [inst_1 : NormalizationMonoid M] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid M] (n : ℕ) (g : M), (∀ (p : M), Irreducible p → p ∣ g → p ^ n ∣ g) → UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical g ^ n ∣ g
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.poly_no_consecutive_powerful_aux1 (generalised from k[X], n = 2 to any normalised UFM and any exponent): if every irreducible factor of g occurs to the n-th power then (radical g)^n divides g.

name: lib_polynomial_natDegree_radical_eq_card_roots_toFinset
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [IsAlgClosed k] (p : Polynomial k) (hp : p ≠ 0) : (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical p).natDegree = p.roots.toFinset.card
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] [IsAlgClosed k] (p : Polynomial k), p ≠ 0 → (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical p).natDegree = p.roots.toFinset.card
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.poly_abc_distinct_roots_complex_aux1 (strengthened from ≤ to =): over an algebraically closed field the degree of the radical of a nonzero polynomial is its number of distinct roots.

name: lib_chebyshev_T_natDegree_le
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (n : ℤ) : (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T R n).natDegree ≤ n.natAbs
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n : ℤ), (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T R n).natDegree ≤ n.natAbs
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.poly_chebyshev_T_card_distinct_real_roots_aux1 (generalised from natural to integer index): the Chebyshev polynomial T_n has degree at most |n| over any commutative ring.

name: lib_fib_two_mul_add_one_cast_eq_fib_succ_mul_lucas
statement: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) : ((Nat.fib (2 * n + 1) : ℕ) : R) = ((Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℕ) : R) * ((Mathlib2.p3_lucas n : ℕ) : R) - (-1) ^ n
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : CommRing R] (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib (2 * n + 1)) = ↑(Nat.fib (n + 1)) * ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) - (-1) ^ n
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_lucas_odd_eq_aux1 (generalised from ℤ to any commutative ring): F_{2n+1} = F_{n+1} L_n - (-1)^n.

name: lib_matrix_mulVec_eq_zero_of_rank_mul_self_eq
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (N : Matrix ι ι K) (hN : (N * N).rank = N.rank) (v : ι → K) (hv : N.mulVec (N.mulVec v) = 0) : N.mulVec v = 0
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (N : Matrix ι ι K), (N * N).rank = N.rank → ∀ (v : ι → K), N.mulVec (N.mulVec v) = 0 → N.mulVec v = 0
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld4_fitting_range_inter_ker_pow_card_aux2: if rank(N^2) = rank N then range N meets ker N trivially, i.e. N(Nv) = 0 implies Nv = 0.

name: lib_antitone_convex_nat_seq_eq_of_succ_eq
statement: (r : ℕ → ℕ) (hanti : ∀ k, r (k + 1) ≤ r k) (hconv : ∀ k, 2 * r (k + 1) ≤ r k + r (k + 2)) (k : ℕ) (hk : r (k + 1) = r k) (j : ℕ) : r (k + j) = r k
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_nilpotent_pow_rank_succ_eq_zero_aux1 (conclusion simplified): a non-increasing convex sequence of naturals that stalls once is constant from then on.

name: arith_padicValNat_two_centralBinom
statement: (n : ℕ) : padicValNat 2 n.centralBinom = (Nat.digits 2 n).sum
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), padicValNat 2 n.centralBinom = (Nat.digits 2 n).sum
informal: v_2(C(2n,n)) equals the number of ones in the binary expansion of n — Kummer/Legendre: v_2 = s_2(n) + s_2(n) - s_2(2n) and s_2(2n) = s_2(n).

name: arith_card_divisors_sq_le
statement: (n : ℕ) : n.divisors.card ^ 2 ≤ 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), n.divisors.card ^ 2 ≤ 4 * n
informal: τ(n) ≤ 2√n — the map d ↦ min(d, n/d) is at most 2-to-1 from divisors into {1..⌊√n⌋}.

name: arith_two_mul_totient_eq_self_iff
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 2 * n.totient = n ↔ ∃ k : ℕ, n = 2 ^ (k + 1)
informal: φ(n) = n/2 iff n is a power of 2 with n ≥ 2 — n must be even; write n = 2^a m with m odd, then φ(n) = 2^(a-1) φ(m) so φ(m) = m forcing m = 1.

name: lib_fib_mul_modEq_sq_of_dvd
statement: (m N : ℕ) (u v : ℤ) (h0 : (Nat.fib N : ℤ) = (m : ℤ) * u) (h1 : (Nat.fib (N + 1) : ℤ) = 1 + (m : ℤ) * v) (j : ℕ) : (Nat.fib (j * N) : ℤ) ≡ (j : ℤ) * (m : ℤ) * u [ZMOD ((m ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)] ∧ (Nat.fib (j * N + 1) : ℤ) ≡ 1 + (j : ℤ) * (m : ℤ) * v [ZMOD ((m ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)]
type: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (u v : ℤ), ↑(Nat.fib N) = ↑m * u → ↑(Nat.fib (N + 1)) = 1 + ↑m * v → ∀ (j : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib (j * N)) ≡ ↑j * ↑m * u [ZMOD ↑(m ^ 2)] ∧ ↑(Nat.fib (j * N + 1)) ≡ 1 + ↑j * ↑m * v [ZMOD ↑(m ^ 2)]
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_mul_dvd_mul_aux2 (the square-zero lifting lemma specialised to ZMod (m^2), stated as congruences): if F_N = m·u and F_{N+1} = 1 + m·v then modulo m^2, F_{jN} ≡ j·m·u and F_{jN+1} ≡ 1 + j·m·v. For the general ring form (μ^2 = 0) use the aux lemma directly.

name: lib_pisano_lucas_two_mul_dvd_and_dvd_four_mul
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 2 * n ∣ Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∧ Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∣ 4 * n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 2 * n ∣ Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∧ Mathlib2.p3_pisano (Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) ∣ 4 * n
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_lucas_odd_eq_aux3 (combined with Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul): for n ≥ 2 the Pisano period of the Lucas number L_n is 2n or 4n — it is a multiple of 2n and a divisor of 4n.

name: lib_orderOf_eq_prime_of_card_prime_mul_prime_of_not_isCyclic
statement: (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q) (G : Type*) [Group G] (hG : Nat.card G = p * q) (hnc : ¬ IsCyclic G) (a : G) (ha : a ≠ 1) : orderOf a = p ∨ orderOf a = q
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G], Nat.card G = p * q → ¬IsCyclic G → ∀ (a : G), a ≠ 1 → orderOf a = p ∨ orderOf a = q
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld3_card_conjClasses_of_card_prime_mul_prime_aux1 (order part, hypothesis weakened from non-abelian to non-cyclic): in a non-cyclic group of order pq every non-identity element has order p or q. (The aux lemma also gives |C(a)| = orderOf a in the non-abelian case.)

name: arith_perfect_dvd_perfect_eq
statement: (m n : ℕ) (hm : m.Perfect) (hn : n.Perfect) (h : m ∣ n) : m = n
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m.Perfect → n.Perfect → m ∣ n → m = n
informal: A perfect number never properly divides another perfect number — write n = k·m; k = 0 is impossible, k = 1 gives equality, and for k > 1 Uses Mathlib2.ab_perfect_mul_abundant at the key step: k·m is abundant, contradicting perfection of n (Nat.Perfect excludes Abundant).

name: arith_two_pow_mod_self_ne_one
informal: For n ≥ 2, 2^n is never ≡ 1 (mod n) — if 2^n % n = 1 then n | 2^n - 1 and Uses Mathlib2.nt2_dvd_two_pow_sub_one_eq_one at this step to get n = 1, contradiction.

name: calc_sum_mul_choose_sq
statement: (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 2), k * (n + 1).choose k ^ 2 = (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1).choose n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 2), k * (n + 1).choose k ^ 2 = (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1).choose n
informal: ∑ₖ k·C(n+1,k)² = (n+1)·C(2n+1,n) — absorb k·C(n+1,k) = (n+1)·C(n,k−1), then Vandermonde ∑ C(n,k−1)C(n+1,n+1−k) = C(2n+1,n) (Nat.add_choose_eq).

name: arith_prime_mul_prime_deficient
statement: (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : p * q ≠ 6) : (p * q).Deficient
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → p * q ≠ 6 → (p * q).Deficient
informal: A product of two primes other than 6 is deficient — Uses Mathlib2.ab_prime_mul_prime_not_abundant at step 1 (not abundant); step 2: not perfect since (p+1)(q+1) = 2pq forces (p-1)(q-1) = 2, i.e. {p,q} = {2,3}, and p² is a prime power; conclude by Nat.deficient_iff_not_abundant_and_not_perfect.

name: calc_integral_log_one_add
statement: : ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, Real.log (1 + x) = 2 * Real.log 2 - 1
type: ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..1, Real.log (1 + x) = 2 * Real.log 2 - 1
informal: ∫₀¹ log(1+x) dx = 2 log 2 − 1 — antiderivative (1+x)log(1+x) − x on [0,1]; FTC.

name: calc_card_even_card_subsets
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin (n + 1)))).filter (fun s => Even s.card)).card = 2 ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {s | Even s.card}.card = 2 ^ n
informal: Exactly half (2ⁿ) of the subsets of an (n+1)-set have even cardinality — involution s ↦ s ∆ {0} flips parity; or ∑ (−1)^|s| = 0 (Finset.sum_powerset_neg_one_pow_card) with total 2^(n+1).

name: calc_integral_sq_div_one_add_sq
informal: ∫₀¹ x²/(1+x²) dx = 1 − π/4 — rewrite integrand as 1 − 1/(1+x²); arctan.

name: lib_polynomial_fermat_quotients_eq_C
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (A B E : Polynomial k) (hE : E ≠ 0) (heq : A ^ n + B ^ n = E ^ n) : ∃ c d : k, algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k) A / algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k) E = RatFunc.C c ∧ algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k) B / algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k) E = RatFunc.C d
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (A B E : Polynomial k), E ≠ 0 → A ^ n + B ^ n = E ^ n → ∃ c d, (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k)) A / (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k)) E = RatFunc.C c ∧ (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k)) B / (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (RatFunc k)) E = RatFunc.C d
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.poly_ratfunc_fermat_curve_const_aux1 (DecidableEq dropped, both quotients): polynomial FLT without coprimality in quotient form — if A^n + B^n = E^n with n ≥ 3, E ≠ 0 in char 0 then A/E and B/E are constant rational functions.

name: arith_dvd_sum_coprime
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : n ∣ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n with k.Coprime n, k
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → n ∣ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n with k.Coprime n, k
informal: For n ≥ 3 the sum of the totatives of n is divisible by n — Uses Mathlib2.nt2_two_mul_sum_coprime_eq_mul_totient at step 1: 2·S = n·φ(n); φ(n) is even for n > 2 (Nat.totient_even), so S = n·(φ(n)/2).

name: calc_tsum_inv_mul_two_pow
informal: ∑_{n≥1} 1/(n 2ⁿ) = log 2 — Real.hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_one at x = 1/2 gives −log(1/2).

name: lib_lucas_two_mul_ring_cast
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] (m : ℕ) : ((Mathlib2.p3_lucas (2 * m) : ℕ) : R) = ((Mathlib2.p3_lucas m : ℕ) : R) ^ 2 - 2 * (-1) ^ m
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] (m : ℕ), ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas (2 * m)) = ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas m) ^ 2 - 2 * (-1) ^ m
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_prime_dvd_lucas_four_mul_mod_eight_aux1 (generalised from commutative rings to any ring): Lucas doubling L_{2m} = L_m^2 - 2(-1)^m.

name: arith_prod_divisors_sq
statement: (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : ∏ d ∈ (m ^ 2).divisors, d = m ^ (m ^ 2).divisors.card
type: ∀ (m : ℕ), 0 < m → ∏ d ∈ (m ^ 2).divisors, d = m ^ (m ^ 2).divisors.card
informal: The product of the divisors of m² is m^τ(m²) — Uses Mathlib2.nt2_prod_divisors_sq at step 1 with n = m²: (∏ d)² = (m²)^τ = (m^τ)², then take square roots in ℕ.

name: calc_integral_arctan_zero_one
statement: : ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, Real.arctan x = Real.pi / 4 - Real.log 2 / 2
type: ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..1, Real.arctan x = Real.pi / 4 - Real.log 2 / 2
informal: ∫₀¹ arctan x dx = π/4 − (log 2)/2 — antiderivative x arctan x − log(1+x²)/2; FTC, arctan 1 = π/4.

name: lib_fib_add_ring_cast
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] (a b : ℕ) : ((Nat.fib (a + b) : ℕ) : R) = ((Nat.fib a : ℕ) : R) * ((Nat.fib (b + 1) : ℕ) : R) + ((Nat.fib (a + 1) : ℕ) : R) * ((Nat.fib b : ℕ) : R) - ((Nat.fib a : ℕ) : R) * ((Nat.fib b : ℕ) : R)
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] (a b : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib (a + b)) = ↑(Nat.fib a) * ↑(Nat.fib (b + 1)) + ↑(Nat.fib (a + 1)) * ↑(Nat.fib b) - ↑(Nat.fib a) * ↑(Nat.fib b)
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_mul_dvd_mul_aux1 (generalised from commutative rings to any ring; same identity as Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_five_pow_aux1 over ℤ): subtraction form of the Fibonacci addition law F_{a+b} = F_a F_{b+1} + F_{a+1} F_b - F_a F_b, with no index shift.

name: arith_totient_add_sigma_eq_two_mul_iff_prime
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n.totient + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n = 2 * n ↔ n.Prime
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → (n.totient + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n = 2 * n ↔ Nat.Prime n)
informal: Equality case of the Sandor–Atanassov inequality φ(n)+σ(n) ≥ 2n (Mathlib2.p5_lemma2): equality iff n is prime — for composite n with least prime factor p, σ(n) ≥ n + n/p + 1 and φ(n) ≥ n - n/p (count of multiples of p is not all non-coprime... use φ(n) ≥ n - Σ_{q|n} n/q carefully, or induct with Mathlib2.p5_sigma_prime_mul_of_dvd), giving strict inequality.

name: arith_abundant_mul
statement: (n k : ℕ) (hn : n.Abundant) (hk : 0 < k) : (k * n).Abundant
type: ∀ (n k : ℕ), n.Abundant → 0 < k → (k * n).Abundant
informal: Every positive multiple of an abundant number is abundant — Uses Mathlib2.ab_abundant_def at the first and last step to pass to full divisor sums, and Mathlib2.ab_t2_mul_mem_divisors to inject d ↦ k·d from divisors of n into divisors of k·n, so σ(kn) ≥ kσ(n) > 2kn.

name: calc_card_no_adjacent_subsets
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin n))).filter (fun s => ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ j : Fin n, i ∈ s → j ∈ s → (i : ℕ) + 1 ≠ (j : ℕ))).card = Nat.fib (n + 2)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {s | ∀ (i j : Fin n), i ∈ s → j ∈ s → ↑i + 1 ≠ ↑j}.card = Nat.fib (n + 2)
informal: Subsets of {0,…,n−1} with no two consecutive elements number F_{n+2} — two-step induction: split by whether the last element is in the set, giving a(n+2) = a(n+1) + a(n); bijections via Fin.castSucc / Finset.map.

name: lib_fib_two_mul_ring_cast
statement: (R : Type*) [Ring R] (m : ℕ) : ((Nat.fib (2 * m) : ℕ) : R) = ((Nat.fib m : ℕ) : R) * (2 * ((Nat.fib (m + 1) : ℕ) : R) - ((Nat.fib m : ℕ) : R))
type: ∀ (R : Type u_1) [inst : Ring R] (m : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib (2 * m)) = ↑(Nat.fib m) * (2 * ↑(Nat.fib (m + 1)) - ↑(Nat.fib m))
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_lucas_dvd_four_mul_aux1 (generalised from commutative rings to any ring): cast form of Nat.fib_two_mul without truncated subtraction, F_{2m} = F_m (2 F_{m+1} - F_m).

name: arith_sum_moebius_mul_card_divisors
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ArithmeticFunction.moebius d * ((n / d).divisors.card : ℤ) = 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ArithmeticFunction.moebius d * ↑(n / d).divisors.card = 1
informal: Σ_{d|n} μ(d)τ(n/d) = 1 — Dirichlet convolution μ * (ζ * ζ) = ζ, then unfold the convolution over divisorsAntidiagonal.

name: lib_matrix_rank_pow_succ_lt_of_isNilpotent_of_ne_zero
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (k : ℕ) (hk : A ^ k ≠ 0) : (A ^ (k + 1)).rank < (A ^ k).rank
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → ∀ (k : ℕ), A ^ k ≠ 0 → (A ^ (k + 1)).rank < (A ^ k).rank
informal: promoted from Mathlib2.bld5_nilpotent_pow_rank_succ_eq_zero_aux2 (hypothesis restated as A^k ≠ 0 instead of rank ≠ 0): for a nilpotent matrix the ranks of the powers strictly decrease as long as the power is nonzero.

name: calc_integral_dalzell
informal: Dalzell's integral ∫₀¹ x⁴(1−x)⁴/(1+x²) dx = 22/7 − π — polynomial division: integrand = x⁶ − 4x⁵ + 5x⁴ − 4x² + 4 − 4/(1+x²); integrate termwise, integral_inv_one_add_sq / arctan 1 = π/4.

name: arith_sum_sigma_divisors
statement: (n : ℕ) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 d = ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, n / d * d.divisors.card
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) d = ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, n / d * d.divisors.card
informal: Σ_{d|n} σ(d) = Σ_{d|n} (n/d)τ(d) — both are the Dirichlet convolution id * ζ * ζ evaluated at n (associativity/commutativity of convolution).

name: calc_integral_x_mul_sin_sq
statement: : ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..Real.pi, x * Real.sin x ^ 2 = Real.pi ^ 2 / 4
type: ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, x * Real.sin x ^ 2 = Real.pi ^ 2 / 4
informal: ∫₀^π x sin²x dx = π²/4 — sin² = (1−cos 2x)/2, antiderivative x²/4 − x sin(2x)/4 − cos(2x)/8; or symmetry x ↦ π−x with integral_sin_sq.

name: arith_sigma_mul_totient_lt_sq
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n * n.totient < n ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n * n.totient < n ^ 2
informal: σ(n)φ(n) < n² for n ≥ 2 — both sides multiplicative; on a prime power σ(p^a)φ(p^a) = p^(a-1)(p^(a+1)-1) < p^(2a); multiply over the factorization (strong induction splitting off ordCompl).

name: calc_integral_log_sq_one_e
statement: : ∫ x in (1:ℝ)..Real.exp 1, Real.log x ^ 2 = Real.exp 1 - 2
type: ∫ (x : ℝ) in 1..Real.exp 1, Real.log x ^ 2 = Real.exp 1 - 2
informal: ∫₁^e log² x dx = e − 2 — antiderivative x log²x − 2x log x + 2x on [1,e]; FTC.

name: calc_card_surjective_fin_three
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Fin 3)).filter (fun f => Function.Surjective f)).card : ℤ) = 3 ^ n - 3 * 2 ^ n + 3
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ↑{f | Function.Surjective f}.card = 3 ^ n - 3 * 2 ^ n + 3
informal: Number of surjections from an n-set (n ≥ 1) onto a 3-set is 3ⁿ − 3·2ⁿ + 3 — inclusion–exclusion over the missed values; count functions avoiding a given value (2ⁿ) and avoiding two values (1).

name: arith_even_gt_46_sum_two_abundant
statement: (n : ℕ) (he : Even n) (hn : 46 < n) : ∃ a b : ℕ, a.Abundant ∧ b.Abundant ∧ a + b = n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Even n → 46 < n → ∃ a b, a.Abundant ∧ b.Abundant ∧ a + b = n
informal: Every even integer greater than 46 is a sum of two abundant numbers — Uses Mathlib2.ab_perfect_mul_abundant with Mathlib2.ab_perfect_six at the key step: every multiple 6k with k > 1 is abundant; split n mod 6: n = 12 + (n-12), n = 20 + (n-20), or n = 40 + (n-40) with 20, 40 abundant and the other summand a multiple of 6 that is ≥ 12.

name: arith_odd_dvd_sq_add_one_mod_four
statement: (n d : ℕ) (hd : d ∣ n ^ 2 + 1) (ho : Odd d) : d % 4 = 1
informal: Every odd divisor of n² + 1 is ≡ 1 (mod 4) — Uses Mathlib2.nt2_prime_three_mod_four_dvd_sq_add_sq at step 1 (with b = 1) to show no prime ≡ 3 mod 4 divides n²+1; so all prime factors of d are ≡ 1 mod 4, and a product of such numbers is ≡ 1 mod 4 (induction on d).

name: arith_totient_pow_add_sigma_pow
statement: (n k : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 2 * n ^ k ≤ n.totient ^ k + ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ^ k
type: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 2 * n ^ k ≤ n.totient ^ k + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ^ k
informal: Power-mean extension of Sandor–Atanassov: φ(n)^k + σ(n)^k ≥ 2n^k for n ≥ 2 — Uses Mathlib2.p5_lemma2 at step 1 (φ + σ ≥ 2n), then convexity of x^k: ((a+b)/2)^k ≤ (a^k+b^k)/2 (inner_le_nnorm_mul_norm / add_pow_le_pow_mul_pow_of_add_eq_one, or induction on k via Chebyshev).

name: calc_sum_card_fixed_points_perm
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => σ i = i)).card = n.factorial
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∑ σ, {i | σ i = i}.card = n.factorial
informal: Total number of fixed points over all permutations of Fin n (n ≥ 1) is n! (expected number of fixed points is 1) — double count pairs (σ,i) with σ i = i: each i has (n−1)! stabiliser elements (MulAction.card stabilizer / Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin), so total n·(n−1)!.

name: calc_tsum_inv_three_consecutive
informal: ∑_{n≥1} 1/(n(n+1)(n+2)) = 1/4 — telescoping: term = (1/2)(1/((n+1)(n+2)) − 1/((n+2)(n+3))); HasSum via tendsto of partial sums 1/4 − 1/(2(N+1)(N+2)).

name: calc_tsum_sq_div_two_pow
informal: ∑ n²/2ⁿ = 6 — write n² = n(n−1)+n, use hasSum_coe_mul_geometric_of_norm_lt_one and tsum_choose_mul_geometric (or differentiate geometric series twice) at r = 1/2.

name: arith_prod_properDivisors_eq_self_iff
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∏ d ∈ n.properDivisors, d = n ↔ n.divisors.card = 4
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → (∏ d ∈ n.properDivisors, d = n ↔ n.divisors.card = 4)
informal: The product of the proper divisors of n ≥ 2 equals n iff n has exactly four divisors — with P the proper-divisor product, ∏ divisors = n·P; Uses Mathlib2.nt2_prod_divisors_sq at the key step: (nP)² = n^τ(n), so P = n iff n⁴ = n^τ(n) iff τ(n) = 4 (pow injective for n ≥ 2).

name: calc_sum_sq_card_fixed_points_perm
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => σ i = i)).card ^ 2 = 2 * n.factorial
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∑ σ, {i | σ i = i}.card ^ 2 = 2 * n.factorial
informal: Second moment of fixed-point count: ∑_σ fix(σ)² = 2·n! for n ≥ 2 (variance 1) — count triples (σ,i,j) with both fixed: n·(n−1)! diagonal plus n(n−1)·(n−2)! off-diagonal; equivalently Burnside for the action on ordered pairs (2 orbits).

name: calc_tsum_cube_div_two_pow
informal: ∑ n³/2ⁿ = 26 — expand n³ in binomials C(n,1)+6C(n,2)+6C(n,3) and use ∑ C(n,k) rⁿ = rᵏ/(1−r)^(k+1) at r = 1/2; or telescoping with S(n)= -(n³+3n²+9n+13)/2^(n-1).

name: arith_mul_sigma_le_sigma_mul
statement: (m n : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : m.primeFactors ⊆ n.primeFactors) : m * ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ≤ ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 (m * n)
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), m ≠ 0 → n ≠ 0 → m.primeFactors ⊆ n.primeFactors → m * (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ≤ (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) (m * n)
informal: If every prime factor of m divides n then mσ(n) ≤ σ(mn) — induct on m by peeling off a prime p | m: Uses Mathlib2.p5_sigma_prime_mul_of_dvd at each step (p | (m/p)·n since p | n) to get σ(p·(m/p)n) > pσ((m/p)n).

name: calc_tsum_fib_div_two_pow
statement: : ∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.fib n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n = 2
type: ∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.fib n) / 2 ^ n = 2
informal: ∑ Fₙ/2ⁿ = 2 — summability by Fₙ ≤ φⁿ-type bound (fib n ≤ (7/4)^n or 2^n·(geometric)), then S = 1/2 + S/2 + S/4 from the recurrence; or closed partial sums 2 − F_{N+3}/2^N…

name: arith_sum_natAbs_moebius
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, (ArithmeticFunction.moebius d).natAbs = 2 ^ ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, (ArithmeticFunction.moebius d).natAbs = 2 ^ ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors n
informal: Σ_{d|n} |μ(d)| = 2^ω(n) — |μ(d)| is the indicator of squarefree d; squarefree divisors of n biject with subsets of n.primeFactors.

name: arith_sum_moebius_mul_totient
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ArithmeticFunction.moebius d * (d.totient : ℤ) = ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, (2 - (p : ℤ))
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, ArithmeticFunction.moebius d * ↑d.totient = ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, (2 - ↑p)
informal: Σ_{d|n} μ(d)φ(d) = ∏_{p|n} (2 - p) — sum over squarefree divisors of a multiplicative function expands as ∏_{p|n}(1 + μ(p)φ(p)) = ∏(1 - (p-1)).

name: calc_card_perm_one_fixed_point
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1)))).filter (fun σ => (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => σ i = i)).card = 1)).card = (n + 1) * numDerangements n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {σ | {i | σ i = i}.card = 1}.card = (n + 1) * numDerangements n
informal: Permutations of an (n+1)-set with exactly one fixed point number (n+1)·D(n) — choose the fixed point, derange the remaining n points (card_derangements_eq_numDerangements, Equiv.Perm.subtypeEquivSubtypePerm / derangements.atMostOneFixedPointEquivSum_derangements).

name: arith_card_divisors_odd_iff_isSquare
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : Odd n.divisors.card ↔ IsSquare n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (Odd n.divisors.card ↔ IsSquare n)
informal: τ(n) is odd iff n is a perfect square — the involution d ↦ n/d on divisors has a fixed point iff n is a square.

name: calc_card_involutions_rec
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 2)))).filter (fun σ => σ * σ = 1)).card = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1)))).filter (fun σ => σ * σ = 1)).card + (n + 1) * ((Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))).filter (fun σ => σ * σ = 1)).card
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {σ | σ * σ = 1}.card = {σ | σ * σ = 1}.card + (n + 1) * {σ | σ * σ = 1}.card
informal: Involution numbers satisfy I(n+2) = I(n+1) + (n+1)·I(n) — split involutions of Fin (n+2) by whether the last point is fixed (I(n+1)) or swapped with one of n+1 others (remaining n points carry an involution).

name: calc_tsum_nat_div_factorial
statement: : ∑' n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) / (n.factorial : ℝ) = Real.exp 1
type: ∑' (n : ℕ), ↑n / ↑n.factorial = Real.exp 1
informal: ∑ n/n! = e — drop n = 0 term, n/n! = 1/(n−1)!, reindex and use Real.exp series (NormedSpace.exp / Real.exp_eq_tsum / hasSum_nat_add_iff).

name: arith_orderOf_two_zmod_three_pow
statement: (n : ℕ) : orderOf (2 : ZMod (3 ^ (n + 1))) = 2 * 3 ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), orderOf 2 = 2 * 3 ^ n
informal: 2 is a primitive root modulo every power of 3: its order mod 3^(n+1) is 2·3^n = φ(3^(n+1)) — the order divides φ; Uses Mathlib2.nt2_lte_three_two_pow_three_pow_add_one at the key step: 2^(3^n) ≡ -1 ≠ 1 rules out divisors of 3^n, and the exact valuation v_3(2^(3^(n-1)) + 1) = n (with 3 ∤ 2^(3^(n-1)) - 1) rules out 2·3^(n-1).

name: calc_cos_le_quartic
statement: (x : ℝ) : Real.cos x ≤ 1 - x ^ 2 / 2 + x ^ 4 / 24
informal: cos x ≤ 1 − x²/2 + x⁴/24 for all real x — even function so WLOG x ≥ 0; derivative of RHS − LHS is sin x − x + x³/6 ≥ 0 (previous Taylor bound), value 0 at 0.

name: calc_tan_ge_cubic
statement: (x : ℝ) (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx : x < Real.pi / 2) : x + x ^ 3 / 3 ≤ Real.tan x
type: ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → x < Real.pi / 2 → x + x ^ 3 / 3 ≤ Real.tan x
informal: tan x ≥ x + x³/3 on [0, π/2) — derivative of tan x − x − x³/3 is tan²x − x² ≥ 0 since tan x ≥ x (Real.lt_tan); monotonicity on [0,π/2).

name: calc_one_add_inv_pow_lt_exp
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ n < Real.exp 1
informal: (1+1/n)ⁿ < e — from 1 + t < exp t for t ≠ 0 (Real.add_one_lt_exp) at t = 1/n, raise to n-th power, exp(1/n)^n = e.

name: calc_card_idempotent_functions
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Fin n)).filter (fun f => ∀ i, f (f i) = f i)).card = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), n.choose k * k ^ (n - k)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {f | ∀ (i : Fin n), f (f i) = f i}.card = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), n.choose k * k ^ (n - k)
informal: Number of idempotent self-maps of an n-set is ∑ₖ C(n,k) k^(n−k) — classify by the image S (= fixed-point set) of size k; the n−k other points map arbitrarily into S.

name: calc_exp_lt_one_add_inv_pow_succ
informal: e < (1+1/n)^(n+1) — equivalent to 1/(n+1) < log(1+1/n), i.e. exp(−1/(n+1)) > 1 − 1/(n+1) = n/(n+1) (Real.add_one_lt_exp at t = −1/(n+1)); invert and raise to power n+1.

name: calc_pi_rpow_exp_lt_exp_pi
statement: : Real.pi ^ Real.exp 1 < Real.exp Real.pi
type: Real.pi ^ Real.exp 1 < Real.exp Real.pi
informal: π^e < e^π — log x / x is strictly decreasing for x ≥ e, or directly log π < π/e from log t ≤ t − 1 with t = π/e ≠ 1 (Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos).

name: calc_rpow_self_ge
statement: (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) : Real.exp (-Real.exp (-1)) ≤ x ^ x
type: ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 < x → Real.exp (-Real.exp (-1)) ≤ x ^ x
informal: xˣ ≥ e^(−1/e) for x > 0 — xˣ = exp(x log x) and x log x ≥ −1/e (apply log t ≤ t − 1 to t = 1/(e x), or Real.mul_log lower bound lemmas).

name: calc_rpow_lt_rpow_swap_of_exp_le
statement: (x y : ℝ) (hx : Real.exp 1 ≤ x) (hxy : x < y) : y ^ x < x ^ y
type: ∀ (x y : ℝ), Real.exp 1 ≤ x → x < y → y ^ x < x ^ y
informal: For e ≤ x < y, yˣ < xʸ — log t / t is strictly decreasing on [e, ∞) (derivative (1 − log t)/t² < 0 for t > e), so log y / y < log x / x; exponentiate.

name: arith_centralBinom_dvd_lcm
statement: (n : ℕ) : n.centralBinom ∣ (Finset.Icc 1 (2 * n)).lcm id
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), n.centralBinom ∣ (Finset.Icc 1 (2 * n)).lcm id
informal: C(2n,n) divides lcm(1,…,2n) — for each prime p, v_p(C(2n,n)) ≤ log_p(2n) (Nat.factorization_choose_le_log) and p^⌊log_p 2n⌋ ≤ 2n lies in the range, so it divides the lcm; assemble via factorization.

name: arith_sigma_le_mul_log
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n ≤ n * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n ≤ n * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)
informal: σ(n) ≤ n(1 + ⌊log₂ n⌋) — σ(n) = Σ_{d|n} n/d ≤ Σ_{k ≤ n} ⌊n/k⌋·[k|n] ≤ n·H_n and H_n ≤ 1 + ⌊log₂ n⌋ by dyadic grouping.

name: calc_tsum_inv_odd_sq
informal: ∑ 1/(2n+1)² = π²/8 — split Basel sum hasSum_zeta_two into even and odd indices (tsum_even_add_odd); even part is (1/4)·π²/6.

name: arith_even_perfect_last_digit
statement: (n : ℕ) (he : Even n) (hp : n.Perfect) : n % 10 = 6 ∨ n % 10 = 8
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Even n → n.Perfect → n % 10 = 6 ∨ n % 10 = 8
informal: Every even perfect number ends in 6 or 8 — by Euclid–Euler (Mathlib) n = 2^k(2^(k+1)-1) with 2^(k+1)-1 prime; k+1 = 2 or odd; reduce 2^k mod 10 by k mod 4.

name: arith_even_perfect_mod_nine
statement: (n : ℕ) (he : Even n) (hp : n.Perfect) (h6 : n ≠ 6) : n % 9 = 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Even n → n.Perfect → n ≠ 6 → n % 9 = 1
informal: Every even perfect number other than 6 is ≡ 1 (mod 9) — Euclid–Euler gives n = 2^(q-1)(2^q-1) with q an odd prime; 2 has order 6 mod 9 and q-1 is even, check the three residues of q-1 mod 6.

name: calc_tendsto_sum_inv_add_log_two
statement: : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / ((n : ℝ) + (k : ℝ) + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.log 2))
type: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / (↑n + ↑k + 1)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.log 2))
informal: lim ∑_{k=1}^{n} 1/(n+k) = log 2 — squeeze: log((n+k+1)/(n+k)) ≤ 1/(n+k) … termwise bounds 1/(m+1) ≤ log(m+1) − log m ≤ 1/m telescope to log((2n+1)/(n+1)) ≤ S_n ≤ log 2; or via H_{2n} − H_n and Euler–Mascheroni asymptotics.

name: arith_two_mul_dvd_totient_pow_add_one
statement: (a n : ℕ) (ha : 1 < a) (hn : 0 < n) : 2 * n ∣ (a ^ n + 1).totient
type: ∀ (a n : ℕ), 1 < a → 0 < n → 2 * n ∣ (a ^ n + 1).totient
informal: 2n divides φ(a^n + 1) for a > 1, n ≥ 1 — a is a unit mod N = a^n + 1 with a^n = -1 ≠ 1 and a^k < N - 1 for k < n, so its order is exactly 2n, and the order divides φ(N).

name: calc_factorial_gt_div_exp_pow
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ((n : ℝ) / Real.exp 1) ^ n < (n.factorial : ℝ)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (↑n / Real.exp 1) ^ n < ↑n.factorial
informal: n! > (n/e)ⁿ for n ≥ 1 — eⁿ = ∑ nᵏ/k! > nⁿ/n! (a single term of the positive exponential series, Real.sum_le_exp_of_nonneg / strict since other terms are positive); or induction using (1+1/n)ⁿ < e.

name: calc_tsum_alternating_inv_sq
informal: ∑ (−1)ⁿ/(n+1)² = π²/12 — equals (odd part) − (even part) of Basel sum = π²/8 − π²/24; uses hasSum_zeta_two and even/odd splitting.

name: arith_mersenne_prime_factor
type: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ≠ 2 → Nat.Prime q → q ∣ 2 ^ p - 1 → q % (2 * p) = 1 ∧ (q % 8 = 1 ∨ q % 8 = 7)
informal: Prime factors q of 2^p - 1 (p odd prime) satisfy q ≡ 1 mod 2p and q ≡ ±1 mod 8 — the order of 2 mod q is p so p | q-1, q odd gives 2p | q-1; 2 = (2^((p+1)/2))² mod q is a square, so q ≡ ±1 mod 8.

name: arith_dvd_two_pow_add_one_three_dvd
informal: If n > 1 divides 2^n + 1 then 3 | n — let p be the least prime factor of n; the order of 2 mod p divides gcd(2n, p-1) = 2 (n is odd), so p | 2² - 1 = 3.

name: arith_sigma_odd_iff
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : Odd (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) ↔ IsSquare n ∨ ∃ m : ℕ, n = 2 * m ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (Odd ((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) ↔ IsSquare n ∨ ∃ m, n = 2 * m ^ 2)
informal: σ(n) is odd iff n is a square or twice a square — σ multiplicative; σ(2^a) is always odd, σ(p^a) for odd p is odd iff a is even.

name: arith_liouville_sum_card_divisors_cube
statement: (n : ℕ) : ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d.divisors.card ^ 3 = (∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d.divisors.card) ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d.divisors.card ^ 3 = (∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d.divisors.card) ^ 2
informal: Liouville's identity Σ_{d|n} τ(d)³ = (Σ_{d|n} τ(d))² — both sides are multiplicative in n; on p^a it is Σ_{j=1}^{a+1} j³ = (Σ j)² (Nicomachus).

name: arith_perfect_not_isSquare
statement: (n : ℕ) (hp : n.Perfect) : ¬ IsSquare n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), n.Perfect → ¬IsSquare n
informal: No perfect number is a square — σ(m²) is odd (each σ(p^(2a)) is a sum of an odd number of odd terms, or p = 2) but σ(n) = 2n is even.

name: arith_card_odd_choose
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun k => Odd (n.choose k))).card = 2 ^ (Nat.digits 2 n).sum
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) | Odd (n.choose k)}.card = 2 ^ (Nat.digits 2 n).sum
informal: Glaisher: the number of odd entries in row n of Pascal's triangle is 2^(number of binary ones of n) — induct on binary digits using C(2n,2k) ≡ C(n,k), C(2n,2k+1) even, C(2n+1,2k) ≡ C(2n+1,2k+1) ≡ C(n,k) mod 2 (Lucas).

name: calc_integral_beta_nat
statement: (m n : ℕ) : ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x ^ m * (1 - x) ^ n = ((m.factorial : ℝ) * n.factorial) / ((m + n + 1).factorial : ℝ)
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..1, x ^ m * (1 - x) ^ n = ↑m.factorial * ↑n.factorial / ↑(m + n + 1).factorial
informal: Beta integral at naturals: ∫₀¹ xᵐ(1−x)ⁿ dx = m! n!/(m+n+1)! — induction on n with integration by parts B(m,n+1) = (n+1)/(m+1)·B(m+1,n); base ∫ xᵐ = 1/(m+1).

name: arith_fermat_prime_factor_mod_two_pow_add_two
informal: Lucas' strengthening: for n ≥ 2 every prime factor of the Fermat number F_n is ≡ 1 mod 2^(n+2) — Uses Mathlib2.nt2_fermat_number_prime_factor_form at step 1 to get p ≡ 1 mod 2^(n+1), hence p ≡ 1 mod 8, so 2 is a quadratic residue mod p (ZMod.exists_sq_eq_two_iff); a square root of 2 then has order 2^(n+2), which divides p - 1.

name: arith_totient_dvd_self_iff
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : n.totient ∣ n ↔ n = 1 ∨ ∃ a b : ℕ, n = 2 ^ (a + 1) * 3 ^ b
informal: φ(n) | n iff n = 1 or n = 2^a 3^b with a ≥ 1 — n/φ(n) = ∏ p/(p-1) must be an integer; for n>2 φ is even so 2 | n; the largest prime factor q>2 forces ∏(p-1) | ∏ p·…, compare 2-adic valuations: each odd prime contributes a factor 2 to φ, so at most one odd prime, and (q-1) | 2^a q forces q = 3.

name: calc_tsum_millin
statement: : ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (Nat.fib (2 ^ n) : ℝ) = (7 - Real.sqrt 5) / 2
informal: Millin series ∑_{n≥0} 1/F_{2ⁿ} = (7−√5)/2 — partial sums ∑_{n=0}^{N} 1/F_{2ⁿ} = 3 − F_{2^N − 1}/F_{2^N} for N ≥ 1 (induction, using F_{2m} = F_m L_m and d'Ocagne/Cassini), and F_{k−1}/F_k → 1/φ = (√5−1)/2.

name: arith_odd_perfect_euler_form
statement: (n : ℕ) (ho : Odd n) (hp : n.Perfect) : ∃ p a m : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p % 4 = 1 ∧ a % 4 = 1 ∧ ¬ p ∣ m ∧ n = p ^ a * m ^ 2
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → n.Perfect → ∃ p a m, Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 4 = 1 ∧ a % 4 = 1 ∧ ¬p ∣ m ∧ n = p ^ a * m ^ 2
informal: Euler's theorem on odd perfect numbers: n = p^a m² with p ≡ a ≡ 1 (mod 4), p ∤ m — σ(n) = 2n ≡ 2 (mod 4), so exactly one factor σ(q^e) is even and it is ≡ 2 mod 4; σ(q^e) for odd q is odd iff e even, and ≡ 2 mod 4 forces q ≡ e ≡ 1 mod 4.

name: arith_least_odd_abundant
statement: (n : ℕ) (ho : Odd n) (ha : n.Abundant) : 945 ≤ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → n.Abundant → 945 ≤ n
informal: 945 is the least odd abundant number — for odd n < 945: n has at most 3 distinct prime factors unless n ≥ 3·5·7·11; bound σ(n)/n < ∏ p/(p-1) and handle the families 3^a5^b7^c < 945 (or a finite case check).

name: arith_sum_lcm
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 2 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, Nat.lcm k n = n * (1 + ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d * d.totient)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → 2 * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, k.lcm n = n * (1 + ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d * d.totient)
informal: Σ_{k=1}^n lcm(k,n) = (n/2)(1 + Σ_{d|n} dφ(d)) — group k by g = gcd(k,n): lcm = n·(k/g) with k/g a totative of d = n/g; Uses Mathlib2.nt2_two_mul_sum_coprime_eq_mul_totient at the inner step for every d > 1 (twice the totative sum is dφ(d)); the d = 1 term contributes the extra 1.

name: arith_odd_perfect_not_dvd_105
statement: (n : ℕ) (ho : Odd n) (hp : n.Perfect) : ¬ 105 ∣ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → n.Perfect → ¬105 ∣ n
informal: No odd perfect number is divisible by 105 — by Euler's form the exponents of 3 and 7 (≡ 3 mod 4) are even, so 3²·5·7² | n and σ(n)/n ≥ (13/9)(6/5)(57/49) > 2 (σ(n)/n is monotone under divisibility), contradiction.

name: fld_finite_field_sum_two_squares
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (a : K) : ∃ x y : K, x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = a
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [Fintype K] (a : K), ∃ x y, x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = a
informal: Every element of a finite field is a sum of two squares — in characteristic 2 every element is a square (FiniteField.isSquare_of_char_two); otherwise apply FiniteField.exists_root_sum_quadratic to X^2 and X^2 - a (card is odd), or pigeonhole on the (q+1)/2 squares.

name: bld6_cyclotomic_coeff_symm
statement: (n k : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hk : k ≤ n.totient) : (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff k = (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff (n.totient - k)
type: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → k ≤ n.totient → (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff k = (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff (n.totient - k)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_cyclotomic_reverse_eq_self: rewrite the left side with reverse Φ_n = Φ_n and apply Polynomial.coeff_reverse with natDegree Φ_n = φ(n) (Polynomial.natDegree_cyclotomic) and revAt φ(n) k = φ(n) - k for k ≤ φ(n).

name: fld_irrational_cbrt_two
statement: (x : ℝ) (hx : x ^ 3 = 2) : Irrational x
type: ∀ (x : ℝ), x ^ 3 = 2 → Irrational x
informal: The real cube root of 2 is irrational — Uses Mathlib2.alg_rat_pow_ne_two at the only step: if x = (q : ℝ) then q^3 = 2 in ℚ by Rat.cast injectivity, contradicting alg_rat_pow_ne_two 3.

name: bld6_cyclotomic_eval_neg_one_of_odd
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h1 : 1 < n) : Polynomial.eval (-1) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ) = 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → 1 < n → Polynomial.eval (-1) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ) = 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_cyclotomic_two_mul_odd_comp_neg: Φ_n(-1) = (Φ_n ∘ (-X))(1) = Φ_(2n)(1) by the library identity (eval_comp); 2n with n odd > 1 is not a prime power, so Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_not_prime_pow gives Φ_(2n)(1) = 1.

name: fld_prime_one_mod_three_eq_sq_add_three_sq
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p % 3 = 1) : ∃ a b : ℕ, p = a ^ 2 + 3 * b ^ 2
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 3 = 1 → ∃ a b, p = a ^ 2 + 3 * b ^ 2
informal: Every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 3) is of the form a^2 + 3b^2 — -3 is a square mod p (cube roots of unity in F_p), so p | x^2 + 3 for some x; Thue's lemma / pigeonhole gives 0 < a^2 + 3b^2 ≡ 0 mod p with a, b < √p, hence a^2 + 3b^2 ∈ {p, 2p, 3p}; 2p is impossible mod 4 (or mod 3) and 3p reduces to p by a = 3a'.

name: bld6_cyclotomic_two_mul_odd_coeff
statement: (n k : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h1 : 1 < n) : (Polynomial.cyclotomic (2 * n) ℤ).coeff k = (-1) ^ k * (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff k
type: ∀ (n k : ℕ), Odd n → 1 < n → (Polynomial.cyclotomic (2 * n) ℤ).coeff k = (-1) ^ k * (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℤ).coeff k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_cyclotomic_two_mul_odd_comp_neg: rewrite Φ_(2n) = Φ_n ∘ (-X) and compute the k-th coefficient of p.comp(-X) as (-1)^k p.coeff k (write -X = C(-1)·X and use the coefficient formula for comp with C a * X).

name: fld_sum_pow_finite_field
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : ∑ x : K, x ^ k = if (Fintype.card K - 1) ∣ k then (-1 : K) else 0
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Fintype K] (k : ℕ), 0 < k → ∑ x, x ^ k = if Fintype.card K - 1 ∣ k then -1 else 0
informal: Complete power-sum formula over a finite field F_q: for k > 0, the sum of x^k over all x is -1 if (q-1) | k and 0 otherwise — since k > 0 the term x = 0 contributes 0, so the sum equals the sum over units, which is FiniteField.sum_pow_units.

name: bld6_nat_pow_lt_pow_swap
statement: (m n : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hmn : m < n) : n ^ m < m ^ n
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), 3 ≤ m → m < n → n ^ m < m ^ n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_rpow_lt_rpow_swap_of_exp_le: apply it with x = m, y = n; the hypothesis e ≤ m follows from Real.exp_one_lt_d9 (e < 3 ≤ m); then convert rpow with natural exponents to Nat powers (Real.rpow_natCast, Nat.cast_lt).

name: fld_prime_one_three_mod_eight_eq_sq_add_two_sq
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 3 → ∃ a b, p = a ^ 2 + 2 * b ^ 2
informal: Every prime p ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 8) is of the form a^2 + 2b^2 — -2 is a square mod p (ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_two_iff / FiniteField.isSquare_neg_two_iff), so p | x^2 + 2; Thue's lemma gives 0 < a^2 + 2b^2 < 3p divisible by p, so it is p or 2p; in the latter case a is even and p = b^2 + 2(a/2)^2. Alternatively use that Z[√-2] is Euclidean.

name: bld6_succ_pow_lt_exp_pow_mul_factorial
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n < Real.exp 1 ^ n * n.factorial
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (↑n + 1) ^ n < Real.exp 1 ^ n * ↑n.factorial
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_one_add_inv_pow_lt_exp: induction on n via (n+1)^n/n! = ∏_{k=1}^n (1+1/k)^k (ratio of consecutive terms is (1+1/(n+1))^(n+1)); each factor is < e by calc_one_add_inv_pow_lt_exp. Strengthens Mathlib2.calc_factorial_gt_div_exp_pow from n^n to (n+1)^n.

name: fld_prime_eq_sq_add_mul_add_sq_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : (∃ a b : ℕ, p = a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ↔ p = 3 ∨ p % 3 = 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ((∃ a b, p = a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ↔ p = 3 ∨ p % 3 = 1)
informal: A prime is represented by the Eisenstein norm form a^2 + ab + b^2 (a, b ≥ 0) iff p = 3 or p ≡ 1 (mod 3) — (→) a^2 + ab + b^2 mod 3 is never 2; (←) 3 = 1 + 1 + 1, and for p ≡ 1 mod 3 write p = c^2 + 3d^2 (the a^2 + 3b^2 theorem), then with c > d: a = c - d, b = 2d, and with c < d use the equivalent form (d - c, c + d) after symmetry, checking nonnegativity.

name: bld6_factorial_lt_exp_mul_pow
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (n.factorial : ℝ) < Real.exp 1 * n * ((n : ℝ) / Real.exp 1) ^ n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ↑n.factorial < Real.exp 1 * ↑n * (↑n / Real.exp 1) ^ n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_exp_lt_one_add_inv_pow_succ: put a_n = n!·e^n/(n·n^n); a_1 = e and a_(n+1)/a_n = e/(1+1/n)^(n+1) < 1 by calc_exp_lt_one_add_inv_pow_succ (the induction step), so a_n < e for n ≥ 2. This is the upper companion of Mathlib2.calc_factorial_gt_div_exp_pow.

name: fld_card_hyperbola_zmod
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) (a : ZMod p) (ha : a ≠ 0) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod p × ZMod p)).filter (fun v => v.1 ^ 2 - v.2 ^ 2 = a)).card = p - 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → ∀ (a : ZMod p), a ≠ 0 → {v | v.1 ^ 2 - v.2 ^ 2 = a}.card = p - 1
informal: For odd p and a ≠ 0 the equation x^2 - y^2 = a has exactly p-1 solutions in F_p — the change of variables u = x+y, v = x-y is a bijection of F_p^2 (2 invertible) turning it into uv = a, whose solutions are (u, a/u) for the p-1 units u.

name: fld_isSquare_three_zmod_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : 3 < p) : IsSquare (3 : ZMod p) ↔ p % 12 = 1 ∨ p % 12 = 11
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], 3 < p → (IsSquare 3 ↔ p % 12 = 1 ∨ p % 12 = 11)
informal: 3 is a quadratic residue mod a prime p > 3 iff p ≡ ±1 (mod 12) — quadratic reciprocity (ZMod.exists_sq_eq_prime_iff_of_mod_four_eq_one / _three) reduces to whether p is a square mod 3, i.e. p ≡ 1 mod 3, with a sign flip when p ≡ 3 mod 4; combine residues mod 4 and mod 3.

name: fld_pell_two_pm_one_solutions
informal: Every solution of x^2 - 2y^2 = ±1 with x > 0, y ≥ 0 is a power of the fundamental unit: x + y√2 = (1 + √2)^n — strong induction on y: if y = 0 then x = 1, n = 0; otherwise multiply by (1+√2)^{-1} = -1 + √2 to get (x', y') = (2y - x, x - y), which is again a solution with x' > 0 and 0 ≤ y' < y (from y ≤ x < 2y for y ≥ 1, with the edge case (1,1)).

name: fld_irrational_logb_two_three
statement: : Irrational (Real.logb 2 3)
type: Irrational (Real.logb 2 3)
informal: log_2 3 is irrational — if log_2 3 = a/b with b > 0 then (a > 0 and) 2^a = 3^b in ℕ after clearing rpow, impossible by parity (2^a even, 3^b odd).

name: fld_isSquare_five_zmod_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hp5 : p ≠ 5) : IsSquare (5 : ZMod p) ↔ p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → p ≠ 5 → (IsSquare 5 ↔ p % 5 = 1 ∨ p % 5 = 4)
informal: 5 is a quadratic residue mod a prime p ≠ 2, 5 iff p ≡ ±1 (mod 5) — since 5 ≡ 1 mod 4, ZMod.exists_sq_eq_prime_iff_of_mod_four_eq_one gives IsSquare (5 : ZMod p) ↔ IsSquare (p : ZMod 5), and the nonzero squares mod 5 are 1 and 4. (Makes the hypotheses of Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_pred_of_isSquare_five checkable.)

name: fld_zsqrtd_neg_five_two_irreducible_not_prime
statement: : Irreducible (2 : Zsqrtd (-5)) ∧ ¬ Prime (2 : Zsqrtd (-5))
type: Irreducible 2 ∧ ¬Prime 2
informal: In ℤ[√-5] the element 2 is irreducible but not prime (the classical non-UFD example) — norm a^2 + 5b^2 never equals 2, so a factorization 2 = xy (norms multiply to 4) has a factor of norm 1, a unit; yet 2 | 6 = (1+√-5)(1-√-5) while 2 divides neither factor (compare coefficients).

name: fld_minpoly_sqrt_two
statement: : minpoly ℚ (Real.sqrt 2) = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - 2
type: minpoly ℚ √2 = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - 2
informal: The minimal polynomial of √2 over ℚ is X^2 - 2 — it is monic, annihilates √2, and is irreducible over ℚ (degree 2 without rational root since √2 is irrational); conclude with minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic.

name: fld_sum_quadraticChar_sq_add
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) (a : ZMod p) (ha : a ≠ 0) : ∑ x : ZMod p, quadraticChar (ZMod p) (x ^ 2 + a) = -1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → ∀ (a : ZMod p), a ≠ 0 → ∑ x, (quadraticChar (ZMod p)) (x ^ 2 + a) = -1
informal: Quadratic character sum Σ_x χ(x^2 + a) = -1 for a ≠ 0 in F_p, p odd — count solutions of y^2 = x^2 + a two ways: it equals Σ_x (1 + χ(x^2 + a)) by quadraticChar_card_sqrts and equals p - 1 by the hyperbola count (y-x)(y+x) = a.

name: fld_minpoly_sqrt_two_add_sqrt_three
statement: : minpoly ℚ (Real.sqrt 2 + Real.sqrt 3) = Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1
type: minpoly ℚ (√2 + √3) = Polynomial.X ^ 4 - 10 * Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1
informal: The minimal polynomial of √2 + √3 over ℚ is X^4 - 10X^2 + 1 — the polynomial is monic and vanishes at √2+√3 ((√2+√3)^2 = 5 + 2√6); Uses Mathlib2.poly_x4_sub_10x2_add_1_irreducible_int for irreducibility over ℤ, transferred to ℚ by Gauss's lemma (Polynomial.Monic.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_fraction_map), then minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic.

name: fld_card_image_sq_finite_field
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (h : ringChar K ≠ 2) : (Finset.univ.image (fun x : K => x ^ 2)).card = (Fintype.card K + 1) / 2
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Fintype K] [inst_2 : DecidableEq K], ringChar K ≠ 2 → (Finset.image (fun x => x ^ 2) Finset.univ).card = (Fintype.card K + 1) / 2
informal: A finite field of odd characteristic with q elements has exactly (q+1)/2 squares. Generalizes Mathlib2.alg_card_range_sq_zmod_prime from ZMod p to all finite fields — squaring is 2-to-1 on nonzero elements (x^2 = y^2 iff x = ±y, and x ≠ -x as char ≠ 2), plus 0; q is odd.

name: bld6_hardy_odd_harmonic_means
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld2_hardy_inequality_tsum and Mathlib2.calc_tsum_inv_odd_sq: apply Hardy's inequality to a_k = 1/(2k+1); summability of a_k^2 and the value ∑ a_k^2 = π^2/8 come from calc_tsum_inv_odd_sq (rewrite (1/(2k+1))^2 = 1/(2k+1)^2), so the bound is 4·π^2/8.

name: fld_card_circle_zmod
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod p × ZMod p)).filter (fun v => v.1 ^ 2 + v.2 ^ 2 = 1)).card = if p % 4 = 1 then p - 1 else p + 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → {v | v.1 ^ 2 + v.2 ^ 2 = 1}.card = if p % 4 = 1 then p - 1 else p + 1
informal: The circle x^2 + y^2 = 1 over F_p (p odd) has p - (-1/p) points: p-1 if p ≡ 1 mod 4 and p+1 if p ≡ 3 mod 4 — if -1 = i^2 the substitution u = x+iy, v = x-iy gives the hyperbola uv = 1 with p-1 points; otherwise count via N = Σ_x (1 + χ(1-x^2)) and the Jacobsthal sum Σ χ(x^2 - 1)·χ(-1) = -χ(-1), or parametrize rationally by lines through (1,0).

name: fld_mul_isSquare_of_not_isSquare
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (a b : K) (ha : ¬ IsSquare a) (hb : ¬ IsSquare b) : IsSquare (a * b)
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [Fintype K] (a b : K), ¬IsSquare a → ¬IsSquare b → IsSquare (a * b)
informal: In a finite field the product of two non-squares is a square — in characteristic 2 everything is a square; otherwise the quadratic character is multiplicative with values ±1 on nonzero elements and equals -1 exactly on non-squares (quadraticChar_neg_one_iff_not_isSquare), so χ(ab) = 1.

name: fld_gaussianInt_prime_of_norm_prime
statement: (z : GaussianInt) (h : Nat.Prime z.norm.natAbs) : Prime z
type: ∀ (z : GaussianInt), Nat.Prime (Zsqrtd.norm z).natAbs → Prime z
informal: A Gaussian integer whose norm is a rational prime is a Gaussian prime — if z = xy then N(x)N(y) = p so one of x, y has norm 1 and is a unit (Zsqrtd.norm_eq_one_iff), so z is irreducible; ℤ[i] is a PID so irreducible elements are prime.

name: fld_card_four_sq_add_self_add_one
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (h : Fintype.card K = 4) (x : K) (h0 : x ≠ 0) (h1 : x ≠ 1) : x ^ 2 + x + 1 = 0
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Fintype K], Fintype.card K = 4 → ∀ (x : K), x ≠ 0 → x ≠ 1 → x ^ 2 + x + 1 = 0
informal: In a field with 4 elements every element other than 0, 1 is a root of X^2 + X + 1 — x^3 = 1 by FiniteField.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one, so (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1) = 0 and x ≠ 1.

name: fld_irreducible_X_sq_add_one_zmod_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1 : Polynomial (ZMod p)) ↔ p % 4 = 3
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1) ↔ p % 4 = 3
informal: X^2 + 1 is irreducible over F_p iff p ≡ 3 (mod 4) — a monic quadratic is irreducible iff it has no root (Polynomial.Monic.irreducible_iff_roots_eq_zero_of_degree_le_three), and a root is a square root of -1, which exists iff p % 4 ≠ 3 (ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff).

name: fld_gaussianInt_isUnit_iff
statement: (z : GaussianInt) : IsUnit z ↔ z = 1 ∨ z = -1 ∨ z = ⟨0, 1⟩ ∨ z = ⟨0, -1⟩
type: ∀ (z : GaussianInt), IsUnit z ↔ z = 1 ∨ z = -1 ∨ z = { re := 0, im := 1 } ∨ z = { re := 0, im := -1 }
informal: The units of ℤ[i] are exactly 1, -1, i, -i — by Zsqrtd.norm_eq_one_iff' a unit has norm re^2 + im^2 = 1, forcing (re, im) ∈ {(±1, 0), (0, ±1)}; the converse is a direct check.

name: fld_zsqrtd_neg_five_isUnit_iff
statement: (z : Zsqrtd (-5)) : IsUnit z ↔ z = 1 ∨ z = -1
informal: The only units of ℤ[√-5] are ±1 — by Zsqrtd.norm_eq_one_iff' (d ≤ 0) units are the elements with re^2 + 5 im^2 = 1, which forces im = 0 and re = ±1.

name: bld6_pisano_prime_not_dvd_succ_of_not_isSquare_five
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (h : ¬ IsSquare (5 : ZMod p)) : ¬ p3_pisano p ∣ p + 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], p ≠ 2 → ¬IsSquare 5 → ¬Mathlib2.p3_pisano p ∣ p + 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld5_prime_dvd_fib_succ_of_not_isSquare_five, Mathlib2.lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period and Mathlib2.lib_fib_period_iff: if π(p) ∣ p+1 then (lib_pisano_dvd_iff_period + lib_fib_period_iff) F_(p+2) ≡ 1 mod p. But p ∣ F_(p+1) (bld5 theorem) gives F_(p+2) ≡ F_p, and F_p ≡ 5^((p-1)/2) ≡ -1 mod p (Euler criterion, from 2^(p-1) F_p = ∑ C(p,2j+1) 5^j; or Cassini F_p^2 ≡ 1 plus F_(p-1) ≡ -F_p and p ∤ F_(p-1)·… ), contradiction as p ≠ 2. Complements bld4_pisano_prime_dvd_two_mul_succ_of_not_isSquare_five: the period divides 2(p+1) but not p+1.

name: fld_isSquare_neg_three_zmod_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : 3 < p) : IsSquare (-3 : ZMod p) ↔ p % 3 = 1
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], 3 < p → (IsSquare (-3) ↔ p % 3 = 1)
informal: -3 is a quadratic residue mod a prime p > 3 iff p ≡ 1 (mod 3) — either via legendreSym multiplicativity, (-1/p) and quadratic reciprocity for 3, or directly: -3 = (2ω+1)^2 where ω is a primitive cube root of unity, which exists in F_p iff 3 | p-1.

name: bld6_pisano_ten_pow
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_mul_of_coprime, Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_two_pow and Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_five_pow: 10^(k+3) = 2^(k+3)·5^(k+3) with coprime factors, so π = lcm(π(2^(k+3)), π(5^(k+3))) (bld4_pisano_mul_of_coprime) = lcm(3·2^(k+2), 4·5^(k+3)) by the two prime-power formulas; since k+2 ≥ 2 the lcm is 3·2^(k+2)·5^(k+3) = 15·10^(k+2).

name: bld6_pisano_two_pow_mul_five_pow_eq_six_mul_iff
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_pisano_mul_of_coprime, Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_two_pow and Mathlib2.bld5_pisano_five_pow: π(2^(a+1)5^(b+1)) = lcm(3·2^a, 4·5^(b+1)) by the coprime-lcm rule and the two prime-power formulas; this equals 12·5^(b+1) for a ≤ 1 and 3·2^a·5^(b+1) for a ≥ 2, i.e. 6n, 3n, 3n/2 respectively — so the extremal ratio π(n) = 6n occurs exactly for a = 0 (n = 2·5^(b+1)).

name: fld_irreducible_X_sq_add_X_add_one_zmod_iff
statement: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.X + 1 : Polynomial (ZMod p)) ↔ p % 3 = 2
type: ∀ (p : ℕ) [inst : Fact (Nat.Prime p)], Irreducible (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.X + 1) ↔ p % 3 = 2
informal: X^2 + X + 1 is irreducible over F_p iff p ≡ 2 (mod 3) — a monic quadratic is irreducible iff it has no root; for p = 3 it is (X-1)^2; for p ≠ 3 a root is exactly an element of multiplicative order 3, which exists iff 3 | p - 1 (cyclic unit group).

name: bld6_tsum_lucas_div_two_pow
statement: : ∑' n : ℕ, (p3_lucas n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n = 6
type: ∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(Mathlib2.p3_lucas n) / 2 ^ n = 6
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_tsum_fib_div_two_pow and Mathlib2.lib_p3_lucas_cast: by lib_p3_lucas_cast L_n = 2F_(n+1) - F_n in ℝ; ∑ F_n/2^n = 2 (calc_tsum_fib_div_two_pow, also giving summability), and dropping the zero term n = 0 gives ∑ F_(n+1)/2^n = 2·2 = 4; so the sum is 2·4 - 2 = 6.

name: bld6_integral_dalzell_companion
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_integral_dalzell and Mathlib2.calc_integral_beta_nat: x^6(1-x)^4/(1+x^2) = x^4(1-x)^4 - x^4(1-x)^4/(1+x^2) pointwise; split the integral (intervalIntegral.integral_sub), the first piece is 1/630 by calc_integral_beta_nat 4 4 and the second is 22/7 - π by calc_integral_dalzell.

name: bld6_pi_dalzell_beta_bounds
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_integral_dalzell and Mathlib2.calc_integral_beta_nat: on (0,1) one has x^4(1-x)^4/2 < x^4(1-x)^4/(1+x^2) < x^4(1-x)^4; integrate (strict monotonicity of the interval integral for continuous functions). The middle integral is 22/7 - π by calc_integral_dalzell, the outer one is 4!4!/9! = 1/630 by calc_integral_beta_nat 4 4.

name: bld6_tsum_inv_fib_mul_fib_add_two
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_tsum_inv_three_consecutive_aux1 (general telescoping HasSum lemma): take g n = 1/(F_(n+1) F_(n+2)); then g n - g (n+1) = (F_(n+3) - F_(n+1))/(F_(n+1)F_(n+2)F_(n+3)) = 1/(F_(n+1)F_(n+3)) by Nat.fib_add_two, g → 0 since F_(n+1) ≥ n/…→∞ (Nat.fib_lt_fib_succ / le_fib_self), and g 0 = 1.

name: fld_finrank_adjoin_sqrt_two_add_sqrt_three
statement: : Module.finrank ℚ (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ ({Real.sqrt 2 + Real.sqrt 3} : Set ℝ)) = 4
type: Module.finrank ℚ ↥ℚ⟮√2 + √3⟯ = 4
informal: [ℚ(√2+√3) : ℚ] = 4 — IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank reduces to the degree of the minimal polynomial, which is X^4 - 10X^2 + 1; Uses Mathlib2.poly_x4_sub_10x2_add_1_irreducible_int (irreducibility over ℤ, hence over ℚ by Gauss) to identify the minimal polynomial.

name: fld_adjoin_sqrt_two_sqrt_three_eq_adjoin_sum
statement: : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ ({Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt 3} : Set ℝ) = IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ ({Real.sqrt 2 + Real.sqrt 3} : Set ℝ)
informal: ℚ(√2, √3) = ℚ(√2 + √3): the sum is a primitive element — ⊇ is clear; for ⊆, with s = √2+√3 one has s^3 = 11√2 + 9√3, so √2 = (s^3 - 9s)/2 and √3 = (11s - s^3)/2 lie in ℚ(s).

name: bld6_tsum_inv_odd_sq_mul_odd_sq
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_tsum_inv_odd_sq and Mathlib2.calc_tsum_inv_odd_consecutive: 1/(a^2(a+2)^2) = (1/4)(1/a^2 + 1/(a+2)^2) - (1/2)·1/(a(a+2)) with a = 2n+1. The sum of 1/a^2 is π^2/8 (calc_tsum_inv_odd_sq), the shifted sum is π^2/8 - 1, and the sum of 1/(a(a+2)) is 1/2 (calc_tsum_inv_odd_consecutive): total (1/4)(π^2/4 - 1) - 1/4.

name: bld6_sum_choose_alternating_div_eq_beta
statement: (m n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * (n.choose k : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + k + 1) = ((m.factorial : ℝ) * n.factorial) / ((m + n + 1).factorial : ℝ)
type: ∀ (m n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (-1) ^ k * ↑(n.choose k) / (↑m + ↑k + 1) = ↑m.factorial * ↑n.factorial / ↑(m + n + 1).factorial
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_integral_beta_nat: expand (1-x)^n by the binomial theorem, so x^m(1-x)^n = ∑ (-1)^k C(n,k) x^(m+k); integrate termwise over [0,1] (integral_pow) to get the left side, and the right side is the value of the same integral by calc_integral_beta_nat m n (final step).

name: fld_sqrt_three_not_in_Q_sqrt_two
statement: (a b : ℚ) : Real.sqrt 3 ≠ (a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2
informal: √3 ∉ ℚ(√2) — squaring gives 3 = a^2 + 2b^2 + 2ab√2, so ab = 0 by irrationality of √2; b = 0 gives √3 = a rational, a = 0 gives 3 = 2b^2, i.e. (2b)^2 = 6, contradicting irrationality of √6.

name: bld6_lcm_mul_integral_central_beta_nat
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_integral_beta_nat and Mathlib2.arith_centralBinom_dvd_lcm: by mul_pow and calc_integral_beta_nat n n the integral is (n!)^2/(2n+1)! = 1/((2n+1)·centralBinom n) (Nat.centralBinom, Nat.choose factorial formula); so the left side equals lcm(1..2n)/centralBinom n, which is a positive natural number q by arith_centralBinom_dvd_lcm (Nair's integrality argument made explicit).

name: fld_cbrt_two_not_in_Q_sqrt_two
statement: (x : ℝ) (hx : x ^ 3 = 2) (a b : ℚ) : x ≠ (a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2
informal: The cube root of 2 does not lie in ℚ(√2) — expand (a + b√2)^3 = (a^3 + 6ab^2) + (3a^2 b + 2b^3)√2 = 2; irrationality of √2 forces b(3a^2 + 2b^2) = 0, so b = 0 and a^3 = 2; Uses Mathlib2.alg_rat_pow_ne_two at this last step.

name: fld_sum_quadratic_residues_one_mod_four
statement: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h : p % 4 = 1) : ∑ a ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 (p - 1)).image (fun x => x ^ 2 % p), a = p * (p - 1) / 4
type: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p % 4 = 1 → ∑ a ∈ Finset.image (fun x => x ^ 2 % p) (Finset.Icc 1 (p - 1)), a = p * (p - 1) / 4
informal: For a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) the sum of the quadratic residues in [1, p-1] equals p(p-1)/4 — -1 is a residue, so r ↦ p - r is a fixed-point-free involution on the (p-1)/2 residues, pairing them into (p-1)/4 pairs each of sum p.

name: fld_pow_char_eq_self_iff_natCast
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] (x : K) : x ^ p = x ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, x = (n : K)
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] (x : K), x ^ p = x ↔ ∃ n, x = ↑n
informal: In any field of characteristic p the fixed points of Frobenius are exactly the prime field: x^p = x iff x is the image of a natural number — (←) Fermat's little theorem in ZMod p pushed along the cast; (→) X^p - X has at most p roots in K and the p distinct elements 0, 1, …, p-1 are roots, so they are all the roots.

name: fld_gaussianInt_one_add_i_prime
statement: : Prime (⟨1, 1⟩ : GaussianInt)
type: Prime { re := 1, im := 1 }
informal: 1 + i is prime in ℤ[i] — its norm is 2, a rational prime, so it is irreducible (a factorization gives norms multiplying to 2, one factor is a unit); ℤ[i] is a Euclidean domain hence a PID, so irreducible implies prime.

name: fld_eval_eq_zero_forall_iff_dvd
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (f : Polynomial K) : (∀ a : K, Polynomial.eval a f = 0) ↔ (Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card K - Polynomial.X) ∣ f
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Fintype K] (f : Polynomial K), (∀ (a : K), Polynomial.eval a f = 0) ↔ Polynomial.X ^ Fintype.card K - Polynomial.X ∣ f
informal: A polynomial over a finite field F_q vanishes at every point iff it is divisible by X^q - X — X^q - X = ∏_{a} (X - a) (FiniteField.roots_X_pow_card_sub_X, separable with all q roots); the factors X - a are pairwise coprime, so each dividing f gives the product dividing f; the converse is FiniteField.pow_card.

name: fld_pow_bijective_iff_coprime
statement: (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K] (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : Function.Bijective (fun x : K => x ^ k) ↔ Nat.Coprime k (Fintype.card K - 1)
type: ∀ (K : Type) [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Fintype K] (k : ℕ), 0 < k → ((Function.Bijective fun x => x ^ k) ↔ k.Coprime (Fintype.card K - 1))
informal: For k > 0 the power map x ↦ x^k is a permutation of F_q iff gcd(k, q-1) = 1 — it fixes 0 and on the cyclic group of units of order q-1 the k-th power map is injective iff gcd(k, q-1) = 1 (if d = gcd > 1 there is an element of order d in the kernel; conversely use Bezout u*k ≡ 1 mod q-1).

name: fld_irrational_cos_pi_div_nine
statement: : Irrational (Real.cos (Real.pi / 9))
type: Irrational (Real.cos (Real.pi / 9))
informal: cos(π/9) = cos 20° is irrational — by the triple angle formula c = cos(π/9) satisfies 8c^3 - 6c - 1 = 0 (cos(π/3) = 1/2); 2c is a root of the monic integer polynomial y^3 - 3y - 1, so if rational it is an integer dividing 1, but ±1 are not roots.

name: fld_irrational_exp_one
statement: : Irrational (Real.exp 1)
type: Irrational (Real.exp 1)
informal: e is irrational (Fourier's proof) — if e = a/b then b!·(e - Σ_{k≤b} 1/k!) is an integer, but it equals Σ_{k>b} b!/k!, which lies strictly between 0 and 1/b ≤ 1 (bound the tail by a geometric series; Real.exp_bound / the series expansion of exp).

name: bld6_chebyshev_T_separable
statement: (n : ℕ) : (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ (n : ℤ)).Separable
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑n).Separable
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_chebyshev_T_card_distinct_real_roots and Mathlib2.lib_chebyshev_T_natDegree_le: n = #distinct roots ≤ card roots ≤ natDegree ≤ n (the first equality from the poly theorem, the last bound from the lib lemma), so T_n has natDegree n, splits over ℝ with all roots simple; a polynomial with natDegree-many distinct roots is squarefree, hence separable in characteristic 0.

name: bld6_chebyshev_T_derivative_card_distinct_real_roots
statement: (n : ℕ) : (Polynomial.derivative (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ (n : ℤ))).roots.toFinset.card = n - 1
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), (Polynomial.derivative (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑n)).roots.toFinset.card = n - 1
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_chebyshev_T_card_distinct_real_roots and Mathlib2.lib_chebyshev_T_natDegree_le: Rolle (Polynomial.card_roots_toFinset_le_derivative) gives n = #roots(T_n) ≤ #roots(T_n') + 1 using the poly theorem; conversely #roots(T_n') ≤ natDegree T_n' ≤ natDegree T_n - 1 ≤ n - 1 by the lib degree bound (the cases n = 0, 1 give the zero / constant derivative).

name: bld6_poly_mul_add_one_eq_pow_const
statement: {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (f h : Polynomial k) (heq : f * (f + 1) = h ^ n) : f.natDegree = 0
type: ∀ {k : Type u_1} [inst : Field k] [DecidableEq k] [CharZero k] (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∀ (f h : Polynomial k), f * (f + 1) = h ^ n → f.natDegree = 0
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_no_consecutive_powerful: f and f+1 are coprime, so in the UFD k[X] any irreducible p dividing f has p-adic multiplicity in f equal to its multiplicity in h^n, a multiple of n ≥ 2, hence p^2 ∣ f; same for f+1. Both powerfulness hypotheses of poly_no_consecutive_powerful hold, giving natDegree f = 0 (last step).

name: bld6_card_circular_no_adjacent_subsets
statement: (n : ℕ) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin (n + 1)))).filter (fun s => ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), i ∈ s → j ∈ s → ((i : ℕ) + 1) % (n + 1) ≠ (j : ℕ))).card = Nat.fib n + Nat.fib (n + 2)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), {s | ∀ (i j : Fin (n + 1)), i ∈ s → j ∈ s → (↑i + 1) % (n + 1) ≠ ↑j}.card = Nat.fib n + Nat.fib (n + 2)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_card_no_adjacent_subsets: split cyclically non-adjacent subsets of Z/(n+1) by whether the last point n belongs to s. If not, s is a linear non-adjacent subset of Fin n: fib(n+2) of them by calc_card_no_adjacent_subsets n; if yes (n ≥ 2), then 0 and n-1 are excluded and the rest is a linear non-adjacent subset of the n-2 middle points: fib n by calc_card_no_adjacent_subsets (n-2); small n by decide. The total is the Lucas number L_(n+1).

name: bld6_abundant_two_mul_totient_lt
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (h : 2 * n ≤ ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 n) : 2 * n.totient < n
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 2 * n ≤ (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n → 2 * n.totient < n
informal: Uses Mathlib2.arith_sigma_mul_totient_lt_sq: 2n·φ(n) ≤ σ(n)·φ(n) < n^2 by the hypothesis and arith_sigma_mul_totient_lt_sq; cancel n > 0. So perfect and abundant numbers have φ(n) < n/2.

name: bld6_card_involutions_even
statement: (n : ℕ) : Even ((Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 2)))).filter (fun σ => σ * σ = 1)).card
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), Even {σ | σ * σ = 1}.card
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_card_involutions_rec: two-step induction with I(m+2) = I(m+1) + (m+1)·I(m) from calc_card_involutions_rec; base cases I(2) = 2 and I(3) = I(2) + 2·I(1) = 4 (again from the recurrence, I(0) = I(1) = 1 by decide), and for m ≥ 2 both I(m+1) and I(m) are even.

name: bld6_nilpotent_max_index_iff_rank
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) : A ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) ≠ 0 ↔ A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → (A ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) ≠ 0 ↔ A.rank + 1 = Fintype.card ι)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld5_nilpotent_max_index_rank and Mathlib2.bld4_nilpotent_corank_one_rank_pow: the forward direction is bld5_nilpotent_max_index_rank; conversely, if rank A + 1 = n then n ≥ 1 and bld4_nilpotent_corank_one_rank_pow with k = n - 1 gives rank(A^(n-1)) = 1, so A^(n-1) ≠ 0.

name: bld6_nilpotent_rank_pow_succ_le_rank_sub
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) (hA : IsNilpotent A) (k : ℕ) : (A ^ (k + 1)).rank ≤ A.rank - k
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), IsNilpotent A → ∀ (k : ℕ), (A ^ (k + 1)).rank ≤ A.rank - k
informal: Uses Mathlib2.lib_matrix_rank_pow_succ_lt_of_isNilpotent_of_ne_zero: induction on k; if A^(k+1) = 0 then A^(k+2) = 0 has rank 0, otherwise the lib lemma gives rank(A^(k+2)) < rank(A^(k+1)) ≤ rank A - k with rank(A^(k+1)) > 0, so rank(A^(k+2)) ≤ rank A - (k+1). Sharpens Mathlib2.bld3_nilpotent_rank_pow_le (card ι - k) and reproves Mathlib2.bld5_nilpotent_pow_rank_succ_eq_zero at k = rank A.

name: bld6_rank_cube_sub_self_defect
statement: (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K) : A.rank + (A - 1).rank + (A + 1).rank = 2 * Fintype.card ι + (A * A * A - A).rank
type: ∀ (K : Type u_1) [inst : Field K] [CharZero K] (ι : Type u_2) [inst_2 : Fintype ι] [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι K), A.rank + (A - 1).rank + (A + 1).rank = 2 * Fintype.card ι + (A * A * A - A).rank
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld3_rank_tripotent_defect and Mathlib2.bld2_rank_add_rank_one_sub: the idempotent-defect identity bld2_rank_add_rank_one_sub applied to A and to -A gives rank(A*A - A) = rank A + rank(A - 1) - n and rank(A*A + A) = rank A + rank(A + 1) - n (ranks invariant under negation); substitute both into bld3_rank_tripotent_defect: rank(A*A+A) + rank(A*A-A) = rank A + rank(A^3 - A). Corollary: A^3 = A iff rank A + rank(A-1) + rank(A+1) = 2n.

name: bld6_real_nonneg_poly_root_sq_dvd
statement: (p : Polynomial ℝ) (h : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x p) (a : ℝ) (ha : Polynomial.eval a p = 0) : (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ 2 ∣ p
type: ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x p) → ∀ (a : ℝ), Polynomial.eval a p = 0 → (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ 2 ∣ p
informal: Uses Mathlib2.poly_real_nonneg_eq_sum_two_squares: write p = f^2 + g^2; evaluating at a gives f(a)^2 + g(a)^2 = 0, so f(a) = g(a) = 0, hence X - a divides both f and g (Polynomial.dvd_iff_isRoot) and (X - a)^2 divides f^2 + g^2.

name: bld6_sum_fixed_points_sub_one_sq_perm
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => σ i = i)).card : ℤ) - 1) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℤ)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∑ σ, (↑{i | σ i = i}.card - 1) ^ 2 = ↑n.factorial
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_sum_sq_card_fixed_points_perm and Mathlib2.calc_sum_card_fixed_points_perm: expand (X - 1)^2 = X^2 - 2X + 1 and sum over the n! permutations: 2·n! (second moment, calc_sum_sq_card_fixed_points_perm) - 2·n! (first moment, calc_sum_card_fixed_points_perm) + n! (Fintype.card_perm) — the number of fixed points of a random permutation has variance 1.

name: bld6_card_image_two_fin_three
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Fin 3)).filter (fun f => (Finset.univ.image f).card = 2)).card = 3 * (2 ^ n - 2)
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → {f | (Finset.image f Finset.univ).card = 2}.card = 3 * (2 ^ n - 2)
informal: Uses Mathlib2.calc_card_surjective_fin_three: for n > 0 the image of f : Fin n → Fin 3 has 1, 2 or 3 elements; size 3 means surjective (3^n - 3·2^n + 3 functions by calc_card_surjective_fin_three), size 1 means constant (3 functions), and all functions number 3^n, so size 2 occurs 3^n - (3^n - 3·2^n + 3) - 3 = 3·2^n - 6 times.

name: p6_kfib
statement: noncomputable def p6_kfib (k : ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ℤ := ((!![k, 1; 1, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) ^ n) 0 1
type: ℤ → ℤ → ℤ
informal: k-Fibonacci number f_n for all integer n (f_0=0, f_1=1, f_{n+1}=k f_n+f_{n-1}), defined as the (0,1) entry of M^n, M=[[k,1],[1,0]], as in the paper's matrix formula

name: gr_mantel_equality_compl_not_connected
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) : ¬ Gᶜ.Connected
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ¬Gᶜ.Connected
informal: The complement of an extremal triangle-free graph is disconnected — Uses Mathlib2.bld4_mantel_equality_complete_bipartite at step 1 to get s with 2|s| = n and Adj x y ↔ (x ∈ s ↔ y ∉ s); then Gᶜ has no edge between s and sᶜ; if n = 0 Connected fails by emptiness, otherwise both sides are nonempty and a Gᶜ-walk from s to sᶜ would need a crossing edge.

name: gr_ramsey_three_four_le_ten
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] (h : 10 ≤ Fintype.card V) (G : SimpleGraph V) : ¬ G.CliqueFree 3 ∨ ¬ Gᶜ.CliqueFree 4
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V], 10 ≤ Fintype.card V → ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), ¬G.CliqueFree 3 ∨ ¬Gᶜ.CliqueFree 4
informal: R(3,4) ≤ 10: every graph on at least 10 vertices has a triangle or an independent 4-set — pick v; if v has ≥ 4 neighbours, either two are adjacent (triangle with v) or 4 of them form an independent set; otherwise v has ≥ 6 non-neighbours, and Uses Mathlib2.r3_ramsey_three_three at this step on the induced graph on the non-neighbours: a triangle there is a triangle of G, an independent triple plus v is an independent 4-set.

name: gr_triangle_free_regular_half_colorable_two
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (d : ℕ) (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (hr : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hd : 2 * d = Fintype.card V) : G.Colorable 2
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] (d : ℕ), G.CliqueFree 3 → G.IsRegularOfDegree d → 2 * d = Fintype.card V → G.Colorable 2
informal: A triangle-free n/2-regular graph is bipartite — the handshake lemma gives 2e = n·d so 4e = n²; then Uses Mathlib2.bld3_mantel_equality_colorable_two at the final step.

name: gr_bipartite_extremal_complete
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (C : G.Coloring Bool) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) (x y : V) (hxy : C x ≠ C y) : G.Adj x y
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] (C : G.Coloring Bool), 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ∀ (x y : V), C x ≠ C y → G.Adj x y
informal: A properly 2-coloured graph with n²/4 edges is complete between its colour classes — a Bool-coloured graph is triangle-free, so Uses Mathlib2.bld4_mantel_equality_complete_bipartite at step 2 to get G = complete bipartite on (s, sᶜ) with both sides nonempty; this graph is connected, so the colouring C must be constant on s and on sᶜ with different values, whence C x ≠ C y forces x,y on opposite sides (alternatively count: e ≤ a·b ≤ n²/4 with equality only if all cross pairs are edges, cf. Mathlib2.comb_card_edgeFinset_le_of_coloring_bool).

name: gr_mantel_equality_dist_le_two
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) (he : 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2) (x y : V) : G.dist x y ≤ 2
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 4 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V ^ 2 → ∀ (x y : V), G.dist x y ≤ 2
informal: An extremal triangle-free graph has diameter at most 2 — Uses Mathlib2.bld4_mantel_equality_complete_bipartite at step 1 to get the balanced bipartition s; x,y on opposite sides are adjacent (dist ≤ 1); on the same side pick z on the other side (nonempty since 2|s| = n ≥ 1) and use the walk x-z-y with SimpleGraph.dist_le.

name: gr_triangle_free_sum_choose_two_le
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : 2 * ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 + 2 * G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V * G.edgeFinset.card
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → 2 * ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 + 2 * G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V * G.edgeFinset.card
informal: In a triangle-free graph the number of 2-paths (cherries) is at most e(n−2)/2 — 2·C(d,2) + d = d², so the left side is ∑ deg² − 2e + 2e... precisely 2∑C(deg,2) + ∑deg = ∑deg²; with the handshake lemma ∑deg = 2e the claim is ∑deg² ≤ n·e, which is exactly: Uses Mathlib2.lib_simpleGraph_sum_degree_sq_le_card_mul_card_edgeFinset at the last step.

name: gr_triangle_free_exists_degree_le_half
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : ∃ v, 2 * G.degree v ≤ Fintype.card V
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V], G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ v, 2 * G.degree v ≤ Fintype.card V
informal: A triangle-free graph has a vertex of degree at most n/2 — take v of minimum degree (G.exists_minimal_degree_vertex) and d = G.minDegree; Uses Mathlib2.bld2_triangle_free_min_degree_le_half at step 2 with d ≤ deg w for all w.

name: gr_triangle_free_compl_edges_lower
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : Fintype.card V ^ 2 ≤ 4 * Gᶜ.edgeFinset.card + 2 * Fintype.card V
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [inst_1 : DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj], G.CliqueFree 3 → Fintype.card V ^ 2 ≤ 4 * Gᶜ.edgeFinset.card + 2 * Fintype.card V
informal: The complement of a triangle-free graph has at least n(n−2)/4 edges — e(G) + e(Gᶜ) = C(n,2) (SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_compl or a direct count), and Uses Mathlib2.bld_mantel_triangle_free at step 2 for 4e(G) ≤ n²; combine: 4e(Gᶜ) = 2n(n−1) − 4e(G) ≥ n² − 2n.

name: gr_self_compl_connected
statement: (V : Type) [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : Nonempty (SimpleGraph.Iso G Gᶜ)) : G.Connected
type: ∀ (V : Type) [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V), Nonempty (G ≃g Gᶜ) → G.Connected
informal: A self-complementary graph is connected — by contradiction: if G is not connected then Uses Mathlib2.comb_compl_connected_of_not_connected at step 1 to get Gᶜ connected, and transport connectedness back along the isomorphism (SimpleGraph.Iso.connected_iff), contradiction.

name: gr_exists_clique_or_indep_three
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : 6 ≤ Fintype.card V) : ∃ s : Finset V, s.card = 3 ∧ (G.IsClique (s : Set V) ∨ G.IsIndepSet (s : Set V))
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], 6 ≤ Fintype.card V → ∃ s, s.card = 3 ∧ (G.IsClique ↑s ∨ G.IsIndepSet ↑s)
informal: Among any 6 vertices there is a clique or an independent set of size 3 — Uses Mathlib2.r3_ramsey_three_three at step 1 to get ¬CliqueFree 3 for G or Gᶜ; unfold CliqueFree/IsNClique to extract the 3-set, and translate a clique of Gᶜ into an independent set of G (SimpleGraph.isClique_compl / isIndepSet_iff).

name: p6_kfib_def
statement: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k 0 = 0 ∧ p6_kfib k 1 = 1 ∧ p6_kfib k (n + 1) = k * p6_kfib k n + p6_kfib k (n - 1)
type: ∀ (k n : ℤ), Mathlib2.p6_kfib k 0 = 0 ∧ Mathlib2.p6_kfib k 1 = 1 ∧ Mathlib2.p6_kfib k (n + 1) = k * Mathlib2.p6_kfib k n + Mathlib2.p6_kfib k (n - 1)
informal: Definition (Sec 2.2): f_0=0, f_1=1, f_{n+1}=k f_n+f_{n-1}; negative indices by f_{n-1}=f_{n+1}-k f_n [Checks that the library definition p6_kfib (entry (0,1) of M^n) satisfies the paper's defining recurrence for every integer n; this characterises it uniquely. Stated for all integers k (paper: k>=1).]

name: gr_acyclic_exists_degree_le_one
statement: (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] (h : G.IsAcyclic) : ∃ v, G.degree v ≤ 1
type: ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V], G.IsAcyclic → ∃ v, G.degree v ≤ 1
informal: A nonempty finite forest has a vertex of degree at most 1 — contrapositive: if every vertex has degree ≥ 2 then Uses Mathlib2.comb_not_acyclic_of_two_le_degree at the only step.

name: p6_kfib_matrix
statement: (k n : ℤ) : (!![k, 1; 1, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) ^ n = !![p6_kfib k (n + 1), p6_kfib k n; p6_kfib k n, p6_kfib k (n - 1)]
type: ∀ (k n : ℤ), !![k, 1; 1, 0] ^ n = !![Mathlib2.p6_kfib k (n + 1), Mathlib2.p6_kfib k n; Mathlib2.p6_kfib k n, Mathlib2.p6_kfib k (n - 1)]
informal: Eq. (3) (Sec 2.2): M^n = [[f_{n+1}, f_n],[f_n, f_{n-1}]], n in Z [Integer matrix power (zpow, inverse for negative n).]

name: p6_kfib_neg
statement: (k : ℤ) (m : ℕ) : p6_kfib k (-(m : ℤ)) = (-1) ^ (m + 1) * p6_kfib k (m : ℤ)
type: ∀ (k : ℤ) (m : ℕ), Mathlib2.p6_kfib k (-↑m) = (-1) ^ (m + 1) * Mathlib2.p6_kfib k ↑m
informal: Sec 2.2 (unnumbered): f_{-m} = (-1)^{m+1} f_m [m taken as a natural number (the paper says 'by induction').]

name: gr_acyclic_exists_leaf_of_edge
